title: Health & Wellness
content_markdown:
[Health & Wellness](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/01/Health-and-Wellness-e1555535312693.jpg)

Health includes taking care of yourself every day, understanding that challenges are normal, and knowing what to do when you don’t feel well\.

## Health insurance

Good health starts with making sure you have up\-to\-date [health insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance)\. UBC requires that all students, domestic and international, have basic and extended health insurance for the duration of their studies\.

## Health services

Before moving into residence, get familiar with the range of health services offered on campus and nearby\. Many resources are available, including workshops to care for your brain and body and safe sex products\.

-   [Student Health and Wellbeing](https://students.ubc.ca/health/)
-   [Wellness Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-centre)
-   [Vancouver Coastal Health](http://www.vch.ca/)

## Counsellor in Residence

If you’re a student living in residence and you’re feeling persistently stressed, anxious or sad, you can make an appointment to see one of UBC’s [Counsellors in Residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/counsellor-in-residence/)\.

## Nurse on Campus

UBC’s [Nurse on Campus](https://students.ubc.ca/health/student-health-service/nurse-campus) program brings registered nurses into residence from September to April to answer student questions about health and wellness\. Nurses typically work one night per week in Totem Park, Place Vanier, Orchard Commons, and Walter Gage\. They also work with Residence Life staff to promote health\-related programs and initiatives for residents\.

## Safer Substance Use

A drug is a substance that causes a change in someone’s mental, emotional or physical state\. All substance use carries a certain amount of risk, making it important to consider the long and short\-term effects on your wellbeing as a student\.

The street drug supply in BC is more toxic and unpredictable than ever\. Any street drug can be poisoned, not just opioids\. It can be hard to know what’s in the substances you’re taking\. Even if they came from a source you trust, like a friend or roommate\. Even if you only take a little, or if it’s your first time, the risks are real\.

### Learn more

-   [Alcohol, cannabis, nicotine and caffeine](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/alcohol-cannabis-nicotine)
-   [Substance use health and harm reduction](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/substance-use-health-harm-reduction)
-   [Preventing and responding to an overdose](https://respondtooverdose.gov.bc.ca/)
-   [Emergency naloxone in residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/safety-security/#naloxone)

## Flu kits and shots

Getting sick is part of life\. When the flu strikes, you may not have the time or energy to pick up fever\-reducing items from the store\. It’s wise to keep a flu kit ready in your room\. Things to include:

-   Digital thermometer
-   Kleenex
-   Over\-the\-counter medications
-   Cough syrup and cough drops
-   Packages of soup
-   Ginger ale and/or juice

One of the best ways to avoid the flu is by getting an [annual flu shot](https://srs.ubc.ca/health-safety/occupational-hygiene/occupational-hazards/flu/)\. They’re free and available on campus\. Consider updating other common vaccines before moving into residence, especially the vaccine for meningococcal menin­gitis\. Check [Immunize BC](https://immunizebc.ca/) for information about which vaccines are advised and for whom\.

## Staying active

There are lots of ways to stay active in residence and on campus\!

-   Every resident has free access to a residence fitness room\.
-   Each term, we offer free [group fitness and yoga sessions](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/fitness/) for residents\.

Plus, there are many other opportunities at UBC for [staying active on campus](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/physical-activity), including UBC Recreation [classes](https://recreation.ubc.ca/fitness-classes/) and [intramurals](http://recreation.ubc.ca/intramurals/), the [UBC Aquatic Centre](https://recreation.ubc.ca/aquatics/) and more\.

## Food and Nutrition

Eating a balanced diet is vital for good health and wellbeing\. Our Registered Dietitians support students in residence by providing resources, guidance and support for a variety of food and nutrition concerns\. [Meet our dietitians](https://food.ubc.ca/nutrition/) and ask a question, check out the [nutrition blog](https://food.ubc.ca/nutrition/), [book an appointment](https://food.ubc.ca/contact-the-dietitian/), and check out [Nutrislice](https://food.ubc.ca/nutrislice/) for online menus, plus info about ingredients and allergens in our residence dining halls\.

## Chaplains in Residence

Chaplains have hours at several residences one day per week\. [UBC Chaplains](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains) answer questions about spirituality and religion and work with Residence Life staff and Nurses on Campus to support programs related to overall health and wellness\.

## More Resources

-   [Tips to stay healthy](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/health-services/ "Health services")
-   [Healthy eating in residence](https://www.food.ubc.ca/nutrition/ "Food for thought")
-   [Understanding stress and the stress response](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/stress-anxiety "Managing stress")
-   [Religion and Spirituality](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality)

title: KonMari your residence room
content_markdown:
### Whether it’s the middle of term or a week before you move out, keep your space fresh and organized with these decluttering tips\!

[Man working at desk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/Man-working-at-desk.jpg)

By Amanda Keating, 3rd year Arts student

During my time living in residence at UBC, it’s safe to say that I have collected *a lot* of stuff\.

In first\-year, I flew in from the US with just three suitcases\. Flash\-forward to third\-year: let’s just say that three suitcases were barely enough to fit my vast collection of UBC sweatshirts\. It’s totally natural to collect more things as you move through residence, but how much is *too* much? As I entered my third year, this was the dilemma I faced\.

Let me paint you a picture of what my room looked like\.

Clothes I hadn’t worn in months filled my closet, textbooks from first\-year haunted my bookshelf, and there was a growing cache of who\-knows\-what under my bed\.

Maybe you’re in the same boat?

Whether you’re [moving out of residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-out/) or just want to tidy things up, figuring out what to keep and what to get rid of can be tough\. That old hoodie from high school can have a lot of memories attached to it\. That copy of *Twilight* on your bookshelf… It’s your next great read, right?\!

Like me, maybe you’re not sure where to start\. I had no idea what to do with the accumulation of stuff that was taking over my space\. Then, after watching her Netflix series, I turned to Marie Kondo’s [KonMari Method](https://shop.konmari.com/pages/about)—like millions of other North Americans\!— and my room is now much happier \(and tidier\) because of it\. Here’s how the process works and how it worked for me\!

## What is the KonMari Method?

According to Marie Kondo, the KonMari Method is not a “set of rules on how to sort, organize, and put things away\. It is a guide to acquiring the right mindset for creating order and becoming a tidy person\.”

A common misunderstanding is that the KonMari Method is actually just about [minimalism](https://konmari.com/konmari-is-not-minimalism/)—about living with less\. Although minimalism and KonMari have many similarities, the KonMari Method is more about living with those things you truly cherish\. The result might be the same, but not necessarily\!

When I decided to declutter my room, I actually used a combination of the Konmari Method and minimalism\. Turned out, I only had a few items that truly sparked joy, which made it easier to get rid of my unnecessary items\. You might have lots of items that spark joy, and that’s okay too\!

## The 5 Steps to Decluttering Your Space

[Woman holding pile of knit blankets](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/decluttering2.jpg)

Even though I used some aspects of minimalism, for simplicity, let’s just stick to the KonMari Method, with its 5 essential steps to decluttering\. Use these steps to help you figure out what to keep, throw away, or donate—or, if you’re moving out, what you want to put into storage or take with you\.

Also, if it’s your first time using this method, I’d recommend setting aside an entire day to tidy up\. Or split your tidying over a couple of days\.

### 1\. Discard by category first\.

The first step is to discard your items—by category\. Marie Kondo recommends using this order:

-   Clothes
-   Books
-   Papers
-   Kimono \(a\.k\.a\., miscellaneous 😜\)
-   Mementos

### 2\. Break your categories into subcategories, if needed\.

If you have a lot of one type of item, like clothes or books, you can break these down into smaller subcategories\. For clothes, the obvious choice is shirts, pants, shoes, etc\. But you could also break that category down by season or colour\. The choice is yours\!

### 3\. Keep only the things that spark joy\.

This is the phrase that put Marie Kondo on the world’s stage\. Here’s how it works:

-   Pick up each item individually\.
-   Really *feel* it\.
-   Then, ask yourself: *does this item spark joy?*

Do you have an emotional connection to the item? Yeah? OK, that one’s a keeper\. Not so much? Looks like it’s time to let it go\. This is the time to decide which items hold meaning for you, or serve a purpose in your life, and which items are, honestly, just *stuff*\. Ask yourself: do you really *need* those books from last term—or are they better off on [someone else’s shelf](https://www.facebook.com/groups/ubc.textbook.4.sale/)?

### 4\. After you’ve finished discarding, it’s time to organize your room\.

Choose where you’re going to store the things you’re keeping, whether it be in your drawers, closet, or under your bed\. Just remember to store the same types of items in the same place\. Looking for some storage options? [IKEA](https://www.ikea.com/ca/en/cat/storage-home-organization-st001/) has tons of cost\-effective and residence\-friendly options to help you optimize your space\.

### 5\. Do it all in one go\.

While you *can* do the process over a couple of days, if you need to, Marie Kondo recommends decluttering your space in one single\-day session, rather than little\-by\-little\. It might seem like an overwhelming thing to do, but trust me, it will take way less time than you think\. And doing so will help change your entire mindset when it comes to maintaining an organized space\.

[Girl sitting in chair reading a book](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/decluttering3.jpg)

And that’s it\! Once you’ve finished decluttering your space with the KonMari Method, you should have 3 piles:

1.  Stuff you’re going to donate\.
2.  Stuff you’re putting in storage\.
3.  Stuff you’re going to recycle or throw away\.

You could also add a fourth pile for items you want to sell on the [UBC Buy & Sell Facebook group](https://www.facebook.com/groups/ubcbuyandsellitems), Craigslist, or a marketplace app\.

## The takeaway

If you decide to declutter in the middle of the school year like I did, your room will be a much happier, less distracting, and better functioning space—whether you need to chill out after a long day of classes, hunker down for a late\-night study session, or quickly pack a bag for a weekend away\.

If you decide to declutter while getting ready to move out, letting go of the things that don’t spark joy will make moving into your next place that much easier\.

For me, using the KonMari Method to declutter my room helped me completely transform my space\. My drawers are less cluttered and my closet is free of all those unworn sweatshirts\. After an arduous study session at IKB, it now feels so comforting to step into a tidy, organized room, which contains items that I *know* spark joy\.

Ultimately, it’s up to you what, and how much, you choose to get rid of when you KonMari your room\. Maybe your space is in dire need of a deep decluttering\. Maybe it just needs a minor clean\-up\. Figure out what’s best for you, and get to it\. Happy decluttering\!

title: COVID-19 Residence Rules
content_markdown:
[Person applying hand sanitizer](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/applying-hand-sanitizer.jpg)

*Last updated: August 12, 2024*

Throughout COVID\-19, Student Housing and Community Services has implemented plans to provide the best possible accommodation for our residents, in\-line with university policies and governmental mandates, guidelines and recommendations\.

As always, health and safety remain a top priority in our student residence communities\.

## COVID\-19 Residence Rules

UBC students, including those living in student residences managed and operated by UBC Student Housing and Community Services \(SHCS\), are required to follow any [campus\-wide rules](https://srs.ubc.ca/health-safety/safety-programs/communicable-disease-prevention-framework/), along with any specific rules for residents and guests of SHCS, put in place to address COVID\-19 or other communicable diseases\.

At present, there are no additional COVID\-19 rules in place for students living in residence\. However, residence services, amenities and rules may change in response to developing circumstances\.

## Additional information

### Travelling to Canada

To find key information about travelling to Canada, visit:

-   UBC Student Services—[Travelling to Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/travelling-to-canada)
-   Government of Canada—[COVID\-19: Travel, testing and borders](https://travel.gc.ca/travel-covid)

### BC’s response to COVID\-19

For information about the BC provincial government’s response to COVID\-19, including vaccinations, treatments and testing kits, visit:

-   Government of British Columbia—[BC’s response to COVID\-19](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/covid-19)

### COVID\-19 Self\-assessment tool

To self\-assess for COVID\-19, please use the BC government’s online [COVID\-19 self\-assessment tool](https://covidcheck.gov.bc.ca/)\.

### How to get a free rapid testing kit

In BC, free rapid antigen testing kits are available to everyone at pharmacies across the province\. [Learn more](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/covid-19/info/testing)\.

### When to self\-isolate while living in residence

Although self\-isolation is no longer required, if you have COVID\-19 or symptoms of COVID\-19, the BC Centre for Disease Control recommends that you stay home as much as possible to reduce the potential spread of illness\. Learn more about [how to self\-isolate](http://www.bccdc.ca/health-info/diseases-conditions/covid-19/self-isolation)\.

While choosing to self\-isolate, you may access shared common areas when necessary—including shared washrooms and kitchens, along with building entrances to retrieve food deliveries—but we encourage you take the following safety measures:

Minimize prolonged face\-to\-face interactions\.

Wear a face covering while in close physical proximity to others\.

Avoid close physical contact with others\.

Avoid hosting guests in your unit\.

Practice regular hand washing\.

Access shared spaces during quieter times, when possible\.

## Questions?

Please [contact us](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.

Iona House is a small, charming and relaxed residence community located in the iconic Iona Building, which once housed the Vancouver School of Theology\. Today, in addition to Iona House residence, this building is home to the Vancouver School of Economics\. Located near a number of other residence communities and recreation, social and academic facilities, Iona House residents have access to many nearby residence and campus amenities\.

## Quick Facts

-   Year Round
-   Mainly upper\-year undergraduate and graduate students

# Facilities at Iona House

-   [icon\_facilities\_frontdesk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_commonsblock.png)  
    
    ## Commonsblock
    
    The hub for residence activities\. Includes: Wi\-Fi, activity and meeting rooms, group and private study spaces, lounge areas, and a convenience store\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_frontdesk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_frontdesk.png)  
    
    ## Support Staff
    
    From our Front Desk staff and Overnight Mobile Team to Residence Life professional and student staff, you are never alone\! [Meet the people](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/meet-the-team/) you can contact with questions, concerns or a request for support\.

-   [icon\_facilities\_health](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_health.png)  
    
    ## Health & Safety
    
    Residents have access to a campus medical clinic and safety programs such as SafeWalk\. There are regular nightly patrols of residence properties\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_family](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_mealplan.png)  
    
    ## Meal Plan
    
    Iona House suites come with kitchens\. Students can purchase an [optional meal plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/ubccard-value-plan/ "Food Services Meal Plans") for convenience—no need to cook or carry cash\.
    

## Sustainability Features

UBC has been recognized internationally for its commitment to sustainable living\. Many residences and rooms have modern [sustainability features](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/ "Sustainability Features") designed to reduce waste, energy consumption, and water use\.

title: Privacy
content_markdown:
To comply with BC’s [Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act](http://www.oipc.bc.ca/about/legislation.aspx), we keep all information about residence applicants private\. Personal information received through an application will not be released to anyone outside the university without written consent from the applicant or unless permitted or required by law\.

## Key Facts

-   On the residence application form, applicants can consent to the release of private information about their residence assignment and fees\.
-   In Workday, applicants can provide [Third Party Authorization](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/third-party-authorization) to consent to the release of certain private information to specific individuals only, such as parents, guardians, other family members or friends\.
-   Applicants can revoke consent at any time within Workday or by contacting [Student Housing](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/ "Contact Us")\.
-   Student Housing does not sell or provide lists of residents’ names or addresses to third parties\.

If the applicant declines permission:

-   University administration is unable to confirm or deny if they have applied for or are living in residence at UBC\.
-   Even if calling on their behalf, family member\(s\) or friend\(s\) will not receive any information about an applicant, including application status, residence assignment or fees\.
-   If friends or family members don’t know, or forget, a student’s residence room / unit number and request this information from staff, we are not able to provide it\.

Learn more about [information privacy for gender diverse students](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/prospective/gender-diverse/information-privacy/) living in residence\.

content_markdown:
["Happy Holidays" text on snowy aerial photograph of UBC](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Winter-Break-2020-Header-1200x675-1.jpg)

**Winter break at UBC can be magical, with campus feeling like your own special place for a few weeks and lots of opportunities to explore the city with your residence neighbours and friends\. And who knows, there might even be snow\!**

**To help you make the most of your winter break, scroll down to** **find out about:**

-   [**Residence amenities**](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/winter-break/#amenities)
-   [**Residence events and activities**](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/winter-break/#events)

-   [**Exploring Vancouver**](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/winter-break/#explore-vancouver)
-   [**Food & drink options**](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/winter-break/#food-drink)

## Residence amenities

#### Upper year residence front desks

Remember, upper year [residence front desks](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/) are open and here to help\. Please visit your residence front desk or contact the Overnight Mobile Team if you need any assistance over the break\.

**Upper year residence:** all residence amenities remain open and operational\.

**First year residence:** Place Vanier, Totem Park and Orchard Commons are closed December 21, 2025 \(12 pm noon\)–January 4, 2026 \(12 pm noon\)\. Ritsumeikan\-UBC House remains open throughout the break and Rits residents can access amenities and front desk services at Marine Drive\.

## Residence events and activities

Lots of great events and activities will be planned for you to participate in during the winter break\. Check out the [Residence Events Calendar](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/events/) or check in with your RA for more details\.

Don't miss your holidays in residence self\-care guide\!

Check out great tips, resources, ideas and more—gift\-wrapped just for you\.

[GET THE GUIDE](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/winter-break-self-care/)

### Function Responsibility Form \(FRF\) Procedures during winter break

If you would like to have a gathering in your unit, please make sure you complete the following steps as soon as possible:

-   You may pick up forms in person at your residence Front Desk during winter break\.
-   As always, you will need to fill out the FRF after seeking approval and signatures from those roommates who are present \(should you live in a shared unit\)\.
-   Once you have filled out the form please return it to Front Desk at least 48 hours prior to the function date\. Please ask Front Desk to date\-stamp your form when you return it to them\.
-   Please ensure you print your name and unit number clearly, as you will then be contacted by a Residence Life staff member to follow\-up on your request\.
-   The function may only proceed once you have received confirmation of approval from a Residence Life staff member \(most likely by email, so please check your junk mail folder\)\.
-   The FRF process will return to regular procedures at the start of Term 2\.

## What’s happening on\-campus and in Vancouver?

There’s a lot happening on campus at UBC and around Vancouver during the winter break\. Here’s a roundup of what to do and where to find more\.

### Explore campus

**Nature**

[Pacific Spirit Park](https://metrovancouver.org/services/regional-parks/park/pacific-spirit-regional-park)

[Acadia and Tower Beach](https://www.alltrails.com/trail/canada/british-columbia/acadia-and-tower-beaches)

[Spanish Banks Beach](https://covapp.vancouver.ca/parkfinder/parkdetail.aspx?inparkid=220)

**Attractions**

[MOA](https://moa.ubc.ca/)

[Beaty Biodiversity Museum](https://beatymuseum.ubc.ca/)

[UBC Botanical Garden](https://botanicalgarden.ubc.ca/)

[Nitobe Memorial Garden](https://botanicalgarden.ubc.ca/visit/nitobe-memorial-garden/)

**Recreation facilities**

[UBC Fitness Centres](https://recreation.ubc.ca/fitness-classes/contact/)

[UBC Aquatic Centre](https://recreation.ubc.ca/aquatics/)

\+ Don’t forget to register for Term 2 UBC Rec [programs](https://recreation.ubc.ca/) and [intramurals](https://recreation.ubc.ca/2024/11/13/winter-2025-intramural-events-leagues/)\!

#### How do I access student services and supports over the holidays?

Find holiday hours for student services, along with 24/7 crisis support and self\-help resources in [Student supports over the holidays](https://students.ubc.ca/ubclife/student-supports-over-holidays) on UBC’s [Student Services](https://students.ubc.ca/) website\.

**Looking for religious or spiritual resources?**

Visit UBC’s [religion and spirituality](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality) page to learn more about [UBC Chaplains](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains), on\-campus [multifaith prayer rooms](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms), and more\.

### Explore Vancouver

**Getting around Vancouver**

Getting off\-campus is a cinch\!  Check out [Translink’s website](https://www.translink.ca/) to explore bus and Skytrain routes, including ways to get to our local mountains\! For more info on getting around or off\-campus, visit [UBC Campus \+ Community Planning](https://planning.ubc.ca/transportation)\.

[Christmas light displays around Metro Vancouver](https://vancouversun.com/news/christmas-lights-metro-vancouver-map-list-2025)

[Destination Downtown](https://miss604.com/2025/11/downtown-vancouver-ferris-wheel-and-winter-fun/)

[Burnaby Village Museum Heritage Christmas](https://www.burnabyvillagemuseum.ca/EN/main/what-s-on/heritage-christmas.html)

**Mountain sports**

Skiing, snowboarding, snowshoeing, or sledding\!

[Cypress Mountain](https://cypressmountain.com/)

[Grouse Mountain](https://www.grousemountain.com/)

[Mount Seymour](https://mtseymour.ca/)

**Daytrips**

[Stanley Park](https://vancouver.ca/parks-recreation-culture/stanley-park.aspx) \(Free\)—walk the seawall or check out the forest trails\.

[Lighthouse Park](https://www.vancouvertrails.com/trails/lighthouse-park/) \(Free\)—a fun, seaside hike on the North Shore\.

[Vancouver Public Library](https://www.vpl.ca/location/central-library) \(Free\)—the Central Library downtown is a pretty cool piece of architecture\.

[Deep Cove](https://www.vancouversnorthshore.com/neighbourhood/deep-cove/) \(Free\)—a great daytrip, just a transit ride away\.

[Capilano Suspension Bridge](https://www.capbridge.com/)—a classic Vancouver attraction\.

[Vancouver Art Gallery](https://www.vanartgallery.bc.ca/)—incredible local and global art exhibitions\. Plus, they offer student discounts\!

[VanDusen Botanical Garden](https://vandusengarden.org/)—beautiful botanical garden in the heart of the city\.

[Bloedel Conservatory](https://vandusengarden.org/explore/bloedel-conservatory/)—gorgeous tropical plant conservatory at the top of Queen Elizabeth Park\.

[Science World](https://www.scienceworld.ca/)—BC’s premier science attraction at the edge of downtown Vancouver\.

[Vancouver Aquatic Centre](https://vancouver.ca/parks-recreation-culture/vancouver-aquatic-centre.aspx)—great indoor swimming pool just across the Burrard bridge\.

## Food and drink

### Eating on campus

Campus is much quieter over the winter break and some Food Service locations close during this period\. For the most up\-to\-date information about what is open, please visit the [Feed Me Now](https://food.ubc.ca/feedme/) webpage\.

On holidays like Christmas Day, Boxing Day, and New Year’s Day food options on campus are limited\. [Harvest Market](https://food.ubc.ca/places/harvest-market/) remains open on these days\.

### Eating off campus

The winter break is a fantastic time to explore Vancouver with your residence friends and neighbours\. Our city has an amazing food scene\. Check out this [Vancouver food bucket list](https://nomsmagazine.com/eat/ultimate-vancouver-food-bucket-list/) article by Noms Magazine for inspiration\. Some restaurants will be closed for dine\-in or take\-out on statutory holidays, so it’s always best to call ahead and ask if they take reservations\.

### Delivery

#### Meal Delivery

If you want to order meals in, popular delivery services include [Skip the Dishes](https://www.skipthedishes.com/), [Uber Eats](https://www.ubereats.com/ca), [Door Dash](https://www.doordash.com/food-delivery/vancouver-bc-restaurants/), [Fantuan\.](https://www.fantuan.ca/en/) Please consider ordering food from nearby locations to reduce the sustainability impact of having meals delivered to campus\.

#### Grocery Deliveries

If you plan on making your own meals, consider ordering groceries online for delivery to your door\. Popular and near\-by options include [Stongs](https://stongs.com/), [Spud](https://www.spud.ca/about/howitworks.cfm), and [Save\-On\-Foods](https://www.saveonfoods.com/shop-online-how-it-works/) \(select “Vancouver” and “UBC” when ordering\)\. We recommend you order well in advance of your preferred delivery date\.

#### Meal Kits

Popular Meal Kit delivery services include [Chef’s Plate](https://www.chefsplate.com/), [Fresh Prep](https://www.freshprep.ca/SCVIA19), [Hello Fresh](https://www.hellofresh.ca/), and [Good Food](https://www.makegoodfood.ca/en/home)\.

Not sure which one to choose? Check out this comparison of [Vancouver’s most popular meal\-kit delivery services](https://www.vancouverisawesome.com/sponsored/meal-kit-delivery-vancouver-fresh-prep-1946451)\.

title: Holidays in residence self-care guide
content_markdown:
[Happy young woman dancing solo](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Winter-Break-Self-Care-Header_1200x675.jpg)

***Staying in residence over the holidays? Check out these tips, resources, ideas and more—gift\-wrapped just for you\.***

Go easy on yourself, and remember that taking care of yourself will help you enjoy the holidays and set you up for success in Term 2\.

Self\-care includes all the activities you do to consciously take care of your physical, mental and emotional health\. The resources on this page, from exercise tips and mindfulness apps to creative prompts, counselling and more, will hopefully provide some valuable self\-care ideas and support\.

## On this page

-   **[Staying physically active](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/winter-break-self-care/#active)**
-   **[Staying mentally healthy](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/winter-break-self-care/#mental-health)**
-   **[Self\-nurturing tips](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/winter-break-self-care/#nurture-tips)**
-   **[Productive solitude: resources from UBC’s Counsellors in Residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/winter-break-self-care/#productive-solitude)**

[Illustration of workout gear](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/SI_self-care_icon_417x150_1-300x108-1.png)

## Staying physically active

### Getting regular exercise is important to mental and physical wellbeing\.

Keeping your body moving has so many benefits, especially in times of stress\. Exercise elevates mood and mental resilience, it helps build a strong immune system, enhances focus, concentration and memory, and it improves good sleep\. Try out some of the many great options for staying active, even in small spaces:

-   **Sit less\.** Break up sedentary time by setting a timer/reminder to get up at least once per hour for a short activity break\. Ideas include taking a phone call while walking around – inside or outside – dancing, stretching, doing a small chore like making a snack, completing a short online exercise, or having a yoga session\.
-   **Get a workout in\.** UBC Recreation offers a ton of physical recreation opportunities\. Check out their [Get Moving Programs](https://recreation.ubc.ca/get-moving/) for free and low barrier activities suitable for all fitness levels\.
-   **Try something new and get creative\!** Think of this change in routine as an opportunity to explore different avenues such as learning how to juggle or taking up Tai Chi\.

Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate\-intensity or 75 minutes of vigorous\-intensity physical activity per week, as well as muscle\-strengthening activities on two or more days a week\. Any activity is better than none and more activity provides more physical and mental health benefits\.

[Illustration of retro iPod and headphones](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/SI_self-care_icon_340x150_2-300x132-1.png)

## Staying mentally healthy

Top tips include connecting with others, eating healthy foods, staying as active as possible, getting plenty of rest, and finding satisfying ways to stay occupied\.

-   **Stay informed, but not overwhelmed\.** Over\-indulging in news from multiple sources can lead to heightened anxiety\. Instead, focus on getting helpful information from trusted sources and limit your intake\.
-   **Communicate and stay connected\.** Staying in contact with other people not only staves off boredom, but it is also critical for minimizing the sense of isolation\. Check in with friends and family every day, and make use of UBC’s [health and 24/7 counselling resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health) if you’re feeling off\-kilter\.
-   **Create and follow routines,** incorporating satisfying activities that leave you feeling recharged and/or give you a sense of purpose, productivity and accomplishment\.

### UBC Mental Health Supports

-   [**UBC Wellbeing’s Thrive 5\.**](https://wellbeing.ubc.ca/thrive-5) Learn how to promote a healthy mind and body with the Thrive 5 by UBC Wellbeing\.
-   [**Counselling Services\.**](https://students.ubc.ca/health/counselling-services) If you’re feeling persistently stressed, anxious, or sad, you can book a virtual or phone appointment with a wellness advisor or counsellor\. Note that UBC Counselling Services will be closed from 2 pm on December 24, 2024 to January 1, 2025\.
-   [**Understand stress and the stress response\.**](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/news/october-10-2022/completing-stress-cycle#:~:text=When%20our%20body%20encounters%20stressors,short%2Dterm%20thinking%20and%20processing) Explore a variety of articles and resources that will guide you in managing your mental health\.
-   [**Mindfulness apps worthy of your attention\.**](https://www.mindful.org/free-mindfulness-apps-worthy-of-your-attention/) Five FREE mindfulness apps to download today to help pass the time\.
-   [**Here2Talk\.**](https://here2talk.ca/home) Get started with free, 24/7 single\-session counselling by phone or online chat for all UBC students, no matter where you are in the world\.

[Illustration of mobile phone with the words "call someone you love"](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/SI_self-care_icon_350x150_3-300x129-1.png)

## Self\-nurturing tips

Want to take it a little deeper? See if you can adjust your mindset to thinking of this time not as forced isolation, but as a chance to recharge, reset and indulge in some well\-deserved self\-nurturing\.

-   **Be kind to yourself\.** It’s OK if you’re not “making the most” of the winter break or you’re wondering how that baking project produced stones instead of scones\. Go easy on yourself and celebrate the small wins, like getting out for a walk or preparing a healthy meal\. Remind yourself that even if it doesn’t feel like it sometimes, you’re doing your best\. Go even deeper with these [self\-compassion practices and exercises](https://self-compassion.org/category/exercises/)\.
-   **Focus on what you can control\.** This might be a good time to remember the serenity prayer: to have the serenity to accept the things you can’t change, to have the courage to change the things you can, and the wisdom to know the difference\.
-   **Treat it like an experiment\.** Put your ego aside, and get curious about the gifts of these strange times\.
-   **Indulge in imaginative self\-reflection\.** Being around other people keeps us being who we’ve always been, because that’s who they expect to see, and we respond to their expectations\. When there’s nobody around to have an opinion, take some time to think about and imagine who you want to be in the long\-term future\.
-   **Practice gratitude\.** There is always something to be grateful for, and regularly practicing gratitude can bring a significant boost to our mental health\. One way to keep track of what we’re grateful for is to [start a gratitude journal](https://www.intelligentchange.com/blogs/read/ultimate-gratitude-journal-guide)\.

## Productive Solitude

### *Resources from UBC’s Counsellors in Residence\.*

Over the winter break, we suspect you may find extra time on your hands\! Here are some ideas for helping you find a bit of productive solitude and fostering intentional reflection, creativity and self\-development\.

Learn more about [UBC’s Counsellors in Residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/counsellor-in-residence/)\.

### Podcasts

Instead of recommending specific shows, here are some approaches for finding some new ones\!

-   Explore podcasts that provide a different perspective\.
-   Listen to shows that you think will make you laugh and smile\.
-   Find shows that take you on a journey\.

### Videos

-   Brene Brown: [The Power of Vulnerability](https://www.ted.com/talks/brene_brown_the_power_of_vulnerability?referrer=playlist-the_most_popular_talks_of_all) \(Ted Talk\)\.
-   Kristin Neff: [The Space Between Self\-Esteem and Self\-Compassion](https://self-compassion.org/videos/) \(Ted Talk\)\.
-   Carol Dweck: [The Power of Believing you can Improve](https://www.ted.com/talks/carol_dweck_the_power_of_believing_that_you_can_improve) \(Ted Talk\)\.
-   [Loneliness in a nutshell](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n3Xv_g3g-mA)\.

### Journal activities

-   [Positive psychology self\-reflection activities](https://positivepsychology.com/introspection-self-reflection/)\.
-   Take the [VIA Strengths Finder](https://www.viacharacter.org/survey/account/register) survey and reflect on what you discover\.
-   [Monthly journaling prompts](https://thecoffeemonsterzco.com/en-ca/blogs/midnight-blogging/journaling-prompts)

### Creativity

-   Paint a kindness rock to place in a park or on someone’s doorstep\.
-   Make cards to send to a senior centre\.
-   Leave a surprise – flowers, homemade cookies, a nice note – on a neighbour’s doorstep\.
-   [Make a zentangle](https://www.google.com/search?q=zentangle&rlz=1C1GCEB_enCA894CA894&oq=zenta&aqs=chrome.0.0i433i457j69i57j0i433l3j0l3.2164j0j15&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8#kpvalbx=_b4DGX5KcL8vY-wTOibTQBw102)\. These fun little drawings are a great tool for letting go and helping reduce stress\.
-   Paint the different sides of yourself\. In this project, paint the different aspects of your personality, giving each a visual representation\. Paint as many or as few as you like\.
-   Make a drawing related to a quote you like\. Take the words of wisdom from someone else and turn them into something visually inspiring\.
-   Take photographs of things you think are beautiful\. No one else has to like them but you\. Print and frame them, if you like, to have constant reminders of the beautiful things in life\.

### Books

-   [Burnout: The Secret to Unlocking the Stress Cycle](https://www.banyen.com/browse/filter/t/Burnout:%20The%20Secret%20to%20Unlocking%20the%20Stress%20Cycle/k/keyword), by Emily Nagoski and Amelia Nagoski\.
-   [Mindset: The New Psychology of Success](https://www.banyen.com/browse/filter/t/Mindset:%20The%20New%20Psychology%20of%20Success/k/keyword), by Carol Dweck\.
-   [Attached: The New Science of Adult Attachment](https://www.banyen.com/browse/filter/t/Attached:%20The%20New%20Science%20of%20Adult%20Attachment/k/keyword), by Amir Levine\.

### Free courses

*Just in case you still feel like studying* 😉

**Harvard University**

[The Path to Happiness: What Chinese Philosophy Teaches Us about the Good Life](https://online-learning.harvard.edu/course/path-happiness-what-chinese-philosophy-teaches-us-about-good-life?delta=0)

Why should we care about Confucius? Explore ancient Chinese philosophy, ethics, and political theory to challenge your assumptions of what it means to be happy, live a meaningful life, and change the world\.

**Yale University**

[The Science of Wellbeing](https://www.coursera.org/learn/the-science-of-well-being)

In this course you will engage in a series of challenges designed to increase your own happiness and build more productive habits\. As preparation for these tasks, Professor Laurie Santos reveals misconceptions about happiness, annoying features of the mind that lead us to think the way we do, and the research that can help us change\. You will ultimately be prepared to successfully incorporate a specific wellness activity into your life\.

title: Cleaning and departure checklists
content_markdown:
[Young person sitting cross\-legged with cleaning supplies\.](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/focal_cleaning2.jpg)

**If you’re moving out, moving to another residence room, or staying on and expecting new roommates, check out our cleaning and departure checklists for:**

-   **[Traditional or modified\-traditional rooms](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-out/cleaning-departure/#trad)**
-   **[Suite\-style residences](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-out/cleaning-departure/#suite)**

**Plus, don’t miss our [cleaning tips videos](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-out/cleaning-departure/#videos) for great tips on how to clean your bathroom, stovetop and oven\.**

## Traditional or modified\-traditional rooms

**Orchard Commons, Place Vanier and Totem Park**

For residents who are moving out or getting a new roommate\.

### Cleaning checklist

-   Take all garbage and recycling to your residence waste sorting area\.
-   Ensure all donations are taken to the donation zone and sorted correctly\.
-   Clean all areas thoroughly: Wipe walls and surfaces such as desk, chair, closet and shelves\. Vacuum floor/carpet\.
-   Remove personal items, furniture and anything else that wasn’t in the unit when you arrived\.
-   Remove all stickers, pins and wall tape\.
-   Move furniture or other items that came with your room back to its original location and re\-assemble if necessary\. You will be assessed if anything is missing or damaged\. Use the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/) to view a furniture inventory for your unit\.
-   Bathrooms in həm̓ləsəm̓, q̓ələχən and Orchard Commons: Clean the toilet, sink, mirror, cupboards, drawers, shower and walls\. Wash the shower curtain and rehang it\.
-   Floor/house lounge: Remove any food or items belonging to you from the fridge\.

### Departure checklist

-   Empty and unlock drawers and closets, put your mattress pad on your bed and lock your room door\. Leave nothing behind\.
-   Return residence keys to the Front Desk\. You will be charged for unreturned keys\.
-   Complete check out procedures at the Front Desk and sign your checkout card\.
-   Use the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/) to sign up for mail forwarding\.

## Cleaning tips\!

We discovered these videos in the Residence Life archives\. Some things don’t age well—like early 2010s iPhone footage—but tips on how to clean are ageless\.

Watch these videos for great tips on how to clean your bathroom, stovetop and oven\.

How to clean your bathroom

[Embedded iframe \(view source\)](https://www.youtube.com/embed/6fz20VTdZf0?)

How to clean your stovetop

[Embedded iframe \(view source\)](https://www.youtube.com/embed/KdZGCr-sHho?)

How to clean your oven

[Embedded iframe \(view source\)](https://www.youtube.com/embed/yXkNpBFnKUc?)

## Suite\-style residences

**Brock Commons, Exchange, Fairview Crescent, Fraser Hall, Iona House, Marine Drive, Ponderosa Commons, Ritsumeikan\-UBC House, tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ, Thunderbird, and Walter Gage\.**

For residents who are moving out or getting a new roommate\.

**Remember:** while individuals are responsible for private bedrooms, **all roommates are responsible for common areas\.** All spaces will be thoroughly inspected\.

### Cleaning checklist

-   Take garbage, compost and recycling to your residence waste sorting stations\.
-   Ensure all donations are taken to the donation zone and sorted correctly\.
-   Clean all areas thoroughly: Wipe walls and surfaces such as countertops, chairs, tables and desks\. Sweep, wash and vacuum all floors/carpets\.
-   Remove personal items, furniture and anything else that wasn’t in the unit when you arrived\.
-   Remove all stickers, pins and wall tape\.
-   Bathrooms: Clean the toilet, sink, mirror, medicine cabinet, bathtub/shower and walls\. Wash the shower curtain and rehang it\.
-   Kitchens: Clean and wipe down cupboards inside and out\. Pull your fridge and stove out and clean underneath\. If roommates are staying, don’t leave any food or other supplies in the fridge or cupboards unless your roommates specifically ask you to\.

### Additional tasks for vacant units

-   Clean the stove, oven and refrigerator thoroughly\. Leave the refrigerator empty but running\.
-   Vacuum cleaner: Remove and discard dust build\-up from the cloth filter bag or replace the disposable bag\. Leave the vacuum cleaner and all accessories in common area\. Instructions are posted in the kitchen cupboard\.
-   Move furniture or other items that came with the unit back to its original location and re\-assemble if necessary\. You will be assessed if anything is missing or damaged\. Use the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/) to review the room condition report for a furniture inventory for your unit\.

### Departure checklist

-   Empty and unlock drawers and closets, put your mattress pad on your bed and lock your room door\. Leave nothing behind\.
-   Return residence keys to the Front Desk\. You will be charged for unreturned keys\.
-   Complete checkout procedures at the Front Desk and sign your checkout card\.
-   Set up mail forwarding in the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/)\. \(Fairview Crescent residents: contact [Canada Post](http://www.canadapost.ca/) to forward mail\.\)

title: Bed & Bath Linens
content_markdown:
[Person raising hands from underneath bed linens](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/bed-linens.jpg)

All furnished rooms come with a mattress pad\. However, Student Housing and Community Services does not provide bedding or bath linens—you must bring your own\.

For extra convenience, [Campus Linens of Canada](https://campuslinenscanada.com/ "Campus Linens Canada") offers online sales of high quality bed and bath linens and is the only vendor approved to deliver products to UBC’s residences before students move in\.

## Delivery order deadline

### **Term 1 Move In \(2026/27\)**

**August 20, 2026:** Deadline to order bed/bath linens from [Campus Linens of Canada](https://campuslinenscanada.com/) for on\-time delivery to residence for Jump Start Move\-in Day \(Term 1\)\.  
**August 26, 2026:** Standard deadline to order bed/bath linens from [Campus Linens of Canada](https://campuslinenscanada.com/) for on\-time delivery to residence \(Term 1\)\.

title: Sustainability Features
content_markdown:
[Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/JPEG-HR-UBC-21.jpeg)

**UBC has been recognized nationally and internationally for its commitment to sustainable living, excellence in energy management, and green\-focused operational initiatives, including innovative building designs and an efficient vehicle fleet\.**

## On this page

-   [Sustainable residence buildings](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/#buildings)
-   [Sustainability features](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/#features)

Live Green

To learn about what we’re doing to achieve UBC’s sustainability and climate action goals and what you can do to help, visit [Live Green: Climate Action for Student Residents](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/)\.

## Sustainable residence buildings

By living in Student Housing at UBC, you’re already helping to reduce the greenhouse gas emissions caused by commuting\. Plus, many of our residence buildings—especially our newest buildings—have important sustainability features built right in\.

### **LEED certified**

As part of our commitment to building a sustainable campus, starting in 2013 with the opening of Ponderosa Commons, all new residence buildings are built to achieve LEED Gold certification or higher\.

LEED \(Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design\) is a third\-party certification program and an internationally accepted benchmark for the design, construction and operation of high\-performance green buildings\.

#### LEED certified residences

-   Brock Commons Tallwood House \(Gold\)
-   Exchange \(Gold\)
-   Orchard Commons \(Gold\)
-   Ponderosa Commons \(Gold\)
-   tə šxwhəleləm̓s tə k̓waƛ̓kwəʔaʔɬ \(Gold\)
-   Totem Park, c̓əsnaʔəm leləm̓ \(Platinum\)

Brock Commons North and South, opened in 2023 and 2024, were also built to LEED Gold standards and we have applied for certification\. Learn more about [LEED at UBC](https://sustain.ubc.ca/campus/green-buildings/leed-ubc)\.

### **Earlier buildings**

Student Housing and Community Services is responsible for a range of earlier residence buildings opened anywhere from the 1950s to 2011\. We continue to upgrade these residences to increase performance and sustainability—and to significantly decrease greenhouse gas emissions—to meet the goals outlined in the university’s [Climate Action Plan](https://sustain.ubc.ca/campus/climate-action/climate-action-plan)\.

Upgrades include decarbonization of gas\-fired equipment, replacing fluorescent and incandescent lighting with LED lighting, and replacing shower heads with more efficient versions\.

## Sustainability features

Many of our residences were designed with a range of sustainability features to help increase building performance and reduce greenhouse gas emissions\.

If you’re a resident, learning more about these features will help you better understand some of the automated or preset aspects of your room or unit, such as automated schedules for bathroom fans, optimized temperature controls, low\-flow plumbing fixtures and more\.

### Categories

-   [Water consumption](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/#Water)
-   [Ventilation](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/#Ventilation)
-   [Energy use](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/#Energy)
-   [Waste sorting](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/#waste-sorting)

### Water consumption

#### **Low\-flow plumbing fixtures**

*Brock Commons \| Exchange \| Orchard Commons \| Ponderosa Commons \|tə šxwhəleləm̓s tə k̓waƛ̓kwəʔaʔɬ \| Totem Park \(c̓əsnaʔəm leləm̓, həm̓ləsəm̓ and q̓ələχən\)  
*  
To help manage water consumption, and reduce the energy required to heat water for showers and washing, plumbing fixtures are low flow, including toilets, showers and taps\.

#### **Cold water laundry**

*Brock Commons \| Totem Park \(c̓əsnaʔəm leləm̓\) \| Exchange \| tə šxwhəleləm̓s tə k̓waƛ̓kwəʔaʔɬ*

In these residences, laundry machines use cold water by default\. Although hot water washing is available, machines automatically return to cold water settings after each load\.

In all areas, for the majority of everyday laundry, we recommend using cold water to help reduce energy use and greenhouse gas emissions\.

### Ventilation

*Brock Commons \| Exchange \| Orchard Commons \| Ponderosa Commons \| tə šxwhəleləm̓s tə k̓waƛ̓kwəʔaʔɬ \| Totem Park \(c̓əsnaʔəm, həm̓ləsəm̓ and q̓ələχən\)*

To help keep air fresh, reduce building humidity and better manage energy use, the majority of bathroom ventilation fans are either always on or are automatically on during peak shower times and cannot be controlled manually\.

### Energy use

Our residences are designed to use significantly less energy, through a variety of sustainability features\.

#### **LED lighting**

*Brock Commons \| Exchange \| Orchard Commons \| Ponderosa Commons \| tə šxwhəleləm̓s tə k̓waƛ̓kwəʔaʔɬ \| Totem Park \(c̓əsnaʔəm, həm̓ləsəm̓ and q̓ələχən\)*

These residences use LED light bulbs, which use less energy and last years longer than standard, incandescent bulbs\.

#### **Heating, ventilation and cooling controls**

We manage energy use through a variety of different methods, depending on the system in a given residence\.

Individual controls

*Brock Commons \| Exchange \| Orchard Commons \| Ponderosa Commons \| tə šxwhəleləm̓s tə k̓waƛ̓kwəʔaʔɬ \| Totem Park \(c̓əsnaʔəm, həm̓ləsəm̓ and q̓ələχən\)*

Where residents can operate individually\-controlled heating, ventilation or cooling \(including baseboard heaters\), preset temperature ranges are established to better manage energy use\.

Air\-to\-air heat pumps

*Totem Park \(həm̓ləsəm̓ and q̓ələχən\)*

Common areas are heated by high\-efficiency, air\-to\-air heat pumps

Window sensors

*Brock Commons \| Exchange \| Orchard Commons \| Ponderosa Commons \|* *tə šxwhəleləm̓s tə k̓waƛ̓kwəʔaʔɬ \| Totem Park \(c̓əsnaʔəm, həm̓ləsəm̓ and q̓ələχən\)*

If a window is open, the heat will shut off\.

#### **Building insulation**

*Orchard Commons \| Ponderosa Commons*

These buildings are insulated with exterior high\-density concrete panels\. This unique exterior layer helps to reduce energy loss\.

#### **Energy Star rated appliances** 

*Ponderosa Commons*

Energy Star rated appliances use less energy than traditional appliances\. You may notice your dishwasher takes a little longer to turn on or your fridge might be a little louder than you’re used to\.

### Waste sorting

In addition to these built in sustainability features, every residence has sorting areas with clearly marked collection bins for:

-   Food scraps
-   Paper
-   Recyclable containers
-   Garbage

Learn more about [waste sorting at UBC](https://sustain.ubc.ca/resources/campus-guides/sort-it-out), find out [which bin different items go into](https://sustain.ubc.ca/resources/campus-guides/sort-it-out/z-recyclepedia-search), and play the [online waste sorting game](https://sorting-game.herokuapp.com/) to test your knowledge\.

title: Musqueam Plants
content_markdown:
**tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ \(The Houses of the Ones Belonging to the Saltwater\) is one of our newest residence communities at UBC\. The xʷməθkʷəy̓əm \(Musqueam\) Nation generously gifted the hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓\-language residence and house names to UBC in spring 2021\.**

A number of plants with cultural significance for xʷməθkʷəy̓əm were planted at tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ, with signage installed to provide the UBC community with information about them\.

Explore the plants below to learn more from xʷməθkʷəy̓əm about the importance of each one and listen to hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ audio pronunciations by Elder Larry Grant\.

Plus, visit the signage installation at [tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/houses-of-ones-belonging-to-saltwater/)\. You will also find many of these plants growing at our other student residence areas and across the UBC Vancouver campus\.

[Embedded audio \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/musqueam-plants/)[Media source](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Douglas-fir-bark-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3?_=5)[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/06/Douglas\-fir\-bark\-Musqueam\-name\-pronunciation\.mp3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Douglas-fir-bark-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3)

[Douglas fir branch](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Douglas-fir-2400x1600-1-1024x684.png)

**Douglas fir has many uses\. The wood was used for a variety of purposes, the thick bark of mature trees was ideal for fires, and the pitch was used as a glue and sealant\.**

## tə́χʷacəɬp

**Pacific Yew**

[Embedded audio \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/musqueam-plants/)[Media source](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Pacific-Yew-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3?_=6)[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/06/Pacific\-Yew\-Musqueam\-name\-pronunciation\.mp3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Pacific-Yew-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3)

[Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Pacific-Yew-2400x1600-1-1024x680.png)

**The hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ name for pacific yew translates as “bow tree”\. The straight grain and hardness of the wood make it ideal for bows\. Deer could still be hunted near UBC into the mid\-1900s\.**

## sic̓əɬp

**Vine Maple**

[Embedded audio \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/musqueam-plants/)[Media source](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Vine-Maple-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3?_=7)[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/06/Vine\-Maple\-Musqueam\-name\-pronunciation\.mp3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Vine-Maple-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3)

[Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Vine-Maple-2400x1600-1-1024x683.png)

**Similar to tə́χʷacəɬp \(yew tree\), sic̓əɬp wood can also be used for bows\. Springy vine maples were used to make trap doors in our fortification near UBC at q̓ələχən\.**

[Embedded audio \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/musqueam-plants/)[Media source](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Pacific-Crab-Apple-Tree-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3?_=8)[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/06/Pacific\-Crab\-Apple\-Tree\-Musqueam\-name\-pronunciation\.mp3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Pacific-Crab-Apple-Tree-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3)

**Pacific Crab Apple Fruit**

[Embedded audio \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/musqueam-plants/)[Media source](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Pacific-Crab-Apple-Fruit-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3?_=9)[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/06/Pacific\-Crab\-Apple\-Fruit\-Musqueam\-name\-pronunciation\.mp3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Pacific-Crab-Apple-Fruit-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3)

[Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Pacific-crab-apple-2400x1600-1-1024x683.png)

**The fruit from crab apples can be saved in rain water then cooked and eaten later\. The wood was used for tools such as clubs for hunting and fishing\. qʷəʔapəɬp is also noted in place names, such as the location of what became St\. Mungo’s cannery on the Fraser River’s South Arm and a creek at Spanish Banks in Burrard Inlet\.**

**Fresh edible shoots of salmonberry, thimbleberry, and related plants**

[Embedded audio \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/musqueam-plants/)[Media source](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Salmonberry-Thimbleberry-Fresh-Edible-Shoots-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3?_=14)[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/06/Salmonberry\-Thimbleberry\-Fresh\-Edible\-Shoots\-Musqueam\-name\-pronunciation\.mp3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Salmonberry-Thimbleberry-Fresh-Edible-Shoots-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3)

## t̕ec̓əɬp

**Spirea**

[Embedded audio \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/musqueam-plants/)[Media source](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Spirea-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3?_=17)[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/06/Spirea\-Musqueam\-name\-pronunciation\.mp3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Spirea-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3)

[Pink spirea blossoms with green leaves and stem](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Spirea_2400x1600-1024x683.png)

**The root of this plant’s name, t̕ec̓, is the word for the sticks used as cross pieces to spread salmon when drying or cooking, as this wood is ideal for these purposes\. Similar to qeθəɬp \(ocean spray\), the wood can be fire hardened\.**

## qeθəɬp

**Ocean Spray**

[Embedded audio \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/musqueam-plants/)[Media source](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Ocean-Spray-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3?_=18)[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/06/Ocean\-Spray\-Musqueam\-name\-pronunciation\.mp3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Ocean-Spray-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3)

[White Ocean Spray blossoms and green\-brown stem](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Ocean-Spray-2400x1600-1-1024x682.png)

**This plant has very hard wood, which can be hardened more by heating it over the fire\. It was used for making tools such as digging sticks, hunting gear, mat needles and fishing equipment such as spears and harpoon shafts\.**

## t̕eqeʔəɬp

**Salal Bush**

[Embedded audio \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/musqueam-plants/)[Media source](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Salal-Bush-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3?_=19)[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/06/Salal\-Bush\-Musqueam\-name\-pronunciation\.mp3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Salal-Bush-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3)

[Dark green Salal leaves and light green stem](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Salal-2400x1600-1-1024x683.png)

**Used as a sweetener, the salal berry is at its peak in August and can be eaten when ripe or dried and stored for future use\.**

## sθχeləm̓

**Sword Fern**

[Embedded audio \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/musqueam-plants/)[Media source](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Sword-Fern-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3?_=20)[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2022/06/Sword\-Fern\-Musqueam\-name\-pronunciation\.mp3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/Sword-Fern-Musqueam-name-pronunciation.mp3)

[Three dark green sword fern fronds](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Sword-Fern-2400x1600-1-1024x683.png)

## Learn more

xʷməθkʷəy̓əm \(Musqueam\)

Read [xʷməθkʷəy̓əm’s story](https://www.musqueam.bc.ca/our-story/) and find [educational resources](https://www.musqueam.bc.ca/our-story/educational-resources/)\.

Learn more about the hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ language:

Learn how to pronounce hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓

Listen to the audio pronunciations of the house names at [tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/houses-of-ones-belonging-to-saltwater-names/)\.

title: Musqueam Names at tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ
content_markdown:
###### [Picture of three houses at tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ \(The Houses of the Ones Belonging to the Saltwater\) on Student Union Boulevard](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/houses-of-ones-belonging-to-saltwater-Suzanne-Rushton.jpg)  
*Photo credit: Suzanne Rushton*

**In spring 2021, the xʷməθkʷəy̓əm \(Musqueam\) Nation generously gifted the hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓\-language name for one of UBC’s newest residence communities, tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ \(The Houses of the Ones Belonging to the Saltwater\)\.**

Along with the residence name, xʷməθkʷəy̓əm also gifted the five house names:

-   **q̓əlɬaləməcən leləm̓** \(Orca House\)
-   **qʷta:yθən leləm̓** \(Sturgeon House\)
-   **sɬewət̕ leləm̓** \(Herring House\)
-   **təməs leləm̓** \(Sea Otter House\)
-   **sqimək̓ʷ leləm̓** \(Octopus House\)

tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ is the first full residence area at UBC that features a gifted hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓\-language name\. Musqueam previously gifted the house names həm̓ləsəm̓ \(2011\), q̓ələχən \(2011\) and c̓əsnaʔəm \(2017\) for use at Totem Park Residence\.

In September 2021, q̓əlɬaləməcən leləm̓ and qʷta:yθən leləm̓ opened, with sɬewət̕ leləm̓ opening in January 2022 and təməs leləm̓ and sqimək̓ʷ leləm̓ opening in April 2022\.

On Tuesday, June 7, 2022, Musqueam and UBC held the naming and opening ceremony for tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ, to celebrate the residence and honour the house names gifted by Musqueam\.

This residence area, located along Student Union Boulevard and Wesbrook Mall, provides housing for nearly 750 students, plus additional residence swing space, hotel accommodations and a Tim Hortons, in a revitalized area of campus with Walter Gage, Brock Commons and Exchange residences\.

## Learn more about the names

### **tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ**

\(The Houses of the Ones Belonging to the Saltwater\)

[Embedded audio \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/houses-of-ones-belonging-to-saltwater-names/)[Media source](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/The-Houses-of-the-Ones-Belonging-to-the-Saltwater-pronunciation.mp3?_=24)[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2021/05/The\-Houses\-of\-the\-Ones\-Belonging\-to\-the\-Saltwater\-pronunciation\.mp3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/The-Houses-of-the-Ones-Belonging-to-the-Saltwater-pronunciation.mp3)

The marine animals, after which the houses at tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ are named, all reside in saltwater\. Collectively, they convey themes of sustainability and biodiversity, along with individuality and cooperation\.

The residence name is deliberately not simplified to prioritize communicating the complexity of the Musqueam language over ease of pronunciation\.

*Artwork by Kelly Cannell, Musqueam artist\.*

## Projects at tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ

Several important projects are now complete or underway at tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ to increase opportunities for student residents, hotel guests and the UBC Vancouver community to engage with Musqueam language and culture at tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ\.

### Glass walkway canopies

Musqueam artist Kelly Cannell was commissioned to produce artwork that corresponded with each of the house names\. Kelly’s designs, featured above, were integrated into three glass canopies, two which cover the walkway between tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ and the Walter Gage Commonsblock\. The third covers a small plaza at the west end of qʷta:yθən leləm̓\. The last of the canopies was installed in winter 2022\.

### Storytelling boards

Work is currently underway with Musqueam on a series of storytelling boards that will be permanently installed in the lobby areas of each building\. These boards will provide important information, details, traditional stories, and visual elements about Musqueam’s relationship with the marine animals for which the buildings are named\.

### Plant signage

A number of plants with cultural significance for xʷməθkʷəy̓əm were planted at tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ and signage is now installed to provide the UBC community with information about each one\. Learn more at [Musqueam plants](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/musqueam-plants/)\.

**It is an honour to receive these naming gifts and it is rewarding to be able to provide our residents with this valuable cultural knowledge through the names and the unique design elements\. – Andrew Parr, Associate Vice\-President, UBC Student Housing and Community Services**

## Our commitment to using hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓

The expectation of the [Musqueam Language](https://www.musqueam.bc.ca/departments/community-services/language/) department is to have the names represented in their full form, not shortened or abbreviated in any way\. By committing to this expectation, UBC Student Housing and Community Services expresses its commitment to Indigenous peoples, and Musqueam people specifically, in following the [Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada’s calls to action](https://www.un.org/development/desa/indigenouspeoples/declaration-on-the-rights-of-indigenous-peoples.html) and adopting the [United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples](https://www.un.org/development/desa/indigenouspeoples/declaration-on-the-rights-of-indigenous-peoples.html) \(UNDRIP\)\.

SHCS is committed to upholding the integrity of each name’s meaning by using them fully and properly when referring to this residence and its five buildings – and by bringing awareness and education to student residents, the campus community, visitors, and UBC and SHCS staff\.

## Background

In recent years, UBC has strengthened its partnership with our host, the Musqueam Nation, including the historic Memorandum of Affiliation, signed in 2006\. Student Housing and Community Services \(SHCS\) has been one of the units on campus to foster its own unique initiatives with Musqueam, including several naming and storytelling initiatives in residence\.

In 2011, Musqueam gifted the names həm̓ləsəm̓ and q̓ələχən, and in 2017, the name c̓əsnaʔəm for use as house names at Totem Park Residence\. These place names connect our student housing residents and the campus community to the land they reside on and the language of the Musqueam people, hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓\.

In 2019, storytelling displays were installed throughout Totem Park to provide residents with an opportunity to learn about their place, its relationship to Musqueam, and Totem Park’s evolving history of using house names to recognize Indigenous communities—in particular the names of the six original houses \(Kwakiutl, Shuswap, Nootka, Dene, Haida, Salish\) and the residence itself, which were named in the 1960s without appropriate community consultation\.

Following the opening of c̓əsnaʔəm, Musqueam and Student Housing and Community Services continued to meet and discuss storytelling and naming opportunities at the new residence area, originally known as Pacific residence\. First, the five houses were gifted their current hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ names; but it was mutually agreed that a hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓\-language name for the residence area would be a better fit\. Shortly thereafter, Musqueam gifted the current name: tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ\.

title: Consent (for parents and guardians)
content_markdown:
[Group of young students together](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Consent_1200x675.jpg)

*Adapted with permission from an article by [Saleema Noon](https://www.saleemanoon.com/), Sexual Health Educator*

**Parental consent for a field trip\. Informed consent to participate in a study\. We throw the word consent around without thinking about it too much, but what about sexual consent? What is it and what do we need to teach our kids about it?**

A while back, I set out to do some research before writing an article about sexual consent when I came across an article on [scarleteen\.com](https://www.scarleteen.com/) \(an amazing sexual health website for teens and people in their 20s\)\. The article, [Driver’s Ed for the Sexual Superhighway: Navigating Consent](https://www.scarleteen.com/article/abuse_assault/drivers_ed_for_the_sexual_superhighway_navigating_consent), gives the most comprehensive discussion of sexual consent I have ever come across \(not shocking, Scarleteen explains everything so much better than I ever could\!\)\.

> **According to Scarleteen, sexual consent is: “An active process of willingly and freely choosing to participate in sex of any kind with someone else, and a shared responsibility for everyone engaging in, or who wants to engage in, any kind of sexual interaction with someone\. When there is a question or invitation about sex of any kind, when consent is mutually given or affirmed, the answer on everyone’s part is an enthusiastic yes\.”**

*So what exactly does that mean?*

Well, “willingly and freely choosing” means that both partners are making sexual decisions in a safe, respectful environment in which they have equal power\. They don’t feel pressured or manipulated, and are comfortable with the consequences of their decision\.

“An enthusiastic yes” reflects a strong desire that a person wants to act on\. They are not indifferent or uncertain\. There are many ways to express a ”yes,” but the safest and clearest way to do it is with words\. Consent is best when it’s a verbal, enthusiastic “YES\!”\.

But sexual consent is not just a one\-time thing\. It is fluid, it can be revoked, it is not one size fits all\.

Jaclyn Friedman, co\-editor of [Yes Means Yes](https://www.sealpress.com/titles/jaclyn-friedman/yes-means-yes/9781580058995/), explains that well when she says:

“Sexual consent isn’t like a light switch, which can be either “on” or “off\.” It’s not like there’s this one thing called “sex” you can consent to anyhow\. “Sex” is an evolving series of actions and interactions\. You have to have the enthusiastic consent of your partner for all of them\. And even if you have your partner’s consent for a particular activity, you have to be prepared for it to change\. Consent isn’t a question\. It’s a state\.

“If, instead of lovers, the two of you were synchronized swimmers, consent would be the water\. It’s not enough to jump in, get wet and climb out—if you want to swim, you have to be in the water continually\. And if you want to have sex, you have to be continually in a state of enthusiastic consent with your partner\.”

So what does all of this mean for us as adults and as parents? Scarleteen does a great job of highlighting the must\-have information for people of all ages about this very complex concept\. Now that’s sexy\!

## The essential rules of the consensual road

**Consent is about everyone involved in a sexual or possibly sexual interaction**\. Not just one gender, not just young people, not just whoever didn’t initiate sex to begin with, not just the person whose body part someone else’s body part may be touching or going into\. For sex to be fully consensual, everyone needs to seek consent, everyone needs to be affirming it, and everyone needs to accept and respect each other’s answers, nixing sex or stepping back, pronto, if and when someone expresses a stop\.

**Consent can ALWAYS be withdrawn\.** Consent to any kind of sex is not a binding contract nor does consent obligate anyone to follow through\. It is also one\-time\-only: because someone consented to sex Tuesday does not mean they were giving consent for sex on Thursday\.

**Nothing makes consent automatic or unnecessary\.** Being someone’s spouse or romantic partner doesn’t give anyone consent by default\. Someone loving you or saying they love you doesn’t mean they have your sexual consent or you have theirs\. No one kind of sex means consent to another, or that anyone is “owed” any sex\. For instance, someone who engages in oral sex is not asking for or consenting to intercourse; someone who says yes to kissing is not saying yes to any other kind of touching\. Because someone has had any kind of sex in the past does not mean they will have sex or consent to sex again with that same person or anyone else nor that they are obligated in any way to do so\.

**In some situations, full, informed and free consent cannot truly be given or shared\.** Those include: being drunk or wasted, being asleep, being unable to really understand what one is saying yes to, including possible risks and outcomes; being under severe duress, like when seriously upset, ill, grieving or scared, or being unable to understand another person’s words or other means of communication\. Consider things like these to be a red light to even asking about sex: sex should usually be off the table entirely in these situations\. Legally, when someone is under the age of legal consent, with someone of an age where sex is not lawful, and in most of the above situations, sex is a crime\.

**Nonconsent means STOP\.** If someone is NOT consenting to something or says no with their words and/or actions, the other person MUST stop trying to do that thing AND must not try to convince that person to do that thing in any way\. If they do not stop, or exert emotional or other pressure and that person gives up and gives in, they are sexually assaulting that person\. Sex is not sex if everyone is not consenting\. If anyone is not consenting or not asking for consent, then what is happening is or may be rape, sexual abuse or assault\.

**A lack of no does not mean yes\.**

## Learn more

### Videos Saleema recommends

[Wanna Have Sex? \(Consent 101\)](https://youtu.be/TD2EooMhqRI)

[Tea Consent](https://youtu.be/fGoWLWS4-kU)

### UBC resources

[Sex and sexual health information and resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/sex-sexual-health), including information about consent\.
