title: Residence Sustainability Enhancement Fund
content_markdown:
**The Residence Sustainability Enhancement Fund \(RSEF\) provides students living in residence at UBC Vancouver with funding for grassroots projects that support sustainability and climate action education and behaviours in our residence communities—and ultimately contribute to a reduction of greenhouse gas emissions\.**

Through this fund, students can submit proposals for projects aimed at reducing UBC Student Housing’s operational greenhouse gas \(GHG\) emissions by 100% in the year 2035, a target in UBC’s [Climate Action Plan 2030](https://planning.ubc.ca/cap2030#focus-areas)\.

Projects can be any size or scope, but they must be climate/sustainability\-themed and specific to student housing at UBC Vancouver\.

## Suggested project areas

Examples of project areas you might consider for your funding proposal\.

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/sustainability-enhancement-fund/)

Waste reduction and recycling initiatives

Projects focused on reducing the amount of waste generated in residence, improving recycling practices and promoting the responsible disposal of materials\.

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/sustainability-enhancement-fund/)

Sustainable food practices

Projects that promote environmentally responsible food production, consumption and waste management, focusing on reducing the carbon footprint of food systems\.

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/sustainability-enhancement-fund/)

Education and awareness campaigns

Projects that aim to raise awareness and educate the residence community on sustainability topics, influencing behavior change and fostering a culture of environmental responsibility\.

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/sustainability-enhancement-fund/)

Behaviour change initiatives

Projects that encourage individuals to adopt more sustainable habits and practices, focusing on reducing energy and resource consumption through behaviour modification\.

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/sustainability-enhancement-fund/)

Green spaces and urban gardening

Projects that enhance the environmental quality of living spaces through the development of green areas, gardens or natural landscapes, contributing to carbon sequestration and biodiversity\.

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/sustainability-enhancement-fund/)

Technology and innovation

Projects leveraging technology to create new solutions for sustainability challenges, often involving energy monitoring, optimization or the development of eco\-friendly systems\.

## All about the fund

### Who can apply?

The RSEF is open to students living in student housing, operated by UBC Student Housing and Community Services \(SHCS\), on UBC’s Vancouver Campus\.

### What is the application timeline?

Applications are welcome each year during the following period\.

-   Applications open: November 17, 2025
-   Application deadline: January 4, 2026 at 11:55 pm

### How much funding is available?

The total pool of funding available in the RSEF is $10,000 CAD\.

### How much can I apply for?

Students can apply for any amount up to the total fund value of $10,000 CAD for their project\.

Applying for a lower or higher amount does not increase or decrease your chances of receiving funding\. All applications will be assessed based on the quality of the project\.

Projects may be approved at a higher \(maximum $10,000\) or lower value than what was applied for, depending on the adjudication results and how many projects are awarded funding\.

### How do I apply?

[Apply online](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4HrHvlOpDx8DNie) between November 17, 2025 and January 4, 2026\.

### When will I find out the results?

We’ll let all applicants know about the results of their applications in February\.

### When do projects need to take place?

The project implementation timeline is flexible–based on the requirements of your individual project– but you will need to start the project before the fall term\.

## Evaluation criteria

Applications will be reviewed based on the following criteria\. All projects must involve actions or activities that take place on residence property\.

### Impact on greenhouse gas emissions \(GHGs\)

The degree to which the project directly or indirectly reduces greenhouse gas emissions\.

Projects should offer measurable and significant reductions in emissions, either through energy efficiency, waste reduction or other mechanisms\.

### Feasability

The practicality of implementing the project within the given timeframe, budget, and available resources\.

Proposals should demonstrate a clear plan, including logistics, timelines, and cost estimates, and should be realistic for students and the institution to carry out\.

### Innovation and creativity

The originality and ingenuity of the project in addressing sustainability challenges\.

Projects should introduce new approaches, leverage emerging technologies or creatively solve sustainability problems may be more impactful and engaging\.

### Educational value

The potential of the project to raise awareness and educate the residence community about sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions\.

Projects should engage students in learning about sustainability, whether through workshops, campaigns or demonstration projects\.

### Scalability and replicability

The potential for the project to be expanded or replicated in other areas of campus or beyond\.

Projects should be able to grow over time, be implemented in other residences or areas of campus, or inspire similar projects that will have a lasting impact\.

### Long\-term sustainability

The ability of the project to maintain its benefits and impact over time without requiring significant ongoing resources\.

Projects that offer long\-term solutions with minimal maintenance or continued input will provide lasting value and sustainability\.

### Student engagement and collaboration

The degree to which the project involves and engages other students, stakeholders, or groups on campus\.

Projects that foster teamwork, student leadership, and collaboration across different areas of campus life will have broader participation and community support\.

### Cost\-effectiveness

The balance between the project’s costs and its expected environmental and educational benefits\.

Proposals should show that they deliver strong sustainability outcomes relative to the budget allocated, maximizing value for the available funds\.

### Measurability of outcomes

The ability to track and assess the success of the project in achieving its goals, particularly in terms of reducing greenhouse gas emissions\.

Projects should include metrics or systems for measuring progress and success, such as energy savings, waste reduction or other quantifiable environmental impacts\.

### Alignment with campus sustainability goals

How well the project aligns with the university’s existing sustainability goals, policies and initiatives\.

Projects that contribute to broader institutional sustainability objectives, such as carbon neutrality goals or waste reduction targets, should be prioritized\.

title: Moving Out
content_markdown:
[Mindful Move Out](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Mindful-Move-Out-2019.jpg)

# Prepare for Move Out

**Moving out at the end of term? Staying on, but expecting new roommates? Let’s make the transition smooth, fair and sustainable—for everyone\!** 

Here are four steps to help you avoid last\-minute moving chaos and ensure that rooms and shared spaces are left as clean as you’d want them if you were moving in\.

Prepare for Move Out Weekend

Find out everything you need to know if you’re moving out on [Move Out Weekend](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-out/move-out-weekend/): April 24–April 26, 2026\. Reminder, **your room must be clean and vacated by 12 pm on April 26**\.  

## 1\. Sort

-   **Keep, donate or recycle\.** Organize your belongings into these three categories for maximum efficiency—and sustainability\!
-   **Donate items at your residence donation zones starting in early April\.**
-   **Return your Friendlier containers\.** Return your containers to the Friendlier collection bins in residence commonsblocks in April\. Make sure to scan your containers to collect your deposit\!
-   **Big Brothers Textile Bins\.** Donate unwanted but still usable clothing and other items in our new textile donation bins in residence waste rooms\.
-   **Remember, some items actually belong in the garbage**: broken, soiled or ripped items that can’t be recycled and half\-eaten or used foods that can’t be composted belong in the garbage\.

Items you can donate

At your donation zone, you’ll see bins where clean and functional items can be donated into the following categories:

-   **electronics**
-   **textiles** \(sheets, clothing, etc\.\)
-   **household items** \(small appliances, kitchen things, dishware, storage containers, mini fridges, shoe racks, lamps, etc\.\)
-   **non\-perishable food** \(not expired, doesn’t require a fridge\)
-   **books and school supplies**

We’re featuring these items to help keep them out of the waste stream and make sure they can find a new home at UBC or in the community\. Circular economy for the win\!

Please make sure items are clean and in good condition before donating\. Thanks\!

Where can I donate or recycle a used bike?

You can donate your used bike to [The Bike Kitchen](https://www.thebikekitchen.ca/), located in the Life Building \(Room 36\)\. They’ll either refurbish or recycle your old bike and bike parts\.

Learn more on the [Campus and Community Planning cycling page](https://planning.ubc.ca/transportation/cycling) and the [Bike Kitchen donations page](https://www.thebikekitchen.ca/donate)\.

Where can I recycle used batteries?

While we don’t accept used batteries in the donation zones, you can recycle yours at convenient locations across campus\!

> View this post on Instagram
> 
> [A post shared by Campus and Community Planning \(@campusubc\)](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DBg_siNywyi/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

  

## 2\. Pack

-   **Don’t leave it until the last minute\!**
-   **Pack a little bit every day\.** You’ll be surprised how many things you can pack up in advance\.
-   **REMINDER:** You must clean your unit and move out BEFORE 12:00 pm on Sunday, April 26\.

**Pro tip:** If you need to store any of your belongings for next year, you might want to consider a local mini\-storage company\. Look into a company that will best suit your needs\. Whatever option you choose, be sure to book early—and ask if they offer student discounts\!

## 3\. Clean

-   **It’s [time to clean](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-out/cleaning-departure/)\!** Every space needs to be cleaned, whether you’re moving out or getting a new roommate\.
-   **Leave the room the way it was when you moved in\.** This means wiping down everything and vacuuming\. 
-   **Your room will be inspected after you move out\.** If it is not cleaned well enough or there is damage, you will be charged\. Visit the [cleaning and departure checklist](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-out/cleaning-departure/) webpage for an overview of what is expected\.
-   **Be thorough, respectful and leave nothing behind\.**

**Pro tip:** Check out some great de\-cluttering tips at [@GoCleanCo](https://www.instagram.com/gocleanco/?hl=en) on Instagram

## 4\. Check out\!

-   **You must clean your unit, remove all of your items and move out BEFORE 12:00 pm on Sunday, April 26\.**
-   **There are usually lineups, so arrive by 11:30 am** to ensure that you can complete the check out process by noon\.
-   **Set up mail forwarding** in the Student Housing [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/)\. \(Fairview Crescent residents: contact [Canada Post](http://www.canadapost.ca/) to forward mail\.\) Note: This service is not available for packages\.  
    
    *If you do not set up mail forwarding, any mail or packages that we receive after you check out will be returned to sender\.* 
    
-   **Check out at your residence check out area\.**
-   **Ensure you have everything taken with you\.**

Please note that all parking rules and signage are in effect\. Parking in fire lanes or “authorized vehicles only” spaces and roads may result in a ticket if you are moving out any day other than April 26\.  

[Cleaning & departure checklists](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-out/cleaning-departure/)

title: Steps to Success
content_markdown:
[Students studying together](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/steps-to-success.png)

By Andy Chen and Humaira Hamid, UBC students

Many new students struggle with questions such as, “How tough are my courses going to be? Will I be able to keep up? What if I need extra help?” Good news\! UBC has resources for students to build exceptional study and learning skills\.

## Use available resources

-   Professors and teaching assistants \(TAs\) are available after class and during office hours to help with assignments and difficult material\. Don’t be afraid to ask\.
-   UBC offers a range of [free resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources) including study tips, writing strategies, and citation guides\.
-   UBC [Chapman Learning Commons](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/) has helpful resources and tools for learning more effectively\.

## Re\-think lectures

Professors have limited time to cover course material in lectures, so they focus on what’s most important\. Stay on top of your reading and assignments, and consider lectures as an opportunity to review material you’ve already covered on your own\. Most professors recommend 2–3 hours of study outside class for every hour in class\.

## Make peace with exams

They’re unavoidable\. Exams are part of university life\. Prepare the best you can but don’t get discouraged by lower\-than\-expected grades at first\. Many students need time to adjust to university life\.

## Connect and engage

Try connecting with people in your classes\. Making friends or forming study groups with like\-minded students is a great way to stay motivated\.

## Manage your time

When scheduling classes, consider this:

-   Is your course load manageable? Many courses include labs, discussions or tutorials on top of lecture hours\.
-   Have you left time for breaks? It can be tempting to schedule courses back\-to\-back, but you’ll need time to eat, socialize and chill\.

## Kickstart your career

Make the most of your time at UBC and [get a head start on your career](https://students.ubc.ca/career)\. Get started with a wide range of UBC tools and resources or build experience by developing and applying your skills and knowledge through local and international opportunities\.

## Understand plagiarism

[Plagiarism](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/resource-guides/understand-academic-integrity/) means using the thoughts or words of another author and passing them off as your own\. Plagiarism is not tolerated at UBC and can quickly end your university career\.

Hello everyone\! My name is Abolaji, and I’m an RA in Place Vanier\. I’m currently in my fourth year in the Faculty of Science, majoring in Biology with a minor in Environmental Science\. This is my third year as a Residence Advisor, and I still can’t believe how far I’ve come\. When I first applied to be an RA, I was so nervous and unsure of what to expect, but here I am now, three years later, feeling confident, proud, and so grateful for everything this role has taught me\.

My time as an RA has been transformative\. It’s helped me build my confidence, strengthen my leadership skills, and grow in ways that have impacted almost every part of my life\. It’s been incredibly rewarding to build meaningful and lasting connections with people, support residents, and create a welcoming environment where students feel seen and valued\.

Outside of Residence Life, I enjoy spending time in nature, reading, drawing, and exploring new creative outlets\. I’m so excited for another amazing year as an RA and I can’t wait to continue growing, learning, and supporting my residents along the way\!

title: Frequently Asked Questions
content_markdown:
[Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/RA-25_job-web-group-scaled.png)  

  
Interested in [applying to be a Residence Advisor](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/jobs/) in 2026/27? Check out our Frequently Asked Questions below and complete the [Residence Advisor Information Course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/C38FPT) to learn more\.  

### Can I apply if I haven’t lived in residence?

Yes, we accept [applications](https://ubc-van.erezlife.com/) from all UBC students\. However, experience living in residence at UBC is strongly preferred\.  

### If I haven’t lived in residence before, where can I find out more about the different residences?

You can find out more on our website under [residences](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences-rooms/residences/)\. Additionally, please note that due to operational requirements, almost all new Residence Advisors will be placed in Place Vanier, Totem Park, or Walter Gage Residences\.  

### I’m here on a student visa\. Can I apply?

Yes\. If selected for a position, you will need a Canadian [Social Insurance Number](http://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/financial-advice/taxes-international/sin) \(SIN\)\.  

### What if I am not currently a UBC student, but am applying to a graduate program for September and do not have a student number or access to Canvas?

While experience living in residence at UBC is strongly preferred, we would be happy to receive your application\! As long as you are enrolled at UBC for September of the year which your RA contract begins, you are welcome to apply\.

When filling out your application, if you do not have a student number yet, feel free to put a random set of numbers as a place holder when creating an account\. You can update the ID to your proper UBC ID once you have it, or you can contact [residence\.life@ubc\.ca](mailto:residence.life@ubc.ca) and we can update it for you\.

For Canvas, you are able to create a guest account and then should be able to gain access to the Canvas course\. Please see this link \(paying close attention to the section on “Guest Accounts”: [How to Create an Account \| UBC Information Technology\.](https://it.ubc.ca/services/accounts-passwords/campus-wide-login-cwl/how-create-account#:~:text=Basic%20accounts%20are%20for%20those,Gather%20your%20information.&text=Together%2C%20this%20becomes%20the%20name%20displayed%20by%20CWL)  

### What should I include in my application?

Incorporate your past work and volunteer experience into your answers in the [online application](https://ubc-van.erezlife.com/)\.

Please note the use of artificial intelligence \(AI\) is not permitted in the RA application process\. If generative AI is detected in your RA application, it will lead to disqualification in the process\.  

### How do I access my application answers from last year?

Unfortunately, we are unable to share answers from previous application years\. If you wish to keep a copy of your answers from this year, in case you need it in the future, please make sure to save a copy on your own device\.

### Do I need to complete the Residence Advisor Information Course?

If you are applying for a new Residence Advisor position, you will need to complete the [Residence Advisor Information Course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/C38FPT) for your application to be considered\. It is mandatory for any applicant who is applying for a RA position\.

[TAKE THE COURSE](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/C38FPT)

*You can self\-enroll in the course at any time prior to the deadline, but we recommend you complete the course as soon as possible, since it will answer additional questions that you may have and help you submit a higher quality application\. **The deadline to complete the course is January 18, 2026**—the same as the application deadline\.*  

### Do I also need to apply to live in residence?

To be considered for a space in residence, either as a Residence Life staff member or a resident, \(depending on the outcome of your job application\), you need to apply to live in residence\. If you are selected for a Residence Life position, you will then be guaranteed a space in residence\. If you are selected to be a Residence Life staff member and this is not the first time you have paid a residence application fee on the UBC Vancouver campus, your Student Housing account will be reimbursed for the $50 application fee\.  

### What will the interview process look like this year?

If you are selected to participate in our interview process, we will contact you via email with more information\. Interviews will be conducted in person on the UBC Vancouver campus\.

While we give consideration to all applicants, because most new Residence Advisor positions are placed in our first\-year residences, it is typically our experience that many applicants who are pursuing undergraduate studies are selected as a Residence Advisor\.

### If I’m offered a job, can I choose my own residence assignment?

We cannot guarantee placement in a specific residence\. Additionally, please note that due to operational requirements, almost all new Residence Advisors will be placed in Place Vanier, Totem Park, or Walter Gage Residences\. While we take your application answers into consideration, they may limit your placement and/or ability to be offered a Residence Advisor position\. Candidates should be willing and able to accept a position in any residence area that they may be placed into\.  

### If I’m offered a job, when will I receive a job offer?

We anticipate that we will be able to begin sending job offers to successful candidates by the end of May\.  

### Can I have a roommate?

Residence Advisors are not permitted to have roommates\. However, if you are married or have a common\-law spouse, your spouse is permitted to live with you\. Please let us know during the interview process if you have a spouse who will be living with you, so that we can ensure you’re placed in appropriate accommodation\.  

### If my family lives in the Lower Mainland, will I have the opportunity to return home from time to time?

Your schedule will give you the opportunity to visit friends and family from time to time\. You are required to stay in residence three nights per week\. One of these nights will be a Friday or Saturday each week\. You will be planning the schedule with your team on an ongoing basis\.

Additionally, you will be required to attend Residence Life staff meetings as follows:

-   Every Monday in September and January
-   Every second Monday for the remainder of each term\.

These staff meetings begin at 7 pm and typically last one hour; they are usually followed by small team meetings \(i\.e\., meetings with a small group of other Residence Advisors that you work closely with\)\.  

### If I am offered a position, will I have opportunities to take time away \(e\.g\., for holidays, academic events, etc\.\)?

Residence Advisors are able to take a specified amount of time away during the year\. All requests must be approved in advance by a manager\.

For more information about vacation time, absences related to illness and examination leave, please review the [Residence Advisor Letter of Agreement](https://hr.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/documents/mos_cupe_116_october_5_2022.pdf)\.  

### Will I be required to work during Reading Break?

You are expected to be present for scheduled in\-nights \(work\) during Reading Break\. The schedule will be determined by your Residence Life team\.  

### Will I be required to work during the holiday break \(late\-December to early\-January\)?

Most staff are able to take time off during the holiday break and are required to work until the last day of exams in December\.  

### Where can I find more information about job expectations?

Please refer to the applicable [job descriptions](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/jobs/)\.  

### Are RAs permitted to accept other paid commitments at UBC?

Advisors may be able to take on additional employment, but it cannot exceed a full\-time number of paid hours per day or week at UBC\. If you are uncertain whether your other paid employment at UBC would result in you exceeding full time hours, please contact [residence\.life@ubc\.ca](mailto:residence.life@ubc.ca)\.  

### Am I able to hold the Residence Advisor position in addition to being a Jumpstart or Imagine UBC Orientation Leader?

Unfortunately, one may not hold the Residence Advisor and Orientation Leader positions at the same time\. This is due to conflicting role\-related responsibilities from late\-August to early\-September\.  

### Are there other jobs available in residence?

We recruit candidates as needed for administrative/support positions such as front desk services and housekeeping\. Visit [SHCS Careers](https://shcs.ubc.ca/careers/) to learn more\. Summer housekeeping jobs are posted in January/February\. [UBC Food Services](http://www.food.ubc.ca/jobs/#student-jobs) also recruits part\-time workers as needed\. You can also find available SHCS and other UBC positions at [UBC Staff Careers](https://ubc.wd10.myworkdayjobs.com/ubcstaffjobs)\.  

### Are there jobs available at Acadia Park?

Typically, four Community Assistants are employed at Acadia Park, UBC’s student family residence\. Contracts end annually on April 30 and are renewed if work performance is satisfactory\. Resumés are accepted year\-round at the Acadia Park Front Desk and kept on file until a position becomes vacant\.  

### How flexible is my schedule during the mandatory two\-week orientation job training in August?

The Residence Advisor job training is a full\-time, intensive training period\. It is recommended that you schedule any other commitments outside of this time\.  

### Who can I ask if I have additional questions?

**New applicants:** Please complete the mandatory [Residence Advisor Information Course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/C38FPT) online via Canvas\. If you have any remaining questions, contact information is provided at the end of the course\.

title: Shared Living
content_markdown:
[Two roommates talking in kitchen](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/Shared-Living.png)

By Brook Jones, UBC student

Living in residence with dozens of peers, and no parents, is probably new\. As with any new experience, there may be a few adjustments to make\.

Luckily, the key to success is summed up in one word: R\-E\-S\-P\-E\-C\-T\. That’s how Aretha Franklin spelled it, and who am I to argue with the First Lady of Soul? The only way to keep these shared living spaces from falling into utter chaos is by showing respect for your room\-, floor\- and house\-mates\.

### Different strokes

One of the great things about living in residence is being close to friends and peers\. But it can sometimes be a drawback\. For example, everyone has their own standard of acceptable noise levels, which can vary depending on the time of day, time or whether exams are happening\.

Realize that you’re a member of an academic community\. You need to respect your neighbours’ noise level needs and they need to respect yours\. If you can do that, and be willing to compromise, you’ll definitely be able to make residence livable\.

### Clean up your act

Cleanliness is another area where respect is paramount\. You’ll share hallways, a lounge and, possibly, a room\. Each one of you will have your own definition of acceptable cleanliness\. It’s important to establish standards and cleaning responsibilities\. With common areas it’s simple:

-   Be tidy\.
-   Don’t let food rot in the fridge\.
-   Clean your dirty dishes promptly\.

Housekeeping staff tidy common areas, but only the basics\. You and your neighbours are all responsible for keeping these areas clean and tidy\. Also, leaving a large mess might result in your floor being charged for the cleanup\.

### Talk it out

Respect for others is the guiding principle of residence contracts, which all residents agree to before moving in\. For questions, or if you feel disrespected, contact your Residence Advisor\. They are there to help resolve these sorts of situations\. Remember, a little Aretha goes a long way\.

title: What Should I Pack?
content_markdown:
[Young woman with moving boxes](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/What-Should-I-Pack_1200x675-1024x576.jpg)

**Space in residence is limited, so try to reduce what you bring with you\. And if you need anything else after you arrive, you can pick up any other essentials at the [UBC Bookstore](https://bookstore.ubc.ca/dorm-shop)—or order ahead and have items prepared for your arrival\!**

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)

### Bring only what you need

Do your best to limit what you bring to residence and accumulate while you’re living at UBC\. You’ll need to take all your belongings with you when you [move out](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-out/) and donate, sell, recycle or throw away all the stuff you no longer want\.

#### **How bringing less helps**

With nearly 14,000 students living in residence, we can generate a lot of waste\. By reducing what you bring in the first place, you’ll help reduce the waste you produce while living in residence\.  
  
Let’s all work together to help [reduce waste in residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/#waste)—in support of UBC’s [Zero Waste Action Plan](https://planning.ubc.ca/zero-waste-action-plan) and [Climate Action Plan](https://planning.ubc.ca/cap2030)\.

## **On this page**

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[What to bring](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#what-to-bring)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Permitted appliances](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#permitted-appliances)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[What not to bring](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#what-not-to-bring)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Prohibited items](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#prohibited-items)

## What to bring

### Essentials

Items everyone should have on their packing list\.

#### Personal items

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Identification documents—including government\-issued photo ID\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Health insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/) documents—health care card and extended health and dental insurance documents\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Renter’s insurance](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/renters-insurance/) documents
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Prescriptions/medications
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Toiletries—toothbrush, toothpaste, soap, etc\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Toiletry tote bag
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Bath towel
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Water bottle—to fill up with [safe, clean drinking](https://srs.ubc.ca/environment/drinkingwater/) water right from the tap\.

#### Room supplies

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Bed and bath linens](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/bed-linens/)—order ahead for delivery to your residence\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Pillow
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Pillow case\(s\)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Clothes hangers
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Laundry bag—for storing your dirty laundry and toting it to the laundry room\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Laundry detergent—detergent sheets/strips are the most sustainable option\!
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Basic cleaning supplies—disinfectant spray and reusable cloth for cleaning surfaces\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Emergency kit](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/emergency-preparedness/#emergency-kit)

#### Electronics

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Laptop
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Laptop security lock
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Headphones
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Extension cord
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Power bar / surge protector
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Ethernet cable—for students living in [residence areas with wired internet](https://it.ubc.ca/services/email-voice-internet/resnet)\.

#### Clothing and footwear

What to pack for Vancouver’s climate: mild, rainy winters and warm, sunny summers\.

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Essential items—pack light, bringing just the essentials you’ll wear regularly\. A minimal wardrobe to reduce waste, decrease environmental impact and travel more sustainably\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Multi\-purpose items—that you can style up or down in any season\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Items you can layer—so you’re ready to adapt to quick weather and temperature changes\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Waterproof outerwear—a jacket that can handle medium to heavy rain\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Weather\-resistant footwear—UBC is mainly a pedestrian campus, so you’ll need good quality footwear for getting around when the weather’s rainy\.

### **For suites with bathrooms and kitchens**

Additional items for residents moving into a suite with a [bathroom](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#bathrooms) and/or [kitchen](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#kitchens)\.

#### Suites with bathrooms

In addition to your personal toiletries, you’ll need these items for your private or semi\-private bathroom\.

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Toilet paper
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Hand soap
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Hand towel
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Cleaning supplies

#### Suites with kitchens

You’ll need to bring these items for your kitchen\.

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Cutlery
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Dishes
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Pots and pans
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Cooking utensils
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Food storage containers
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Dish cloths
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Kitchen towels
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Dish detergent
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Dishwasher detergent—if your suite features a dishwasher\.

Remember, you’ll need to take everything with you when you leave\.

-   Plan ahead and consider which items you’ll actually use\.
-   Connect with roommates to reduce duplicate items\.
-   Visit our annual [Mindful Market](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/mindful-market/) in September to purchase cheap, second\-hand items and support UBC’s circular economy\.

**🌿 Sustainability tips—cleaning supplies\!**

To reduce plastic waste and your overall environmental impact, try to buy cleaning supplies that are biodegradable, non\-toxic, concentrated, and/or come in recyclable packaging or refillable containers\.

Reusable cleaning cloths or sponges, instead of single\-use options, are great too\!

### UBC’s Mindful Consumption Guide

Check out UBC’s [Mindful Consumption Guide](https://sustain.ubc.ca/resources/mindful-consumption-guide) to learn about making informed purchasing decisions and discover UBC resources, programs and more\.

## Permitted appliances

These cooking and cooling appliances are permitted in residence\.

### Cooking appliances

If you’ll be living in a unit with a kitchen, it will feature a stove, oven\* and fridge, with some also offering a dishwasher and microwave\. Check your [residence and room type](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences-rooms/residences/) to confirm\!

\*except in our [Nano suites](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/rooms/nano/), where the kitchenette features a stovetop only\.

If you want to bring some additional appliances, these items are permitted, as follows\.

#### Permitted in any residence area

These items are permitted in any residence area, but are typically not needed in Orchard Commons, Place Vanier or Totem Park, which have a required meal plan for the residence dining halls\.

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Toaster
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Electric kettle
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Coffee maker
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Rice cooker
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Sandwich maker

#### Permitted—except in first year residence areas

These items are permitted in residence, except in Orchard Commons, Place Vanier and Totem Park, where they are prohibited\.

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Toaster oven
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Air fryer

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)

### Pro tips\!

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)If you’ll be living in Orchard Commons, Place Vanier or Totem Park, you won’t need any additional appliances \(cooking or a mini fridge\), except perhaps an electric kettle, since you’ll have an [All Access Residence Dining Plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/residence-meal-plan-all-access-dining/) with access to residence dining rooms from early morning to late at night\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)If you have roommates, connect with them before you move in and see what they’re bringing or what they already have to reduce the chance of duplicates\.

### Appliance not listed above?

If there’s a cooking appliance you were hoping to bring, but it’s not listed above, you must [contact your Residence Life Manager](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/) to find out if it could be permitted\.

### Can I bring a mini fridge?

While you are permitted to bring a mini fridge to residence—that’s no bigger than 0\.14 cubic metres \(5 cubic feet\)—many students end up finding that it’s an unnecessary item\.

If you’re moving into a unit with a kitchen, you already have access to a fridge\. If you’re in a residence with a dining hall, you’ll have access to plenty of food and drink from morning to night through your meal plan\.

Plus, it’s burdensome to move in and out of residence and can result in extra electronic waste at the end of the year\.

## Cooling appliances

While most residence buildings don’t include air conditioning, Vancouver’s mild climate means that a portable cooling appliance isn’t necessary during the Winter Session \(September to April\) but may be valuable during the Summer Session \(May to August\)\.

### What is and isn’t permitted

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Portable fans—permitted in all residences\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Portable air conditioners—only permitted in Year Round and Summer residence areas, with written approval from your Residence Life Manager\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Window air conditioners—not permitted in any residence\.

### What you’ll need to stay cool

#### During the Winter Session

If you’re living in a Winter Session residence area, you won’t need a fan—and air conditioners are not permitted in Winter Session residence areas\.

#### During the Summer Session

With temperatures during the Summer Session \(May to August\) becoming warmer on average, some students living in Year Round residence areas find a fan useful for staying cool during these months\.

While portable air conditioners are permitted in Year Round and Summer residence areas, you must [email your Residence Life Manager](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/) to request approval, in advance, to bring one to your unit/room\.

And before you purchase a portable air conditioner, to help us reduce energy use and appliance waste during move out, we ask you to consider whether one is truly necessary and [explore alternative ways to stay cool in hot weather](https://vancouver.ca/home-property-development/hot-weather.aspx#tips)\.

[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Return to top

## What not to bring

**We don’t recommend you bring these items\.**

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Printers](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#printers)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Bikes and vehicles](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#bikes-vehicles)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Expensive and priceless items](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#expensive-priceless)

### Printers

You’ll submit the majority of your assignments digitally, so it’s unlikely you’ll need to print much, if anything, during your time at UBC\. In the rare case, you need to print something, you’ll have easy access to printers in libraries across campus through [UBC Pay for Print](https://services.library.ubc.ca/computers-technology/copy-print-scan/)\.

### Bikes and vehicles

UBC is a very walkable campus—flat and pedestrian\-friendly, with everything inside a 15\-minute walk or so and much of campus a car\-free zone\. So you don’t need to bring a bike or vehicle to get around\.

Plus, with plenty of rain in the winter, students who bring a bike often find they don’t use it as much as they thought they would\.

#### Alternative transportation options

If you need to travel a little further away or get somewhere in a hurry, here are some options\.

##### For getting around campus

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)The [route 68 community shuttle](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-around-ubc/)—an on\-campus TransLink shuttle bus that’s covered under your [U\-Pass](https://planning.ubc.ca/transportation/transit/u-pass-compass-card)\. Great for grocery trips to Wesbrook Village\!
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)UBC’s [Bike Share program](https://planning.ubc.ca/bikeshare)—an affordable bike share program through Mobi, with plenty of locations across campus to access bikes and e\-bikes\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)UBC [Accessibility Shuttle](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/ubc-accessibility-shuttle/)—a free, shared ride service for people with conditions that impact their mobility\.

##### For going off\-campus

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Take transit](https://planning.ubc.ca/transportation/transit)\! With thousands of buses leaving campus each day, it’s easy to get off\-campus with your [U\-Pass](https://planning.ubc.ca/transportation/transit/u-pass-compass-card)\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Bike Share](https://planning.ubc.ca/bikeshare)—Mobi bikes and e\-bikes aren’t just for use on\-campus\. They can be docked and undocked at any of Mobi’s stations throughout UBC and across the City of Vancouver\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)[Car Share](https://planning.ubc.ca/transportation/driving/car-sharing): Modo and Evo—two great options if you need access to a vehicle now and again\.

#### If you do bring a bike

If you do end up bringing a bike or buying one while you’re at UBC, make sure it’s inexpensive—and bring a good U\-lock\. Bike theft happens\. [Learn more](https://planning.ubc.ca/transportation/cycling/cycling-basics-and-maps) about cycling at UBC and how to keep your bike safe on\-campus\.

#### If you do bring a vehicle

Parking availability is limited\. Make sure you apply early\. [Learn more](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/parking/) about residence and campus parking\.

### Expensive and priceless items

Avoid bringing expensive or priceless items to residence, such as luxury jewellery or family heirlooms\. It’s not worth the risk of losing items while moving/travelling or to theft\.

#### Alternative options

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Leave them with someone you trust—a parent/guardian, other family member or supporter, if possible\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Store them in a safety deposit box—explore secure, off\-site storage options, such as a safety deposit box at a bank, either where you call home or here in Vancouver\.

#### If you bring expensive/priceless items

If you do end up bringing any items of significant value to residence \(or store them in a safety deposit box\) ensure that your [renter’s insurance](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/renters-insurance/) covers you in the event of theft or loss\.

[https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/moving\-in/what\-should\-i\-pack/\#top](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#top)[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Return to top

## Prohibited items

The following items are prohibited in residence\. While some items might be obvious, such as firearms, other items might seem less obvious, but are also prohibited for a range of reasons\.

Thank you for your support, cooperation and understanding regarding these prohibited items\. We all play a role in contributing to a safer residence environment\.

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Additional/unauthorized furniture—you must [email your Residence Life Manager](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/) to request approval for any additional furniture that is not listed above\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Air fryers—prohibited in Orchard Commons, Place Vanier and Totem Park only\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Toaster ovens—prohibited in Orchard Commons, Place Vanier and Totem Park only\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Hot plates
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Butane stoves
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)BBQs/barbecues
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Propane / propane tanks
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Hoverboards
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Large appliances—such as washing machines, clothes dryers, stoves, dishwashers and refrigerators\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Pets—except for approved service animals\.\*
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Subwoofer audio equipment
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Window air conditioners
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Mercury thermometers
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Explosives
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Firecrackers
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Real, replica or fake firearms/guns or other weapons\*\*
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Illegal drugs
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/)Any other items that are also prohibited by Canadian federal law and BC provincial law

\*Students must apply for approval via the UBC [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) before bringing a service animal to residence\. For students moving into Acadia Park \(Family Housing\), [learn more](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/acadia-park-pet-policy/) about animals permitted in residence\.

\*\*Please refer to the weapons clause in your [Residence Contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/) for further detail\.

## Questions?

If you have any questions about what to bring, what not to bring, permitted appliances or prohibited items, please [contact us](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.

title: Spirituality
content_markdown:
[UBC Nitobe Garden](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/Spiritual-Fitness.png)

*By Carol Young, Student Housing and Community Services*

## What is spirituality?

Spirituality can be defined in many ways\. Broadly, it is seeking self\-awareness, meaning and understanding of our experiences in the world\. It is searching for a connection to something bigger than ourselves\.

Often university is a time when you become more aware of what has formed and informed you as you connect with others who hold similar and different views\. As your perspectives are affirmed and challenged, you sift through those exchanges to discover what it is that you value and what gives your life meaning\.

## Exploring your spirituality

No matter how you choose to explore spirituality, it is an opportunity for self\-reflection about yourself and how you connect to the world\. Some questions to consider include:

-   What influenced how I was formed and how does that impact the way in which I see and engage others?
-   Do things happen for a reason?
-   How do I extend gratitude to the world?
-   How am I called to improve the lives of others?
-   How have my experiences from the past couple of years changed me? And what learnings will I carry forward from this time to help navigate future challenges and circumstances that come my way?

### Ways to explore spirituality

At UBC, you have many options for exploring your spirituality, if you choose to\. How you practice is entirely up to you\. Here are some ideas:

#### Connect with nature

Take a walk in Pacific Spirit Park, Nitobe Memorial Garden or on Tower Beach\.

#### Connect with people

Engage people in discussions that deepen or challenge your ideas\. Seek out spiritual resources and amenities on campus\.

#### Volunteer

Take part in a service learning or volunteer opportunity to experience the joy of giving back\.

#### Start a journal

Record thoughts and feelings, express gratitude and reflect on big decisions and everyday encounters\.

#### Reflect

Meditate, pray or worship—alone or with others\. Exploring spirituality for some students may come through an association with a church, temple, mosque or synagogue\. Other students may choose to pray, meditate or find comfort in a personal relationship with God or a higher power\. Every student’s spiritual journey is unique\.

**Spirituality is concerned with those qualities of the human spirit—such as love and compassion, patience, tolerance, forgiveness, contentment, a sense of responsibility, a sense of harmony—which brings happiness to both self and others\.**

*Excerpt from* Ancient Wisdom, Modern World: Ethics for the New Millennium *by Tenzin Gyatso, the Fourteenth Dalai Lama\. Published by Little, Brown and Company, United Kingdom\.*

## Chaplains at UBC

Another way some students explore their spirituality is with Chaplains at UBC, which helps members of the UBC community engage with their spirituality and faith\.

The word chaplain was originally associated with the Christian faith, but is now a widely used and accepted term to refer to men and women who represent many religions or philosophical traditions\.

The current membership includes Buddhist, Muslim, Jewish, Christian, and Bahá’í representation\. Among Christian denominations you will find representatives from the Anglican, Baptist, Brethren Tradition, Pentecostal, Presbyterian, Roman Catholic, and United Churches\.

Most chaplains offer one\-on\-one pastoral or spiritual counselling and other opportunities to explore the faith that they represent, like fellowship groups, meals, worship, faith exploration and training, or study\. These groups are a good way to have fun, make friends and explore some of the big questions of life\.

## Learn more

Religion and spirituality

Learn more about [religion and spirituality at UBC](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality), including spiritual practices and spiritual resources—such as Chaplains at UBC, multifaith prayer rooms, and student\-run organizations\.

title: Designated Roommates
content_markdown:
**Residents in self\-contained units, such as studios or one bedrooms, may be eligible to add a designated roommate\.**

## On this page

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)[What is a designated roommate?](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/#definition)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)[Eligibility](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/#eligibility)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)[Access and privileges](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/#access-privileges)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)[Request approval for a designated roommate](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/#request-approval)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)[Review, approval and move\-in](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/#review-approval-move-in)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)[Responsibilities](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/#responsibilities)
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)[FAQs](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/#faqs)

## What is a designated roommate?

A designated roommate is another person—typically a spouse or partner—who the resident \(i\.e\., the residence contract holder\) wishes to live with long\-term\.

This type of roommate is different from [roommates in shared rooms or multi\-bedroom suites](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/roommate-assignments/), who are other UBC students assigned by Student Housing, and who have their own bed or bedroom\.

## Eligibility

To be eligible, your designated roommate application must meet the following criteria:

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)**Eligible unit types:** studio, one bedroom and Exchange townhouse type A\.\*
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)**Living arrangements:** the contract holder and the designated roommate must both live in the unit together; the designated roommate is not entitled to reside in the accommodation unless the contract holder also resides there at the same time\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)**Contract holder eligibility:** the contract holder must continue to meet all [eligibility requirements](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/) for living in UBC Student Housing\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)**Designated roommate eligibility:** the designated roommate does not need to be a UBC student\. However, the designated roommate must meet the [minimum age requirement](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/) for the residence and room type and be in good standing with Student Housing\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)**Requested in advance:** you must obtain prior written consent from Student Housing and Community Services before the designated roommate moves in\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)**Previous designated roommate history:** contract holders are typically eligible to have one designated roommate added for the duration of their time in UBC Student Housing\. Requests to replace or add a new designated roommate when previously approved for a designated roommate are unlikely to be approved\.

\*Nano suites are also eligible unit types\. However, due to their small size, we do not recommend adding a designated roommate\.

*Please note that unauthorized occupancy may result in the termination of a residence contract\. Student Housing and Community Services reserves the right to deny the addition of an occupant or to revoke approval at any time\.*

## Access and privileges

After the application is approved and while the designated roommate lives in the suite, they can:

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)Receive and hold a key for your unit\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)Receive mail for your unit\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)Access residence amenities, such as the commonsblock and fitness room\.

They will not have access to the Student Housing Online Service Centre, so any maintenance requests will need to be submitted by the contract holder\.

## Request approval for a designated roommate

To submit an application for a designated roommate:

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)Make sure your application meets the eligibility requirements outlined above\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)Complete the [Designated Roommate Request Form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6t08EmPkOmifbEO), providing all required information and any supporting documentation\.

### [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)Apply online

Submit your designated roommate application via our online form in Qualtrics\.

[https://ubc\.ca1\.qualtrics\.com/jfe/form/SV\_6t08EmPkOmifbEO](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6t08EmPkOmifbEO)[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)Apply

*Note: The UBC contract holder must submit the application, not the designated roommate\.*

### When should I submit my application?

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)**Submit at least seven business days before the start date:** We will be able to review your application and reply within 5–7 business days after receiving it\. With that in mind, please submit your application at least seven business days in advance of the start date indicated in your application\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)**Submit at any stage of your contract:** You are eligible to submit your application any time—either before or after your contract starts\.

### Is there any time of year when applications are not reviewed?

Due to operational requirements, we are not able to review designated roommate requests or approve designated roommate start dates between August 15 and September 15, except for students whose contracts start between those dates\.

If you submit a request or start date during this period and your contract starts at a different time, the earliest you can anticipate a reply is seven business days after September 15\.

Requests submitted with start dates before or after the August 15 to September 15 period will continue to be reviewed as usual\.

## Review, approval and move\-in

Once you submit, we’ll review your application and let you know if it’s approved or not\.

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)Once we receive your application, we’ll typically review it within five business days—except for August 15–September 15, as noted above\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)Then, we’ll reply by email \([information@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:information@housing.ubc.ca)\) to let you know if the request is approved—or if we have any follow\-up questions or require additional supporting documentation\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)If approved, we’ll let your residence front desk know, and your designated roommate can move in on or after the start date you indicated in your application\.

### [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/designated-roommates/)**You must visit the residence front desk together**

To get your designated roommate a key/card to access your building and unit, when they move in, you and your designated roommate must visit the residence front desk together\.

## Responsibilities

While your designated roommate is living with you in residence, you and your designated roommate are responsible for adhering to the residence contract, including our residence standards\.

### Adhering to the residence contract

Both you and your designated roommate must adhere to all terms and conditions specified in the Residence Contract\. If your designated roommate arrangement ceases to be eligible at any point, Student Housing and Community Services reserves the right to revoke approval at any time\.

### Residence Standards violations

If the designated roommate violates any residence standards, the UBC contract holder may face consequences for the designated roommate’s actions\. Contract holders are responsible for the behaviour and actions of their designated roommate throughout the tenancy\.

## FAQs

### Can I add a designated roommate if I will be away?

No, you must be living in your suite to be eligible for a designated roommate—as outlined in Section 1\.03 or 1\.04 of your [residence contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/)\.

-   If you will be living elsewhere during the Summer Session \(May–August\), you are not eligible to have a designated roommate, but you are eligible to [sublet your unit](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/subletting/)\.
-   If you will be on Co\-op or Exchange during either Term 1 or Term 2 of the Winter Session \(September–April\), you are not eligible to have a designated roommate\. [Learn more about your options](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/subletting/#ws-coop-exchange)\.

### I have a guest/visitor coming to stay for a while\. Do I need to apply for them to be a designated roommate?

No, a short\-term guest or visitor does not need to be added as a designated roommate\. Learn more about hosting guests and visitors in your [residence contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/)\.

### My previously approved designated roommate will be moving out, is there anything I need to do?

Yes, please be sure to inform your residence front desk that your designated roommate is moving out—no later than 10 days after they depart—and return any keys\.

You can do this by visiting the front desk together or separately to inform the residence front desk team, return the keys, and ask for your designated roommate to be checked out\.

## Questions?

If you have any questions, please [contact us](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.
