title: Frequently Asked Questions
content_markdown:
[Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/RA-25_job-web-group-scaled.png)  

  
Interested in [applying to be a Residence Advisor](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/jobs/) in 2026/27? Check out our Frequently Asked Questions below and complete the [Residence Advisor Information Course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/C38FPT) to learn more\.  

### Can I apply if I haven’t lived in residence?

Yes, we accept [applications](https://ubc-van.erezlife.com/) from all UBC students\. However, experience living in residence at UBC is strongly preferred\.  

### If I haven’t lived in residence before, where can I find out more about the different residences?

You can find out more on our website under [residences](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences-rooms/residences/)\. Additionally, please note that due to operational requirements, almost all new Residence Advisors will be placed in Place Vanier, Totem Park, or Walter Gage Residences\.  

### I’m here on a student visa\. Can I apply?

Yes\. If selected for a position, you will need a Canadian [Social Insurance Number](http://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/financial-advice/taxes-international/sin) \(SIN\)\.  

### What if I am not currently a UBC student, but am applying to a graduate program for September and do not have a student number or access to Canvas?

While experience living in residence at UBC is strongly preferred, we would be happy to receive your application\! As long as you are enrolled at UBC for September of the year which your RA contract begins, you are welcome to apply\.

When filling out your application, if you do not have a student number yet, feel free to put a random set of numbers as a place holder when creating an account\. You can update the ID to your proper UBC ID once you have it, or you can contact [residence\.life@ubc\.ca](mailto:residence.life@ubc.ca) and we can update it for you\.

For Canvas, you are able to create a guest account and then should be able to gain access to the Canvas course\. Please see this link \(paying close attention to the section on “Guest Accounts”: [How to Create an Account \| UBC Information Technology\.](https://it.ubc.ca/services/accounts-passwords/campus-wide-login-cwl/how-create-account#:~:text=Basic%20accounts%20are%20for%20those,Gather%20your%20information.&text=Together%2C%20this%20becomes%20the%20name%20displayed%20by%20CWL)  

### What should I include in my application?

Incorporate your past work and volunteer experience into your answers in the [online application](https://ubc-van.erezlife.com/)\.

Please note the use of artificial intelligence \(AI\) is not permitted in the RA application process\. If generative AI is detected in your RA application, it will lead to disqualification in the process\.  

### How do I access my application answers from last year?

Unfortunately, we are unable to share answers from previous application years\. If you wish to keep a copy of your answers from this year, in case you need it in the future, please make sure to save a copy on your own device\.

### Do I need to complete the Residence Advisor Information Course?

If you are applying for a new Residence Advisor position, you will need to complete the [Residence Advisor Information Course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/C38FPT) for your application to be considered\. It is mandatory for any applicant who is applying for a RA position\.

[TAKE THE COURSE](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/C38FPT)

*You can self\-enroll in the course at any time prior to the deadline, but we recommend you complete the course as soon as possible, since it will answer additional questions that you may have and help you submit a higher quality application\. **The deadline to complete the course is January 18, 2026**—the same as the application deadline\.*  

### Do I also need to apply to live in residence?

To be considered for a space in residence, either as a Residence Life staff member or a resident, \(depending on the outcome of your job application\), you need to apply to live in residence\. If you are selected for a Residence Life position, you will then be guaranteed a space in residence\. If you are selected to be a Residence Life staff member and this is not the first time you have paid a residence application fee on the UBC Vancouver campus, your Student Housing account will be reimbursed for the $50 application fee\.  

### What will the interview process look like this year?

If you are selected to participate in our interview process, we will contact you via email with more information\. Interviews will be conducted in person on the UBC Vancouver campus\.

While we give consideration to all applicants, because most new Residence Advisor positions are placed in our first\-year residences, it is typically our experience that many applicants who are pursuing undergraduate studies are selected as a Residence Advisor\.

### If I’m offered a job, can I choose my own residence assignment?

We cannot guarantee placement in a specific residence\. Additionally, please note that due to operational requirements, almost all new Residence Advisors will be placed in Place Vanier, Totem Park, or Walter Gage Residences\. While we take your application answers into consideration, they may limit your placement and/or ability to be offered a Residence Advisor position\. Candidates should be willing and able to accept a position in any residence area that they may be placed into\.  

### If I’m offered a job, when will I receive a job offer?

We anticipate that we will be able to begin sending job offers to successful candidates by the end of May\.  

### Can I have a roommate?

Residence Advisors are not permitted to have roommates\. However, if you are married or have a common\-law spouse, your spouse is permitted to live with you\. Please let us know during the interview process if you have a spouse who will be living with you, so that we can ensure you’re placed in appropriate accommodation\.  

### If my family lives in the Lower Mainland, will I have the opportunity to return home from time to time?

Your schedule will give you the opportunity to visit friends and family from time to time\. You are required to stay in residence three nights per week\. One of these nights will be a Friday or Saturday each week\. You will be planning the schedule with your team on an ongoing basis\.

Additionally, you will be required to attend Residence Life staff meetings as follows:

-   Every Monday in September and January
-   Every second Monday for the remainder of each term\.

These staff meetings begin at 7 pm and typically last one hour; they are usually followed by small team meetings \(i\.e\., meetings with a small group of other Residence Advisors that you work closely with\)\.  

### If I am offered a position, will I have opportunities to take time away \(e\.g\., for holidays, academic events, etc\.\)?

Residence Advisors are able to take a specified amount of time away during the year\. All requests must be approved in advance by a manager\.

For more information about vacation time, absences related to illness and examination leave, please review the [Residence Advisor Letter of Agreement](https://hr.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/documents/mos_cupe_116_october_5_2022.pdf)\.  

### Will I be required to work during Reading Break?

You are expected to be present for scheduled in\-nights \(work\) during Reading Break\. The schedule will be determined by your Residence Life team\.  

### Will I be required to work during the holiday break \(late\-December to early\-January\)?

Most staff are able to take time off during the holiday break and are required to work until the last day of exams in December\.  

### Where can I find more information about job expectations?

Please refer to the applicable [job descriptions](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/jobs/)\.  

### Are RAs permitted to accept other paid commitments at UBC?

Advisors may be able to take on additional employment, but it cannot exceed a full\-time number of paid hours per day or week at UBC\. If you are uncertain whether your other paid employment at UBC would result in you exceeding full time hours, please contact [residence\.life@ubc\.ca](mailto:residence.life@ubc.ca)\.  

### Am I able to hold the Residence Advisor position in addition to being a Jumpstart or Imagine UBC Orientation Leader?

Unfortunately, one may not hold the Residence Advisor and Orientation Leader positions at the same time\. This is due to conflicting role\-related responsibilities from late\-August to early\-September\.  

### Are there other jobs available in residence?

We recruit candidates as needed for administrative/support positions such as front desk services and housekeeping\. Visit [SHCS Careers](https://shcs.ubc.ca/careers/) to learn more\. Summer housekeeping jobs are posted in January/February\. [UBC Food Services](http://www.food.ubc.ca/jobs/#student-jobs) also recruits part\-time workers as needed\. You can also find available SHCS and other UBC positions at [UBC Staff Careers](https://ubc.wd10.myworkdayjobs.com/ubcstaffjobs)\.  

### Are there jobs available at Acadia Park?

Typically, four Community Assistants are employed at Acadia Park, UBC’s student family residence\. Contracts end annually on April 30 and are renewed if work performance is satisfactory\. Resumés are accepted year\-round at the Acadia Park Front Desk and kept on file until a position becomes vacant\.  

### How flexible is my schedule during the mandatory two\-week orientation job training in August?

The Residence Advisor job training is a full\-time, intensive training period\. It is recommended that you schedule any other commitments outside of this time\.  

### Who can I ask if I have additional questions?

**New applicants:** Please complete the mandatory [Residence Advisor Information Course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/C38FPT) online via Canvas\. If you have any remaining questions, contact information is provided at the end of the course\.

title: Information for sponsors
content_markdown:
[Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/54688561707_560e133192_o.gif)

**Organizations can sponsor UBC students’ housing and meal plan fees\. Sponsors must meet eligibility criteria and apply by the deadline\.**

## On this page

-   [Eligibility](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/information-for-sponsors/#eligibility)
-   [How to apply](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/information-for-sponsors/#apply)
-   [Application deadlines](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/information-for-sponsors/#deadlines)
-   [Invoices and payments](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/information-for-sponsors/#invoices-payments)
-   [Information privacy](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/information-for-sponsors/#information-privacy)

## Eligibility

### Who can sponsor

Sponsors must be a government agency, company, Indigenous band or other organization\. Individuals, parents or relatives cannot sponsor a student through this program\. If a sponsor or third\-party vendor reimburses fees directly to the student rather than paying UBC, this is not considered sponsorship\.

### How sponsorship works

Sponsors are invoiced each term for the costs they agree to cover and pay UBC directly for these fees\. All sponsors must submit an online Student Housing Sponsorship Application for each student—or one application for a group of students who fall under the same sponsorship criteria\.

### Currency and exchange rates

UBC accepts payments in Canadian or US funds only\. US funds will be converted to Canadian funds using UBC Finance’s daily exchange rate on the date we process the payment\. We cannot use exchange rates provided by sponsors\.

To avoid exchange rate discrepancies, send funds in Canadian dollars\. When setting a sponsorship contract dollar limit, you can only set limits in Canadian funds\.

#### Tax receipts

Following Canada Revenue Agency guidelines, sponsoring organizations must issue a T4A tax receipt to their sponsored students\. UBC does not provide this document\.

## How to apply

Complete the Student Housing Sponsorship Application for each student you intend to sponsor—or one application for each group of students who fall under the same sponsorship criteria—by the deadlines below\.

You can sponsor a student for as short as one term or for the entire calendar year\.

If you support a student for one term and later want to continue the sponsorship, submit a new application\. Contracts do not automatically renew\.

[SUBMIT A SPONSORSHIP APPLICATION](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_8q9foXnpnROykLA)

If you are unable to apply online, please email a completed [Student Housing sponsorship billing form \(PDF\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Student-Housing-Sponsorship-Application.pdf) to [information@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:information@housing.ubc.ca)\.

## Application deadlines

Submit your sponsorship application by these dates\. If you’re unable to apply before the deadlines, [contact us](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.

| Academic session | Time period | Application deadline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Summer Session | May to August | **April 1** |
| Winter Session Term 1 | September to December | **August 1** |
| Winter Session Term 2 | January to April | **November 1** |

UBC sponsorship for tuition fees

If you plan to support your student\(s\) with tuition or other student\-related fees, apply separately through the [Sponsorship Billing office](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsors/) by their deadline\.

## Invoices and payments

### When you’ll receive invoices

We invoice sponsors at the end of each term for the costs they agree to pay\. If you’re covering multiple terms and require separate invoices in advance, indicate this request on your application form\.

### Making a payment

Paying by cheque is the preferred method for sponsorship funding\. Other payment options are also available\.

#### To pay by cheque:

1.  Make your cheque payable to “The University of British Columbia”
2.  Enter the following information in the memo field
    -   Residence / meal plan fees
    -   Student’s full name
    -   Student number
3.  Mail your cheque to:

SHCS MAIN OFFICE  
MARINE DRIVE BUILDING 6  
2205 LOWER MALL  
VANCOUVER BC  V6T 1Z4

***If funding was sent to the UBC Sponsorship Billing Office in error, please email [information@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:information@housing.ubc.ca)\.*** 

## Information privacy

By entering into a sponsorship agreement, students agree to allow UBC to share limited information from their student housing account with you for the duration of the sponsorship\.

Information that can be shared includes:

-   student name and student number
-   residence area and room type
-   room fees

Any further student information, including exact address, cannot be shared with a sponsor unless the student has authorized you as a third\-party\.

### Student academic information

If your sponsorship conditions include receiving updates on the student’s academic progress, transcripts or other documents, ask the student to send these directly to you\. UBC cannot provide this information to sponsors\.

## Questions?

If you have any questions, please [contact us](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.

title: Information for sponsored students
content_markdown:
[Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/49173404418_7f176df178_o.gif)

**Some UBC students have a portion of their housing and meal plan fees paid by a sponsor, such as an Indigenous community, employer or government agency\. If you have a sponsor, this page explains what to expect and your responsibilities\.**

## On this page

-   [How sponsorship billing works](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/information-for-sponsored-students/#sponsorship)
-   [Your responsibilities](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/information-for-sponsored-students/#responsibilities)
-   [Information privacy](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/information-for-sponsored-students/#information-privacy)

## How sponsorship billing works

Student Housing will invoice your sponsor for the housing and meal plan fees they agree to cover, up to the coverage limit they specified\.

Your sponsor\(s\) will receive an invoice after each term’s course change date that includes:

-   Your name and student number
-   Residence area and room type
-   Room fees for the sponsorship period

**Invoice delivery times**

-   Winter Session Term 1: mid\-August
-   Winter Session Term 2: mid\-November

UBC sponsorship for tuition fees

If your sponsor plans to support you with tuition or other student\-related fees, they’ll need to apply separately through the [Sponsorship Billing office](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsors/) by their deadline\.

## Your responsibilities

### Confirm your sponsorship

You must complete the [Sponsor Student Declaration](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_80lLxNhTIl76Fsa) to acknowledge that you’re entering into a sponsorship and understand your responsibilities\. Complete this as soon as possible after your sponsor applies\.

### Understand your sponsorship agreement

Connect with your sponsor to understand the terms and length of your sponsorship agreement\. Student Housing cannot co\-ordinate this on your behalf\.

You’re responsible for informing your sponsor of any changes to your situation that may affect your sponsorship level\.

If you’re unsure about the terms or coverage limits of your sponsorship, contact Student Housing\.

### Pay fees not covered by your sponsor

You must pay any housing fees not covered by your sponsor by the deadline in your housing offer\.

Please refer to your housing contract for penalties for unpaid fees\. Contact Student Housing if you’re unsure about fees you owe\.

## Information privacy

Your student records at UBC are protected under BC’s Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act \(FIPPA\), which means that the information you provide to UBC and information UBC has on file about your academic progress, conduct and wellbeing, and student housing information is not available to anybody other than you\.

By entering into a sponsorship agreement, you’re agreeing to allow UBC to share limited information from your student housing account with your sponsor for the duration of the sponsorship\.

Information that can be shared includes:

-   Your student name and student number
-   Residence area and room type
-   Room fees

Further information, including your exact address, cannot be shared unless you’ve authorized your sponsor as a third\-party\.  

## Questions?

If you have questions about your sponsorship status, please [contact us](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.

title: Food Delivery to Residence
content_markdown:
**Ordering food delivery to residence? Follow these tips to ensure your order arrives smoothly and to help reduce waste and wildlife visits\.**

## Tips for smoother deliveries

-   **Provide accurate location and delivery instructions:** Include your building name, commonsblock location and any helpful landmarks when placing your order—to help your driver navigate campus more easily and get you your food quickly\.
-   **Always meet your driver:** You must always meet your driver \(either at your building or commonsblock\) and pick up your food delivery immediately—to avoid attracting wildlife and pests, spoiled and wasted food, strong odours or messy spills\.
-   **If you have an ongoing grocery or meal subscription:** Pick up deliveries promptly and remember to pause your subscription when you’re away\.

## Why prompt pickups matter

**When food is delivered to the wrong location or left uncollected, it creates problems for everyone:**

-   Mess and unpleasant odours
-   Food waste
-   Wildlife and pests \(raccoons and seagulls love abandoned orders\)
-   Frustrated residents and delivery drivers

## Sustainability and climate

**Food delivery services are convenient but come with environmental costs:** 

-   Significant packaging waste
-   Carbon emissions, especially from off\-campus restaurants
-   Single\-use plastics and containers

Reduce your delivery orders to support UBC Student Housing’s sustainability and climate action goals\. Learn more about what you can do to [Live Green](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/) in residence\.

### Ways to reduce your impact

-   Plan ahead and stock your kitchen—keep easy meals and late\-night snacks on hand so you’re not tempted to order delivery
-   Shop for groceries on campus—try the [Food Hub Market](https://foodhub.ubc.ca/market/), [Gage Market](https://food.ubc.ca/places/gage-market/) or other on\-campus stores
-   Order less frequently and combine orders with roommates when you do
-   Choose restaurants closer to campus
-   Use your residence dining hall or cook in your unit
-   Support restaurants with sustainable packaging

## What we’re doing

We’re working to improve food delivery across all residence areas\.

**Current pilot program:** We’re testing new signage and procedures at Marine Drive and Walter Gage to manage deliveries more effectively, enhance commonsblock delivery areas and help drivers more easily navigate residence complexes\.

**Next steps:** Based on what works, we’ll expand improvements to other residence areas\.

title: Student Housing Experience Survey: Results
content_markdown:
[Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/RA-Training_Summer-2025-scaled.jpg)  

  
**In November 2024 \(Term One\) and March 2025 \(Term Two\), approximately 13,000 UBC residence contract holders were invited to provide feedback on their residence experience in both the Term One and Term Two [Student Housing Experience Survey](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/student-housing-experience-survey/) \(SHES\)\.**

Over 4,800 residents from Winter Session, Year Round and Student Family housing completed at least one of the two surveys\.

Thank you to everyone who gave feedback on their residence experience\. Your feedback is invaluable and helps shape the future of Student Housing at UBC—providing us with important insights that help us understand what we’re doing well and what areas we need to prioritize to enhance the residence experience and best serve students living in Student Housing\.

## On this page:

-   -   [Survey highlights](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/student-housing-experience-survey/results/#highlights)
    -   [Priority opportunities for improvement](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/student-housing-experience-survey/results/#improvement)
    -   [Learn more](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/student-housing-experience-survey/results/#learn)

## Survey highlights

According to survey feedback, Student Housing excels in and will continue to prioritize these aspects of residence life\.

### Creating a sense of connection and belonging in residence

Nine out of ten respondents \(88 per cent\) shared they feel connected to UBC as a result of living in residence and 94 per cent felt comforted knowing they get to return “home” to their residence at the end of the day\.

### Providing a greater awareness of diversity

Three out of four respondents \(76 per cent\) shared that living in residence helped them become more aware of identities different from their own\.

### Educating residents on sustainable food choices in residence

Two out of three respondents \(64 per cent\) with an All Access Dining or Swipe meal plan shared that dining in residence encouraged them to eat less red meat, try more plant\-based foods or learn about the sustainability value of plant\-based options\. This aligns with UBC’s goals to promote healthy, sustainable living in residence and [UBC’s Climate Action Plan 2030](https://planning.ubc.ca/cap2030)\.

We will continue to monitor the success of these initiatives and continue prioritizing these aspects of the residence experience in 2026 and beyond\.

## Priority opportunities for improvement

While we continue to make improvements to all aspects of the residence experience, based on the insights gathered from the two 2024/25 SHES surveys, we have identified the following areas as priorities for the upcoming year\.  

### Improving the Student Housing website

**Finding:** On average, one out of two residents \(43 to 66 per cent\) surveyed found that the Student Housing website was easy to navigate and were able to find the information they were looking for\.

**What we’re doing:** Already identified as a priority, in 2025 we redesigned the home page to help visitors more easily navigate the site and access relevant information\. Plus, we’re currently developing a new website with improved information architecture, navigation and features, which is planned for launch in late 2026\. The website’s navigation and layout were developed using insights from usage analytics, survey data \(from over 1,000 current and former residents\) and numerous focus groups with students and staff\.  

### Reducing the amount of waste that’s incorrectly sorted

**Finding:** Three out of four residents \(74 per cent\) reported that they always sort their waste properly in residence\. Despite those efforts, residence sorting stations still exhibit significant waste contamination rates \(i\.e\., waste materials placed in the incorrect bins\.\)

**What we’re doing:** In addition to our ongoing efforts to educate residents on how to correctly sort their waste, in summer 2025 we collaborated with [UBC Sustainability](https://sustain.ubc.ca/) to introduce a waste sorting pilot program at Marine Drive residence and study a set of waste sorting interventions to see which best reduced contamination rates and prevented the most waste from ending up in the landfill\. The results from this pilot were used to develop a food scraps pickup program at Marine Drive, which launched in September 2025 and, based on results, may be expanded to other suite\-style residence areas\.

We will continue to collaborate with UBC Sustainability to explore, study and implement novel systems to help reach UBC’s [zero waste goals](https://sustain.ubc.ca/campus/recycling-waste) and contribute to UBC’s [Climate Action Plan 2030](https://planning.ubc.ca/cap2030)\.  

### Increase the sense of community in residence and provide the tools and support needed to build productive roommate experiences

**Finding:** Students who reported feeling a poorer sense of community in residence said their experience living with their roommate at that time was the main cause\.

**What we’re doing:** With the launch of a new Student Housing Management System in late 2026, we’ll be able to provide better roommate matches by asking additional application questions related to lifestyle, habits, and preferences and stronger tools for students to connect with potential roommates\.

In addition to the current level of support that Residence Advisors provide to help residents successfully navigate living with roommates, the following strategies are being implemented:

-   -   -   **Enhanced Residence Advisor \(RA\) training:** In August 2025, we updated RA training to emphasize the importance of facilitating communication between roommates and addressing roommate conflict, providing them with the tools to coach residents on addressing conflict, having difficult conversations and establishing boundaries with assertiveness\. This additional training will continue in August 2026 and beyond\.
        -   **Updated guidance for RAs about when to seek support from their Residence Life Manager:** Starting in 2025, RAs received updated guidance about when to seek support from their Residence Life Manager, to help provide mediation for and resolve roommate\-related sooner\.
        -   **Providing additional content, resource handouts and a roommate survey to educate residents on positive roommate dynamics:** These materials were provided to first\-year residents in August 2025 in a roommate social event that took place during Weekend of Welcome\. These resources will be offered again in August 2026\.

### Provide enhanced resources for gender diverse residents throughout the housing application and assignment process

**Finding:** Respondents who identify as transgender or gender diverse have reported having a less positive experience in residence, including in navigating their housing application and assignment\.

**What we’re doing:** While we continuously seek opportunities to elevate the residence experience for transgender / gender diverse students, from a clear application and room assignment process to a welcoming and inclusive experience living in residence, in 2025 we launched the [Gender Diverse Students guide](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/prospective/gender-diverse/) and updated our content related to gender and room assignments for all prospective residents\.

In 2026, we look forward to providing even more education, as part of our new to residence orientation campaign for incoming first\-year residents, on gender diversity at UBC to help ensure an inclusive and welcoming residence and campus environment\.

### Educating residents on career development opportunities

**Finding:** Two out of five residents \(45 per cent\) surveyed said they were not aware of opportunities in residence to build their interview skills or learn professional \(i\.e\., workplace\) etiquette\.

**What we’re doing:** In 2026, we are partnering with the UBC Career Centre to bring new career development workshops to residence, which will provide unique residence programming and help connect residents with the services provided directly by the Career Centre\.

## Learn more

Learn more about the [Student Housing Experience Survey](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/student-housing-experience-survey/) and check the email associated with your Workday Student account at the end of January 2026 for your personalized term two survey link\.

title: Acadia Park Highrise Sprinkler System Replacement
content_markdown:
[Acadia Park Highrise](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Acadia-Park-Highrise.jpg)

To maintain, improve and expand our campus facilities to continue to provide a strong student experience, construction, renovation and repair work at UBC is an everyday activity\.

The sprinkler system in the Acadia Park Highrise \(built in 1967\) is fully functional but is reaching the end of its serviceable life\. From May to August 2026, we will be replacing the system throughout the building, in units and common areas\.

The building remains safe for every resident, and this project is a proactive and required step to ensure the continued safety of residents and modernize the system\.

To move forward effectively, the project requires the staged relocation of Highrise residents, either to other units at Acadia Park or to lower floors in the Highrise, as work proceeds in stages up the building\. We sincerely appreciate the patience, understanding, cooperation and feedback from the Highrise community, which we acknowledge is significantly affected\.

## Project overview

### Map

[Embedded iframe \(view source\)](https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12!1m3!1d1727.1146006003962!2d-123.23736481861819!3d49.2623184359112!2m3!1f0!2f0!3f0!3m2!1i1024!2i768!4f13.1!3m3!1m2!1s0x548672c5dc232ce7%3A0x4ee56df481d1dbda!2sAcadia%20Park%20Highrise%2C%202725%20Melfa%20Rd%2C%20Vancouver%2C%20BC%20V6T%201N4!5e1!3m2!1sen!2sca!4v1772057668459!5m2!1sen!2sca)

### Summer 2026 timeline

**May 2026:** Repairs completed on Floors 1–3\.

**June 2026:** Repairs completed on the remaining floors in the building, with work progressing in stages, starting with Floor 4 and ending on the Penthouse level \(Floor 15\)\.

**Late August 2026:** Primary repairs are expected to be complete\.

### Daily work schedule

**Construction typically occurs during UBC’s standard approved hours of work: Monday–Friday, 7:30 am–7 pm, and Saturday, 9 am–5 pm\.**

**Some workers will arrive on\-site before the construction start time to begin getting ready for their day\.**

Construction hours may be extended \(e\.g\., earlier start time; extended to Sundays\) to ensure the project is completed on time\.

### Daily noise and disruptions

During approved hours of work:

-   Highrise residents should expect to hear noise, primarily from the operation of handheld construction tools and equipment\.
-   One of the two elevators will be reserved for the use of construction personnel\.
-   Highrise residents may notice some dust related to construction work in the ground level lobby and the elevator used by construction personnel\.
-   We anticipate some limited impacts related to this project for the wider Acadia Park community, including some construction\-related noise and work vehicles near the Highrise and commonsblock\.

As you are likely aware, construction at UBC is an everyday activity, and safe, prudent construction practices are always followed\. Nevertheless, while UBC can reduce the impact to residents and the campus community, it cannot be avoided altogether\.

### Questions?

**Why do residents need to relocate?**

We have planned the project in such a way that the building can remain occupied, completing the work in sequence by floor, with each floor impacted for approximately three weeks while out of use\. The nature of the work involved in each unit is comprehensive, requiring our contractor to:

-   Cut out and remove sections of ceiling drywall\.
-   Cut apart and remove copper sprinkler system pipes, which contain water\.
-   Reinstall and activate the new sprinkler system\.
-   Replace the ceiling drywall\.
-   Patch, paint and restore the unit to a livable condition\.

This work is expected to produce significant dust and mess and requires ease of movement throughout the workspace to be completed efficiently\.

To ensure that we are not risking damage to residents’ personal belongings and that the work proceeds according to a set schedule—which provides predictability for all residents in the building—it is unfortunately not feasible for residents to leave any belongings in their current units and relocate temporarily \(except for Penthouse level residents, where the work will be less invasive\)\.

Moving residents permanently to a new unit also means they only have to move once\.

**What should I expect on my weekend relocation dates?**

While we are still working out the details, we anticipate that you will have from Saturday morning to Sunday afternoon on your relocation weekend to complete your move, moving all your furniture and belongings and fully vacating your current unit\.

We will have staff on hand to coordinate elevator use so moves can be completed in an orderly way\. Packing boxes and moving carts will also be available to support residents with the move\. Additional details about the move will be provided throughout the project\.

**What if I am not able to move on the dates scheduled for my floor?**

We recognize that some Highrise residents will be away for parts of the summer while these moves are taking place\. If you will be away or unavailable to move on the dates scheduled for your floor, please email [family@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:family@housing.ubc.ca) to let us know as soon as possible, so we can work with you to find a solution that works for your individual circumstances

**If I don’t like the unit I am moved to, can I move out without penalty?**

While typically residents are required to provide one month’s notice to cancel their contract, under these circumstances we can permit short notice cancellations for Acadia Park Highrise residents impacted by this project, to allow you to move out of Acadia Park without penalty\.

**Are you offering a discount for Highrise residents?**

Construction at UBC, including renovations and repairs, is an everyday occurrence that we should all be prepared for—and that the UBC community will ultimately benefit from\. Residents who are required to relocate will receive a one time credit to help offset any costs associated with moving; the specific details were communicated to residents directly\.

**How noisy will *my* unit be during work hours?**

While noise from the replacement work will be kept within reasonable limits, every person responds to noise and disruption differently\. With that in mind, we cannot anticipate how noisy your particular room will be or how the noise will affect you\.

**Will any units not be affected?**

Any resident of the Acadia Park Highrise might experience some noise in their unit or another part of their residence area\.

**Are there any safety concerns?**

-   **Construction work:** Safe, prudent construction practices are always followed, and residents who will be living in the Acadia Park Highrise while repairs are taking place are asked to observe any and all signage and guidance\.
-   **Building and sprinkler system:** The sprinkler system in the Acadia Park Highrise \(built in 1967\) is fully functional but is reaching the end of its serviceable life\. The building remains safe for every resident, and this project is a proactive and required step to ensure the continued safety of residents and modernize the system\.

**Is there any risk of flooding during the work?**

The risk of flooding during the work is minimal\. The current sprinkler system is controlled by zones and the relevant zones will be turned off during the work\. We also have rapid response procedures in place to quickly shut water off in the unlikely event an incident occurs\.

**What if damage to residents' belonging happens during the project?**

Given residents will be moving out of units ahead of work taking place, it is unlikely that damage would occur\. Should that happen, it will be addressed through our standard incident/claims process\.

#### Additional questions?

If you are are a Highrise resident, and your question isn’t answered above, please refer to the latest project emails/updates from Student Housing \(sent from [family@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:family@housing.ubc.ca)\), where we have communicated more detailed and specific information\.

If you have any remaining questions, please email us at [family@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:family@housing.ubc.ca)\.

title: Services & Amenities
content_markdown:
There are so many perks to campus living\!

All UBC residents have access to a variety of campus resources that support intellectual growth, healthy lifestyles, and personal safety\. Life at UBC is truly a home\-away\-from\-home where residents can pursue their academic and personal goals in a safe, comfortable, and fun environment\.

### Stay Connected

[Stay connected](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/02/icon_facilities_internet.png)

[ResNet](http://it.ubc.ca/services/email-voice-internet/resnet) connects our residences to the internet and campus network\. Depending on what residence area you are in, ResNet is delivered through either a hardwired port or wireless connection\.

### Easy Eating

[Meal Plan](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_mealplan.png)

At UBC, it’s easy to enjoy delicious, high\-quality foods every day\. Students who live in Orchard Commons, Place Vanier, and Totem Park purchase a required [Residence Meal Plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/residence-meal-plan-all-access-dining/ "Totem & Vanier")\. Students who are offered accommodation in other residences will have a kitchen, but can also enjoy added convenience and savings with a [UBCcard Value Plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/ubccard-value-plan/)\. Learn more about [food at UBC](https://food.ubc.ca/)\.

### Sustainability and climate action

[icon\_facilities\_SortingStation1](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/SortingStation1.png)

Learn about [sustainability features in residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/), from low\-flow water fixtures and LED lighting to building automation, that help increase building performance, reduce energy use, manage water consumption and ultimately reduce our greenhouse gas emissions\. Plus, visit [Live Green: Climate Action for Student Residents](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/) to discover all the ways we’re helping UBC achieve its sustainability and climate action goals—and what you can do to help\.

### Safety and Security

[icon\_facilities\_lock](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/icon_facilities_lock.png)

We work together with the campus community, including our residents, to help make UBC Vancouver a safer campus\. Find out about residence safety strategies, ways to stay safe on campus after dark, emergency contacts, additional safety services and lots more—including substance use information and access to emergency naloxone\. [Learn more](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/safety-security/)\.

### Your Health

[icon\_facilities\_health](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_health.png)

Live well to learn well\. Check out the range of health and wellness services and resources residents have access to, in residence and across UBC\. [Learn more](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/health-wellness/)\.

### Residence Life

[icon\_facilities\_outdoor](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_outdoor.png)

At UBC, there’s always [something to do](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life) and ways to [meet people](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved)\. All residences have fitness facilities and games rooms, and are surrounded by vast outdoor spaces for intramural sports, hiking, or beachcombing\. There are also many opportunities to [get involved](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/ "Get Involved") in the residence community, like joining a committee or [becoming a Residence Advisor](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/jobs/ "Jobs")\. UBC is also well known for world\-class athletics, museums, gardens, theatre, and guest speakers\. [UBC Recreation](http://www.recreation.ubc.ca/) runs programs throughout the year\.

### Front Desk

[Front Desk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_frontdesk.png)

Open from 7 am to 11 pm, seven days a week, this is the place to ask a question, pick up mail, rent game and sports equipment and more\. [Meet the team](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/meet-the-team/)\.

### Overnight Mobile Team

[Front Desk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_frontdesk.png)

Operating from 11 pm to 7 am, seven days a week, the Overnight Mobile Team is here to help with certain urgent, but non\-emergency, situations overnight\. For example, if you get locked out of your building or room, they’re the team to call\. [Meet the team](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/meet-the-team/)\.

### Laundry Facilities

[icon\_facilities\_laundry](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_laundry.png)

How convenient\! Each residence has [laundry machines](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/laundry-facilities/) that are operated on a card system—no need to collect coins\.

### Maintenance Services

[icon\_facilities\_wrench](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/icon_facilities_wrench.png)

Getting something fixed is easy\. Residents can use the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/) to request maintenance or repairs in their suite\.

### Transportation and Parking

[Parking & Bike Storage](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_parking.png)

UBC is a very walkable campus—flat and pedestrian\-friendly, with everything inside a 15–20\-minute walk and much of campus a car\-free zone\. So you don’t need to bring a bike or vehicle to get around\. [Learn more](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#bikes-vehicles) about all your transportation options for getting around or going off campus, including walking, bike share, car share and public transit—plus, if you do bring a bike, how to keep it safe and, if you do bring a vehicle, how to apply for parking\.

## Student Housing account \(New\)

### Who logs in

[https://starrezportal\.vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/](https://starrezportal.vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/)[Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/your-account/)Log in

Learn more about the [transition to the new system](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/your-account/#transition)\.

## Transition to the new system

Starting in spring 2026, we’re transitioning to a new student housing management system using StarRez, a leading residence platform adopted widely in Canada and across North America\.

This change is part of a broad effort to modernize our systems and improve the online experience for UBC students\.

The system you [log in](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/your-account/#top) to depends on the type of housing you applied for or where you live\.

### Phases

The current plan for transitioning to the new system\. Schedule subject to change\. Precise transition dates will be provided to residents via email\.

-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/your-account/)**Spring 2026:** Student Family \(Acadia Park\) application opens in the new system\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/your-account/)**Summer 2026:** Student Family \(Acadia Park\) accounts move to the new system\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/your-account/)**By fall 2026:** Year\-round accounts move to the new system; Year\-Round application opens in the new system\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/your-account/)**Fall 2026:** Winter Session application \(2027/28\) opens in the new system\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/your-account/)**Winter 2027:** Summer Session residence application \(for 2027 Summer Session\) opens in the new system\.
-   [Embedded svg \(view source\)](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/your-account/)**Summer 2027:** Full transition to the new system\. Summer Session \(2027\) and Winter Session \(2027/28\) residents—who applied in the new system—continue to manage their accounts in the new system\.

### Your information

Your student housing history and records are safe\. StarRez is an encrypted platform that meets top information security standards\. This transition won’t affect your existing contracts or applications\.

## Questions?

If you have questions about which system to use, [check above](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/your-account/#top) or in any recent communication from UBC Student Housing to confirm\.

If you have questions about the transition to the new system or need support, please [contact us](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.

title: Food scraps pickup program
content_markdown:
We’re introducing a twice\-weekly food scraps pickup program in select residences to help make waste sorting more convenient\.  

### How the program works

-   -   1.  Pick up free compostable bags from your building waste room 
        2.  Line your compost pail using only the provided compostable bags \(no plastic\) 
        3.  Compost your food scraps  
        4.  Tie the bag and place your pail outside your unit before your residence pick up time 

After pick up, service staff will empty your food scraps and replace your compostable liner for continued use\. 

### Residence food scraps pickup schedule

  

  

#### Brock Commons

-   Tuesdays by 10 am
-   Fridays by 10 am

**Iona House** 

-   Tuesdays by 10 am
-   Fridays by 10 am

#### Marine Drive

Buildings 1 and 5

-   Tuesdays by 10 am
-   Fridays by 10 am

Buildings 2, 4 and 6

-   Mondays by 10 am
-   Thursdays by 10 am

**Walter Gage**

-   Mondays by 10 am
-   Thursdays by 10 am

**Exchange**

-   Tuesdays by 10 am
-   Fridays by 10 am

#### Ponderosa Commons

Arbutus and Maple: 

-   Mondays by 10 am
-   Thursdays by 10 am

Cedar, Oak, Spruce: 

-   Tuesdays by 10 am
-   Fridays by 10 am

#### tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ

-   Mondays by 10 am
-   Thursdays by 10 am

### **What can I put in the food scraps pail?**

It’s surprising how much you can put in the food scraps pail, from cooked food to uncoated, wooden chopsticks\.

Find out all the items you can put in the food scraps pail \(and how to sort other waste at UBC\):

-   [Sort\-it\-out guide](https://sustain.ubc.ca/sites/sustain.ubc.ca/files/images/campusInitiatives/11x17-SortitOut-Guide-textonly.pdf): check out the poster
-   [Waste Sorting Recyclepedia](https://sustain.ubc.ca/resources/campus-guides/sort-it-out/z-recyclepedia-search): search any item and find out where it goes\.
-   [Sort it Out game](https://sorting-game.herokuapp.com/): a fun game to help you figure out how to sort waste at UBC\.

### Why are we doing this

Food scraps make up more than 50% of the waste produced in student resident buildings\. By composting food scraps properly, we can:

-   -   -   Reduce landfill waste
        -   Lower greenhouse gas emissions
        -   Improve recycling and waste sorting overall
        -   Help make residence communities cleaner and more sustainably

But most importantly, we want to make composting easier for students\!

### Learn more

To learn more about the food scraps pickup program, email [residence\.events@ubc\.ca](mailto:residence.events@ubc.ca)\. If you have questions about the food scraps pickup program in your residence, contact your [Building Services manager](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/unit-inspections/)\.

Learn more about sustainability and climate action in residence and how you can help achieve UBC’s goals by visiting [Live Green: Climate Action for Student Residents](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/)\.

title: Health & Safety
content_markdown:
[Campus security at UBC](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/campus-security-ubc.jpg)

**Stay safe\. Take care of yourself\. And be prepared\.**

UBC is a safe place to live where students have convenient access to safety services and resources that support physical and mental wellbeing\. Student Housing, along with UBC at large, has committed significant resources to providing a safe living and learning environment\. But we can’t do it alone—your partnership and vigilance is critical\. Being prepared and educated is the best strategy\.

## Safety and Security

Find out about residence safety strategies, staying safe on campus after dark, emergency contacts, additional safety services and lots more—including substance use information and access to naloxone\.

[Learn more](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/safety-security/)

## Health and wellness

Discover health and wellness services, resources and tips, in residence and across UBC—from health insurance and counsellor in residence to flu shots and substance use\.

[Learn more](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/health-wellness/)

## Emergency preparedness

Are you ready for an emergency? Find out how to prepare for and respond to an emergency, such as an earthquake, fire, severe weather, leak or flood, and more\.

[Learn more](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/emergency-preparedness/)

title: Essential Application Facts
content_markdown:
### All Applicants

-   $50 non\-refundable application fee required\.
-   All residence offers are sent by email and include an expiry date to respond and pay a deposit\.
-   Separate residence applications required for UBC Vancouver and UBC Okanagan\.
-   Submitting an application does not guarantee an offer will be made\.
-   Prospective undergraduates can submit a residence application after applying to UBC\.

### Year Round Residence—May to April

[Brock Commons](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/brock-commons/) \| [Exchange](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/exchange/) \| [Fraser Hall](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/fraser-hall/ "Fraser Hall") \| [Iona House](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/iona-house/) \| [Marine Drive](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/marine-drive-residence/ "Marine Drive") \| [Ponderosa Commons](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/ponderosa-commons/ "Ponderosa Commons") \| [tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/houses-of-ones-belonging-to-saltwater/ "tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ") \| [Thunderbird](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/thunderbird/ "Thunderbird")

-   For returning/mature students and graduate students\.
-   Applications accepted any time\.
-   Students prepared to begin occupancy at the start of May are best positioned to receive an offer\.
-   [Applications to sublet](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/subletting/ "Waitlists & Sublets") accepted during the summer months\.

### Winter Session Residence—September to April

[Fairview Crescent](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/fairview-crescent/ "Fairview Crescent") \| [Orchard Commons](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/orchard-commons/) \| [Place Vanier](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/place-vanier/ "Place Vanier") \| [Ritsumeikan\-UBC House](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/ritsumaiken-ubc-house/ "Ritsumeiken-UBC House") \| [Totem Park](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/totem-park/ "Totem Park") \| [Walter Gage](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/walter-gage/ "Walter Gage")

-   Mainly for new students who qualify for a [guaranteed room in residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/first-year-guarantee/ "Who Gets Priority")\.
-   Prospective UBC students can submit a residence application after applying to UBC\. Apply online with Student Housing and Community Services by May 1\.
-   A very limited number of [spaces are available for returning students](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/returning/ "Returning Students")\. Application deadline: February 1\.

### Year Round Graduate Colleges—September to August

[Green College](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences-rooms/graduate-colleges/ "Graduate Colleges") \| [St\. John’s College](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences-rooms/graduate-colleges/)

-   College membership required\.

### Year Round Student Family Residence—ongoing

[Acadia Park](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/acadia-park/ "Acadia Park")

-   [Applications](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-to-apply/application-forms/ "Application Forms") accepted any time and can be submitted before applying to and being accepted by UBC\. We recommend applying early\. \(Offers are based on application date and availability at the desired occupancy date\.\)
-   Additional documents will be required—birth certificates, passports, visas, etc\.
-   [Eligibility factors](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/ "Eligibility") determine how applicants are chosen from the waitlist\.

### Summer Residence—May to August

[Fairview Crescent](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/fairview-crescent/ "Fairview Crescent")

-   For UBC students and Stay Through students studying or staying on\-campus until August and [eligible](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/ "Eligibility") visiting research students\.

### Early Arrival

Early arrivals are not typically permitted\. [Eligible](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/ "Eligibility") students must apply by the [required deadline](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/important-dates/ "Dates & Deadlines")\.

-   There is an [early arrival fee](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/fees-payments/early-arrival/ "UBC Early Arrival Fees")\.
-   May be required to move to different accommodation on short notice \(less than 24 hours\)\.

title: Living With Roommates
content_markdown:
[Roommates](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/Roommates.jpg)

> “You will make new friendships that last a lifetime and have plenty of support for those tough assignments and exams\.” – Marine Drive resident

## Tips for living with roommates

Code of living

Download the [Roommate Agreement Form](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Roommate-Agreement-Form.pdf) and [Unit Cleaning Schedule](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Unit-Cleaning-Schedule.pdf) to help you and your roommates discuss shared living expectations\.

### Getting Acquainted

First encounters can sometimes be a bit awkward and first impressions deceiving\. Try easing into the initial conversation with new roommates by using simple conversation starters, then exchange more detailed information when you feel comfortable around each other\.

#### Begin with easy questions

-   Where do you call home?
-   What’s your major?
-   Why did you choose UBC?
-   What are your favourite things to do?

#### Set basic expectations

-   How should the unit common space be used?
-   How loud is too loud?
-   How do we feel about parties or gatherings in the room/unit?
-   How we will keep our unit safe and secure?

#### Plan activities together

-   Have lunch, take a walk, or attend a residence program together\.
-   1st year residents: Attend Roommate Bootcamp together during the Week of Welcome\.
-   Upper year residents in suite\-style communities: Arrange a unit visit with your Residence Advisor\.

#### Discuss sleep and study habits

-   Are you a morning or night person?
-   Are you a heavy or light sleeper?
-   Will you be studying in our unit or elsewhere?
-   Can you study with music on or with guests in our unit?

#### Talk about alcohol

-   Do you drink alcohol?
-   How would you describe your drinking habits?
-   Do you think it’s okay to drink alcohol in our unit?

#### Discuss safety & security

-   Talk about always locking the door when you leave your unit and when you’re sleeping\. Ensure your roommate\(s\) know to always take their keys\.
-   What is the policy for letting guests into your unit?
-   How will you communicate if you’re uncomfortable with a particular guest in your unit?
-   Always check in with each other, especially if you haven’t seen one another recently\.
-   Let each other know when you’re going to be away, when you’re planning to return, and what to do if you don’t see one another for a while\.

#### Guests and sharing

-   How do you feel about overnight guests?
-   Is there a time that guests of other genders cannot be in our room?
-   Can guests of other genders use our washroom?
-   Are there times when you’d prefer not to have guests?
-   Do you prefer to be asked before someone borrows something?
-   What items are going to be shared?

#### Discuss cleaning responsibilities

-   How do you prefer to arrange our unit?
-   How do we define a clean unit?
-   How do we rotate cleaning and household chores?
-   Who is responsible for buying the toilet paper and cleaning supplies?

### Conflicts

Sometimes there’s conflict between roommates, typically due to noise levels, unwanted guests and cleaning responsibilities\. If you’re having trouble, speak to your roommate\(s\) about the issue before getting other people involved\. It’s always best when roommates take a direct and tactful approach to conflict resolution before asking a Residence Advisor for help\.

#### Cleaning

-   Divide the work and take turns\.
-   Set a cleaning schedule and clear expectations \(what happens when someone fails to do their part\)\.
-   Hire someone to clean, then split the bill\.
-   Decide how household items \(cleaning supplies, toilet paper, dish soap, etc\.\) will be purchased\.
-   Create a schedule for composting, recycling, and waste removal and assign roles to tackle each\.

#### Daytime noise

Some daytime noise is reasonable, however:

-   Set limits on reasonable volume from TV, music, Skype calls, video games, etc\.
-   Choose to go to a residence study room or library to study\.

#### Evening noise

-   Set limits on reasonable volume from TV, music, Skype calls, video games, etc\.
-   Consult with your roommate\(s\) before inviting guests over\.
-   Decide on computer cut\-off times in a shared room\.
-   Use headphones or earplugs to reduce noise\.

Residence quiet hours

Quiet hours for all residence areas:

-   **Sunday–Thursday:** 10 pm–7 am
-   **Friday & Saturday:** 1 am–7 am

#### Guests

-   Only on weekends?
-   Only on weeknights, before 10 pm?
-   Only during the daytime?

## Living in Acadia Park

Student families live in Acadia Park, which also offers accommodation for eligible couples that include at least one UBC student\. This residence is child\-friendly and promotes healthy families through community activities, support programs, and nearby amenities, such as schools, shopping and green spaces\. Nearby [child care](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/child-care-school-registration/) is also available, but apply as soon as possible, since waitlists can be lengthy\.

## Quick Facts

-   Year Round Student Family Residence
-   Unfurnished suites with [non\-standard floor plans](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/acadia-park-sample-floor-plans/ "Acadia Park Sample Floor Plans")
-   42 four\-bedrooms, 35 three\-bedrooms, 288 two\-bedrooms, 257 one\-bedrooms, 4 studios
-   [Resources](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/acadia-park-resources/)
-   [Get involved](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/get-involved-acadia-park/)
-   [Moving in and out of Acadia Park](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-acadia-park/)
-   Telephone and [internet](https://it.ubc.ca/services/email-voice-internet/resnet) available from the provider of your choice
-   [Eligibility requirements](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/ "Eligibility")
-   [Fees](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/fees-payments/acadia-park/)
-   Non\-smoking; [pet policy](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/acadia-park-pet-policy/ "Acadia Park Pet Policy")
-   [Residence sustainability features](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/)

**Acadia Park Front Desk**  

2707 Tennis Crescent  
Vancouver, B\.C\. V6T 2C1  
Tel: 604 822 3172

[family@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:family@housing.ubc.ca)

-   [Acadia Park Residence Map](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/Map_Acadia_3.png)

# Rooms at Acadia Park

Acadia Park suites are various sizes and come with [non\-standard floor plans](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/acadia-park-sample-floor-plans/ "Acadia Park Sample Floor Plans")—from split\-level townhouses to high\-rise condos\. Part of the Acadia Park charm is that each suite is unique\.

-   [icon\-one\-bedroom\-suite](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon-one-bedroom-suite.png)  
    
    # One Bedroom
    
    One bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, living area and eating area\. Some suites also have a den\.
    
-   [icon\-two\-bedroom\-suite](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/02/icon-two-bedroom-suite.png)  
    
    # Two Bedroom
    
    Two bedrooms, bathroom, kitchen, living area and eating area\. Some suites have an additional bathroom\.
    
-   [icon\-three\-bedroom\-suite](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/02/icon-three-bedroom-suite.png)  
    
    # Three Bedroom
    
    Three bedrooms, two bathrooms, kitchen, living area and eating area\.
    
-   [icon\-four\-bedroom\-suite](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon-four-bedroom-suite.png)  
    
    # Four Bedroom
    
    Four bedrooms, two bathrooms, kitchen, living area and eating area\.

# Facilities at Acadia Park

-   [icon\_facilities\_frontdesk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_commonsblock.png)  
    
    ## Commonsblock
    
    The hub for activities, programs and services designed to support education, family life and recreation\. There’s a fitness room, fireside lounge, and activity centre\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_outdoor](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_outdoor.png)  
    
    ## Activities
    
    Acadia Park residents get exclusive access to activities with a [UTown@UBC Community Services Card](http://utown.ubc.ca/discovering-utownubc/utownubc-community-programs/utownubc-community-services-card/apply-utownubc)\. Residence Life staff also organize a variety of events and programs throughout the year\.
    
-   [sorting station](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/icons_sorting_orange.png)  
    
    ## Sort It Out\!
    
    Sustainability is a shared value in residence\. Acadia Park has a large sorting area with collection bins for household recyclables, e\-waste, charitable donations, and trash\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_laundry](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_laundry.png)  
    
    ## Laundry Facilities
    
    Machines operate on a card system—no need to worry about coins\. Machines are available for suites in townhouses, Sopron House and Point Grey Apartments\.
    

-   [icon\_facilities\_parking](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_parking.png)  
    
    ## Parking & Bicycle Storage
    
    [Parking](https://parking.ubc.ca/) is available for a fee\. Bicycle racks are available\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_frontdesk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_frontdesk.png)  
    
    ## Support Staff
    
    From our Front Desk staff and Overnight Mobile Team to Residence Life professional and student staff, you are never alone\! [Meet the people](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/meet-the-team/) you can contact with questions, concerns or a request for support\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_health](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_health.png)  
    
    ## Health & Safety
    
    Residents have access to a campus medical clinic and safety programs such as SafeWalk\. There are regular nightly patrols of residence properties\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_family](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/02/icon_facilities_family.png)  
    
    ## Family Friendly
    
    Playgrounds for children, family\-centric programs, and a close\-knit community\.
    

## Sustainability Features

UBC has been recognized internationally for its commitment to sustainable living\. All residences have waste sorting areas and residences and modern [sustainability features](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/ "Sustainability Features") designed to reduce waste, energy consumption, and water use\.

## Living in Orchard Commons

Orchard Commons is one of our newest residences\. It's ideal for students who are new to UBC and want space and time for studying, the comforts of home, and a relaxed communal atmosphere ideal for making new friends\. Students always have someone to walk to class with, talk to, or have dinner with, all within a fun and supportive environment\.

The building features stunning architecture and design, a LEED Gold certificate, dining facilities as well as interconnected floor lounges with snack kitchens and wonderful mountain and ocean views\. It is also home to Vantage College\.

## Quick Facts

-   Winter Session \(September to April\)
-   Mainly first\-year undergraduate students
-   Most residents eligible for [First Year Guarantee](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/first-year-guarantee/ "First Year Guarantee")[http://www\.food\.ubc\.ca/campus\-plans/residence\-meal\-plan](http://www.food.ubc.ca/campus-plans/residence-meal-plan)

-   1,035 beds in 2 houses; mixed gender floors
-   Furnished rooms: 971 connected singles, 8 singles with bathrooms, 25 shared rooms with shared private bathrooms, 6 one\-bedrooms
-   Internet access \(Wi\-Fi\) in each room
-   Bike storage hooks in each room
-   [Eligibility requirements](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/ "Eligibility")

# Facilities at Orchard Commons

-   [icon\_facilities\_mealplan](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_mealplan.png)  
    
    ## Meal Plan
    
    Orchard Commons residents don’t have to cook\. The mandatory [All Access Dining Plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/residence-meal-plan-all-access-dining/) is valid at more than 30 campus locations, including Open Kitchen—the on\-site dining hall\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_commonsblock](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_commonsblock.png)  
    
    ## Commonsblock
    
    The hub for many residence activities\. Includes: Wi\-Fi, Dining Room, fitness room, music rooms, group and private study spaces and games lounge
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_frontdesk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_frontdesk.png)  
    
    ## Support Staff
    
    From our Front Desk staff and Overnight Mobile Team to Residence Life professional and student staff, you are never alone\! [Meet the people](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/meet-the-team/) you can contact with questions, concerns or a request for support\.
    
-   [sorting station](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/icons_sorting_orange.png)  
    
    ## Sort It Out\!
    
    Sustainability is a shared value in residence\. Orchard Commons has waste sorting stations with collection bins for household recyclables, e\-waste and charitable donations\. The dining hall has an area to separate and compost food waste\.
    

-   [icon\_facilities\_laundry](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_laundry.png)  
    
    ## Laundry Facilities
    
    Machines operate on a convenient card system—no need to worry about coins\. Facilities are located in each House\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_parking](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_parking.png)  
    
    ## Parking & Bicycle Storage
    
    Monthly [parking](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/parking/) is available for a fee\. A bike hook is provided in your room\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_outdoor](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_outdoor.png)  
    
    ## Outdoor Facilities
    
    Orchard Commons features a large courtyard perfect for lounging or playing sports and it is adjacent to many campus recreation facilities\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_health](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_health.png)  
    
    ## Health & Safety
    
    Residents have access to a full array of services including the campus medical clinic, couselling services, and personal safety programs\.
    

## Sustainability Features

UBC has been recognized internationally for its commitment to sustainable living\. Many residences and rooms have modern [sustainability features](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/ "Sustainability Features") designed to reduce waste, energy consumption, and water use\. Read the design & sustainability [case study](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Orchard-Commons-Design-Case-Study.pdf) for Orchard Commons\.

# Orchard Commons Residence LIfe

Living in Orchard Commons was an amazing experience\! It gave me the opportunity to form deep connections and feel a strong sense of belonging—and have great conversations with my housemates\! – Ani Nkiru, Orchard Commons resident

title: Get Involved
content_markdown:
Living on campus means there’s always something to do, opportunities to make friends, and ways to give back to the community that will help you build valuable skills for your future\. Residence Life staff are among the best\-connected people at the university\. They’re committed to enhancing the student experience for all residents\.

Residence Advisors spend countless hours organizing orientation programs, volunteer opportunities, and fun events like recreational sports, movies, field trips, and more\. They also lend an ear when needed and help address community issues\.

Residence Life Managers are professional staff who live and work in each residence area\. They help supervise staff, manage student behaviour, and have extensive knowledge of campus resources\. RLMs are responsible for ensuring each resident has the opportunity enjoy a positive experience living at UBC\.

## Ways to get involved

### Residence\-wide

There are plenty of ways to get involved in programs and initiatives for all residents\.

#### Residence\-wide programs

Free [events, workshops, programs and fitness sessions](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/residence-programs/), plus our [Professor in Residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/professor-in-residence/), [Counsellor in Residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/counsellor-in-residence/), and programs specifically for [grad students](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/grad-student-programs/)\.

#### Student Housing Experience Survey

As part of our strategy to continuously improve the experience of students living in residence, we invite residents to participate in the [Student Housing Experience Survey](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/student-housing-experience-survey/) twice per year\.

#### Sustainability and climate action for student residents

The university has set ambitious targets to cut down our operational greenhouse gas \(GHG\) emissions and reduce the carbon footprint from our entire community\. To reach these goals, we need your help\. Learn more at [Live Green](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/)\.

Plus, find out how to apply for our [Residence Sustainability Enhancement Fund](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/live-green/sustainability-enhancement-fund/)\.

### In your residence community

Meet your Residence Life Manager and find out how to get involved in your residence community—with your residence association, a committee, or other community leadership opportunities, events and initiatives\. Plus, find out how to apply for a position as a Residence Advisor\.

Acadia Park

Acadia Park has one professional staff member and multiple community assistants who work hard to promote a safer, inclusive and enjoyable community for residents\.

[Emma Chartrand](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Emma-Chartrand-960x1200-1-240x300.jpg)

“I’m Emma Chartrand, Residence Life Manager at [Acadia Park](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/acadia-park)\. I have a background in counselling and I’ve been a part of the Acadia Park community since 2012, most recently as a coordinator for the Parents and Tots program\. It’s an honour to serve the UBC community and to enrich the residence experience at UBC\. I look forward to working together to shape our community\. Please come by and say hello\. My door is always open\!”

[emma\.chartrand@ubc\.ca](mailto:emma.chartrand@ubc.ca) \| Tel: 604 822 6389

1\. Acadia Park Residence Association  
Gain valuable skills for your resumé\. Members meet regularly to organize community initiatives\.

2\. Residence Life Leadership  
Community Assistants are student staff \(or student spouses\) who plan fun events, lend an ear when needed and help address community issues\.

3\. Acadia Park Garden Program  
Calling all green thumbs\. We need volunteers to help oversee our cooperative, organic community garden \(coordinators, committee members, etc\.\)\.

4\. Volunteers  
Volunteers help run a variety of family\-centric programs including Parents & Tots and T\-ball\. New program ideas are welcome\.

5\. Attend Events  
Acadia Park residents can apply for a [UTown@UBC Community Services Card](http://utown.ubc.ca/discovering-utownubc/utownubc-community-programs/utownubc-community-services-card/apply-utownubc) for exclusive discounts on UBC attractions and events\.

Student Housing and Community Services operates residences on UBC’s 400 hectare Vancouver campus\. This map is primarily intended to show residence areas and their proximity to main roadways and buildings\.

Visit UBC’s [official map](http://www.maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index.php "Wayfinding at UBC") to find more campus facilities and academic buildings\.

---

## Living at Exchange

Exchange is one of our newest residence communities at UBC\. Home to over 650 students, Exchange offers an active, urban energy and a uniquely connected location\. It is located alongside the UBC bus exchange and just steps from the UBC Aquatic Centre and Student Recreation Centre\. The AMS Nest, UBC Life Building and many other campus amenities are right nearby\.

## Quick Facts

-   Year Round
-   Mainly upper\-year undergraduate and graduate students
-   650 beds: 71 nano suites, 88 studios, 5 large/accessible studios, 77 one\-bedroom suites, 19 two\-bedroom suites, 84 four\-bedroom suites, 15 townhouses \(2\-bedroom\)
-   Furnished living areas and private bedrooms
-   Furnished/appliance\-equipped kitchens\. All units except Nano suites equipped with dishwashers
-   [High\-speed wireless internet](https://it.ubc.ca/services/email-voice-internet/resnet)
-   [Eligibility requirements](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/)
-   [Fees](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/fees-payments/exchange-fees/)
-   [Residence sustainability features](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/)
-   Read a [Sustainability Case Study](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/200616-UBC_Exchange_Sustainabiliy_CaseStudy.pdf) about Exchange residence
