title: Building Community Together
content_markdown:
**How to help create equitable, inclusive communities in residence\.**

Meeting new people and exploring different identities are part of living, working and learning in a diverse university environment\.

Living in residence comes with a responsibility to encourage and support activities and living spaces where all people can thrive socially and academically, no matter what uniquely shapes their identity\.

This principle is important at UBC, which is home to students from over 150 different countries, each with their own identities, life experiences and expressions\.

[Two ethnic friends](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/08/intercultural-understanding.png)

Uttara Kumar, science major, and Payal Shah, psychology major, know first\-hand what it’s like to live in residence in a community of people with diverse identities, backgrounds and customs, which were new to them when they arrived in residence\.

Both from India, they met in the Jump Start orientation program, lived in Place Vanier during their first year of studies and then became roommates in Marine Drive\. They offered to share their experiences and some advice for living and learning on a vibrant, equitable, diverse and inclusive campus\.

**Before you arrived, how did you expect people from different cultures would interact?**

P: When I was doing my research, I read about the diversity at UBC and was a little scared\. I wondered, “What if I offend someone or say something I shouldn’t?” I also worried that people wouldn’t understand my background and that it would be hard for other people to relate to me\.

**How did it feel when you moved in?**

P: It was such a positive experience\. Everyone I met was understanding and interested in getting to know me\. People were very respectful of other’s feelings\.

U: I agree\. A lot of people we met are international students too\. We all have different experiences and perspectives but can relate to each other\. We did the Jump Start program before moving into residence, which helped us get used to our surroundings and all the different people\.

**What challenges did you face with so many diverse people living in the same place?**

P: At first, I was concerned about approaching people\. I wasn’t sure if it was okay to walk up to someone and say hi\. Building relationships works differently here than it does back home\.

U: I was mostly concerned about trying to maintain friendships\. Just because you meet someone, doesn’t mean you’ll see them again because there are so many people here with different interests\. Group friendships didn’t happen quickly, but they did happen\.

**How does UBC create a sense of inclusion among residents?**

P: It’s all about participating in different activities\. In my first year, I was a floor representative at Place Vanier and helped organize many events\. I think the whole purpose is to bring people together from different backgrounds to get to know one another and learn about unique traditions and customs\.

**You’re both from India\. Does that mean you’re the same, culturally?**

P: No\! We have strong differences because we’re from different parts of India\. Our family customs are different and we speak different languages\. Living together, we realized there’s so much diversity even within our own country\.

**Have you learned anything new about other cultures while living in residence?**

U: We have another roommate from France\. It’s fun when she teaches us new words\. She even made us crepes, which we had never tried before, and they were so good\! It was also interesting to learn that people from France don’t speak the same as French Canadians\. We didn’t really know that\.

**You’re both from India\. Does that mean you’re the same, culturally?**

P: No\! We have strong differences because we’re from different parts of India\. Our family customs are different and we speak different languages\. Living together, we realized there’s so much diversity even within our own country\.

**Do you think there could be cultural barriers among roommates?**

P: Sometimes, but very rarely\. I think there could be challenges mostly related to language, food choices and sense of humour\. But we all recognize that people do things differently around the world\. As long as you’re willing to learn, everyone can get along\.

**What’s your best piece of advice when it comes to unique cultural perspectives in residence?**

P: Living in residence might be difficult for people who are set in their ways and not willing to expand their horizons\. It’s always best to be open\-minded and accept people’s differences\.

To learn more, check out UBC’s [Equity and Inclusion Office](https://equity.ubc.ca/)—an important resource for students interested in learning more about UBC’s commitment and policies related to equity, diversity and inclusion, looking to get involved in campus initiatives or seeking support on conflicts or human rights incidents on campus, including discrimination\.

title: How We Assign Rooms
content_markdown:
[how\_we\_assign\_rooms\_770x433](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/10/how-we-assign-rooms-770x433.jpg)

Residence assignments are based on a number of factors, including the application date, your age, [gender identification](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/#gender-identification) and the vacancy type\.

### Winter Session Residence

First year applicants could receive an offer to live at one of our traditional first year residences \(Orchard Commons, Totem Park or Place Vanier\) or a room in a suite\-style residence such as Walter Gage or Ritsumeikan\-UBC House\.

Upper year applicants could receive an offer to live at Fairview Crescent, Ponderosa Commons \(Cedar House\) or Walter Gage\.

1.  Most offers go to First Year students who qualify for a [guaranteed room in Winter Session Residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/first-year-guarantee/ "Who Gets Priority")\. A limited number of spaces are reserved for upper\-year students\.
2.  After accepting an offer, we work behind\-the\-scenes to assign residence areas and rooms based on room type preferences and roommate group requests\. We cannot make guarantees in this process\.
3.  Students who do not receive an offer will be placed on a waitlist and may receive an offer any time during the summer or upcoming academic year\.

### Year Round Residence

Applicants could receive an offer to live at Brock Commons, Exchange, Fraser Hall, Iona House, Marine Drive, Ponderosa Commons \(Arbutus, Maple, Oak and Spruce Houses\), tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ or Thunderbird\. Offers are sent based on:

1.  Application date\.
2.  Earliest occupancy date\. Students prepared to begin occupancy at the start of May are best positioned to receive an offer—contracts typically run from May to April\.
3.  Preferences listed\. Your waitlist numbers will vary depending on the residence area and room type you select, as some residence room types are more popular than others\. Please ensure you only indicate a preference on your application that you are willing to accept an offer for\.  Please keep in mind that we make only **one** offer per application\.

### Student Family Residence

When a vacancy occurs at Acadia Park, an offer will be made to the next person on the waitlist whose eligibility matches the size of the available unit according to these guidelines\.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Children\*** | **One Bedroom** | **One Bedroom \+ Den** | **Two Bedroom** | **Three Bedroom** | **Four Bedroom** |
| None | Yes | Yes | No | No | No |
| One | Yes\*\* | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Two | No | No | Yes | Yes | No |
| Three | No | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| More than three | No | No | No | No | Yes |

\*”Children” refers to anyone who has not yet turned 19 years of age who resides full\-time in the residential premises for at least ten months of any calendar year\.  
\*\* For children up to the age of 12 months\.

### Summer

[Eligible](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/ "Eligibility") residents are placed in [Fairview Crescent](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/fairview-crescent/ "Fairview Crescent") with roommates who, similarly, may be new to the unit or who are living there already\. Students will receive a residence offer first, followed by room assignments in mid\-April\. We may need to relocate current residents for operational purposes \(example: renovations\)\.

### Additional Information

#### Gender and trans experience

In addition to application date, age and vacancy type, we make room assignments based on the gender identity and trans experience a student identifies in their residence application\.

**Single\-gender units**

Many of our shared suite\-style units are single gender—students are placed in a unit with other students who indicated the same gender identity\.

For example, if you are assigned to a woman\-identifying unit, you may be placed with roommates who identify as cisgender women, transgender women or non\-binary \(or a combination if you have multiple roommates\)\.

**All\-gender units**

We also have a small number of all\-gender units\. Students who indicate a preference for an all\-gender unit may be assigned to this type of unit with students of any gender\.

For example, if you are assigned to an all\-gender unit, you may be placed with roommates who identify as non\-binary or another gender diverse identity, transgender or cisgender\.

While we do our best to accommodate all requests for an all\-gender unit, especially for trans, non\-binary and other gender diverse students, placement depends on availability, and we cannot guarantee placement for every student who selects an all\-gender unit as a preference on their application\.

Learn more about how we assign rooms for [gender diverse students](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/prospective/gender-diverse/)\.

#### **Questions?**

If you have any questions or concerns regarding the assignment process, please [contact us](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.

## Living in Fraser Hall

Located near University Village, Thunderbird Arena and the South Campus neighbourhood, Fraser Hall is known for its relaxed and friendly atmosphere—a welcoming community for upper\-year undergraduate and graduate students\.

## Quick Facts

-   Year Round
-   Mainly upper\-year undergraduate and graduate students
-   Furnished six bedroom suites, two shared bathrooms
-   [High\-speed wireless internet](https://it.ubc.ca/services/email-voice-internet/resnet)
-   Only single\-gender roommate assignments
-   132 beds: 22 six\-bedrooms
-   [Eligibility requirements](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/ "Eligibility")
-   [Fees](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/fees-payments/fraser-hall/)
-   [Residence sustainability features](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/)

**Front Desk**  

2707 Tennis Crescent  
Vancouver, B\.C\. V6T 2C1  
Tel: 604 822 3172

[information@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:information@housing.ubc.ca)

# Rooms at Fraser Hall

-   [icon\-six\-bedroom\-suite](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon-six-bedroom-suite.png)  
    
    # Six Bedroom
    
    Six single private bedrooms with two communal bathrooms, kitchen, living area and balcony\. All areas fully furnished\.
    
    [Six Bedroom Suite](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/rooms/six-bedroom/ "Six Bedroom Suite")[btn\-arrow\-teal](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/btn-arrow-teal.png)
    

# Fraser Hall Photo Gallery

-   [https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2014/03/Res\_detail\_FH\_exterior4\_NA\_720x4801\.jpg](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/Res_detail_FH_exterior4_NA_720x4801.jpg)[Exterior view and entry to Fraser Hall, UBC\.](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/Res_detail_FH_exterior4_NA_720x4801-180x120_c.jpg)

    Bedroom at Fraser Hall\.
    

# Facilities at Fraser Hall

-   [icon\_facilities\_frontdesk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_commonsblock.png)  
    
    ## Commonsblock
    
    The hub for many residence activities\. Includes: Wi\-Fi and lounging areas\. Fitness facilities available at Acadia Park\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_frontdesk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_frontdesk.png)  
    
    ## Support Staff
    
    From our Front Desk staff and Overnight Mobile Team to Residence Life professional and student staff, you are never alone\! [Meet the people](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/meet-the-team/) you can contact with questions, concerns or a request for support\.
    
-   [sorting station](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/icons_sorting_orange.png)  
    
    ## Sort It Out\!
    
    Sustainability is a shared value in residence\. Fraser Hall has a large sorting area with collection bins for household recyclables, e\-waste, charitable donations, and trash\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_laundry](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_laundry.png)  
    
    ## Laundry Facilities
    
    Machines operate on a convenient card system—no need to worry about coins\. Facilities are located on the main floor\.
    

-   [icon\_facilities\_parking](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_parking.png)  
    
    ## Parking & Bicycle Storage
    
    Limited monthly [parking](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/parking/) is available for a fee\. Indoor and outdoor bicycle storage is available\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_outdoor](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_outdoor.png)  
    
    ## Outdoor Facilities
    
    Basketball, tennis courts, playing fields and beaches are easily accessible\. Nearby Pacific Spirit Regional Park has over 35 kilometres of multipurpose trails to explore\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_health](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_health.png)  
    
    ## Health & Safety
    
    Residents have access to a campus medical clinic and safety programs such as SafeWalk\. There are regular nightly patrols of residence properties\.
    

## Sustainability Features

UBC has been recognized internationally for its commitment to sustainable living\. Many residences and rooms have modern [sustainability features](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/ "Sustainability Features") designed to reduce waste, energy consumption, and water use\.

title: Cancellations
content_markdown:
Refer to the details below for information about residence cancellation fees and possible fee exemptions\.   

Please see the [refunds](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/refunds/) page for more information about refund options and processing times\. All cancellations must be completed through the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/)\.

[Submit a cancellation](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/)

## On this page

-   [Cancelling before your move\-in date](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/cancellations-refunds/#cancelling-before-move-in)
-   [Cancelling after your move\-in date](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/cancellations-refunds/#cancelling-after-move-in)
-   [Supporting documents for all contract types](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/cancellations-refunds/#supporting-documents)
-   [FAQs](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/cancellations-refunds/#faqs)

## Cancelling before your move\-in date

### **Winter Session Contract**

#### **Fairview Crescent,** **Orchard Commons,** **Place Vanier,** **Ponderosa Commons \(Cedar House\),** **Ritsumeikan\-UBC House, Totem Park and Walter Gage\.**

Term 1 cancellation details

-   $50 residence application fee is non\-refundable\.
-   $300 Residence Allocation Process Deposit \(if applicable\) will be refunded if a cancellation request is received no later than May 1\.
-   May be subject to additional $400 cancellation fee from July 1 to July 31\.
-   From August 1 until scheduled move\-in date, cancellations will be subject to a cancellation fee of either: $950 if you have not paid a Residence Allocation Process deposit; or $700 if you have paid a Residence Allocation Process deposit\.
-   You may qualify for a fee exemption if you can demonstrate:
    1.  You are not admitted to UBC; or
    2.  You have a substantiated medical condition preventing University attendance; or
    3.  The University has cancelled your courses\.

To request an exemption from the cancellation fees, acceptable evidence and notice of cancellation must be received online by the day before the move\-in date noted on the Residence Acceptance Confirmation\.

Acceptable evidence must also be submitted by email to [information@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:information@housing.ubc.ca)\. Your request for exemption will then be reviewed and the decision provided to you by email\.

Term 2 cancellation details

-   $50 residence application fee is non\-refundable\.
-   $300 Residence Allocation Process deposit \(if applicable\) will be refunded if a cancellation request is received no later than May 1\.
-   Additional $400 fee for cancellations between November 15 and December 15\.
-   From Dec\. 16 until scheduled move\-in date, residence cancellations will be subject to a cancellation fee of either: $950 if you have not paid a Residence Allocation Process deposit; or $700 if you have paid a Residence Allocation Process deposit\.
-   You may qualify for a fee exemption if you can demonstrate:
    1.  You are not admitted to UBC; or
    2.  You have a substantiated medical condition preventing University attendance; or
    3.  The University has cancelled your courses\.

To request an exemption from the cancellation fees, acceptable evidence and notice of cancellation must be received online by the day before the move\-in date noted on the Residence Acceptance Confirmation\.

Acceptable evidence must also be submitted by email to [information@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:information@housing.ubc.ca)\. Your request for exemption will then be reviewed and the decision provided to you by email\.  

### **Year Round Contract**

#### **Brock Commons, Exchange, Fraser Hall, Iona House, Marine Drive, Ponderosa Commons \(Arbutus, Maple, Oak and Spruce Houses\),** **tə šxʷhəleləm̓s tə k̓ʷaƛ̓kʷəʔaʔɬ** **and Thunderbird**

Cancellation details

-   $50 application fee is non\-refundable\.
-   You may be required to pay a cancellation fee equal to the acceptance deposit amount\. For additional details, please refer to Section 1\.11 and Appendix III in the [Year Round Residence Contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/)\.
-   You may qualify for a fee exemption if you can demonstrate:
    1.  You are not admitted to UBC; or
    2.  You have a substantiated medical condition preventing University attendance; or
    3.  The University has cancelled your courses\.

To request an exemption from the cancellation fees, acceptable evidence and notice of cancellation must be received online by the day before the move\-in date noted on the Residence Acceptance Confirmation\.

Acceptable evidence must also be submitted by email to [information@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:information@housing.ubc.ca)\. Your request for exemption will then be reviewed and the decision provided to you by email\.  

### **Acadia Park Residential Agreement**

Cancellation details

-   $50 application fee is non\-refundable\.
-   If you cancel prior to the move in date noted on your Residence Acceptance Confirmation, you will forfeit your security deposit\.
-   You may qualify for an exemption if you can demonstrate:
    1.  You are not admitted to UBC; or
    2.  You have a substantiated medical condition preventing University attendance; or
    3.  The University has cancelled your courses\.

Acadia Park residents can submit a cancellation request and apply for a fee exemption by logging into their [Student Housing Account](https://starrezportal.vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/StarRezPortalX/7F99AA1E/1/1/Home-Home?UrlToken=8281C523)\.

Acceptable documentation may be required before the move in date noted on your Residence Acceptance Confirmation\.

### **Green College and St\. John’s College**

Cancellation details

-   $50 application fee is non\-refundable\.
-   May be subject to a cancellation fee equal to the acceptance deposit amount\.
-   You may qualify for a fee exemption if you can demonstrate:
    1.  You are not admitted to UBC; or
    2.  You have a substantiated medical condition preventing University attendance; or
    3.  The University has cancelled your courses\.

To request an exemption from the cancellation fees, acceptable evidence and notice of cancellation must be received online by the day before the move\-in date noted on the Residence Acceptance Confirmation\.

Acceptable evidence must also be submitted by email to [information@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:information@housing.ubc.ca)\. Your request for exemption will then be reviewed and the decision provided to you by email\.  

### **Summer Residence and Summer Stay\-through Contract**

Cancellation details

-   $50 application fee is non\-refundable\.
-   $150 cancellation fee applies unless written notice is received 22 days prior to the move\-in date shown on your Residence Acceptance Confirmation\.
-   Refunds are processed using the initial method of payment\.
-   After moving in, 30 days notice is required to cancel\.

### **Early Arrival**

Contact [Student Housing and Community Services](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/ "Contact Us")\. Students who need to arrive early should consider booking [short\-term accommodation\.](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/other-housing/visitor-campus-housing/ "Visitor Housing")

Cancellation details

-   Reservations will be charged unless cancelled by July 31, regardless of whether or not the room is occupied\.
-   Payments will be refunded only if proof of non\-acceptance to UBC is provided\.

## Cancelling after your move\-in date

### Winter Session Contract

#### Totem Park, Place Vanier, Orchard Commons, Ritsumeikan House, Ponderosa Commons \(Cedar House\), Walter Gage, Fairview Crescent

Cancellation details

You will be subject to a termination fee\. The termination fee is equal to 25% of your total residence fees or the remainder of your residence fees from the time you check out, whichever is less\. For additional details, please refer to Section 1\.14 in the [Winter Session Residence Contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/)\.

### **Year Round Contract**

#### **Brock Commons, Exchange, Fraser Hall, Iona House, Marine Drive, Ponderosa Commons \(Arbutus, Maple, Oak and Spruce Houses\), Thunderbird\.**

Cancellation details

You will be subject to a termination fee\. The termination fee is equal to 25% of your total residence fees or the remainder of your residence fees from the time you check out, whichever is less\.

For additional details, please refer to Section 1\.12 in the [Year Round Residence Contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/)\.

## Supporting documents for all contract types

If supporting documents are required as part of your cancellation, here is what you need:

-   **Program Completion**—provide a letter from your faculty’s advising office confirming the date you are expected to complete your degree requirements\.
-   **Work term placement**—provide a letter from your co\-op office confirming the dates of your work term\.
-   **Go Global Student Exchange Program**—provide a letter from the Go Global office confirming the dates of your exchange program\.
-   **Teaching practicum**—provide a letter from the Teacher Education Office confirming your practicum dates\.
-   **Graduate Students**—provide a copy of your program completion and closure date memo from the Faculty of Graduate Studies\.

## FAQs

### I’m completing my program in April, but I need housing until graduation\. Can I stay in residence?

If you live in Year Round Residence and will complete your program in April, but need housing until graduation \(i\.e\., your convocation ceremony\), you may be eligible to remain in your room/unit\.

#### Action required

-   **February:** accept your contract renewal offer for the next academic year, when you receive it via email\.
-   **By no later than April 1:** submit a cancellation request via the SHCS [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/), indicating that you are staying for convocation\. In spring, we’ll send you your approved departure date, which varies from year to year and depends on the date of the final convocation ceremony\.

Please note that if you submit your cancellation request after the April 1 deadline, you may be subject to cancellation fees, as outlined in your [housing contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/)\.

### I’m completing my program in April, but I need housing for the summer\. Can I stay in residence?

You may be eligible to live in residence—but in Summer Residence, rather than your current Year Round residence assignment\. Learn more about what action you need to take\.

#### Action required

1.  **February:** do not accept your contract renewal offer for the next academic year, when you receive it via email\.
2.  **Late\-February/early\-March:** apply for Summer Residence in the SHCS [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/)\.

Please note that your Summer Residence room/unit assignments will likely be different from your current assignment\. Most Summer Residence students are assigned to Fairview Crescent\.

### I’m completing my program partway through the summer, but I need housing for the entire summer\. Can I stay in residence?

You may be eligible to live in residence, in your currently\-assigned room/unit, up until the end of August, but your specific departure date might vary, depending on the current year’s calendar\. Please refer to your [residence contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/) for the latest departure date in August\.

#### Action required

1.  **February:** accept your contract renewal offer for the next academic year, when you receive it via email\.
2.  **By no later than June 30:** submit a cancellation request via the SHCS [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/), indicating a departure date at the “end of August”\. Specific departure dates may vary depending on the year\. Please contact us to verify the latest accepted departure date—or find it in your residence contract under “Termination of the Residence Contract On or After Move\-In Date”\.

### I am withdrawing / being withdrawn from my academic program\. When do I need to cancel my residence contract and move out?

#### Voluntary withdrawal

If you are planning to voluntarily withdraw from your academic program, you will no longer be eligible to remain in Student Housing\.

**Action required**

-   Submit a cancellation request via the SHCS [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/)—at least two months in advance of your intended withdrawal date\.\*
-   Indicate a departure date no later than the end of the month you are withdrawing \(i\.e\., if you’re withdrawing on January 15, indicate a withdrawal date of no later than January 31\)\.

\*If you are not able to provide two month’s notice, please [let us know](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.

Please note that your cancellation may be subject to cancellation fees as outlined in your [housing contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/)\.

#### Required withdrawal

If you live in Year Round Residence and you are required to withdraw from your academic program at the end of the Winter Session \(i\.e\., at the end of April\), and you will no longer be a student in September, you can continue living in residence until the end of August, if needed\.

Please refer to your [residence contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/) for the latest departure date in August\.

**Action required**

-   **February:** accept your contract renewal offer for the next academic year, when you receive it via email\.
-   **By no later than June 30:** submit a cancellation request via the SHCS Online Service Centre, indicating a departure date at the “end of August”\. Please contact us to verify the latest accepted departure date—or find it in your residence contract under “Termination of the Residence Contract On or After Move\-In Date”\.

Please note that your cancellation may be subject to cancellation fees as outlined in your [housing contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/)\.

***Appealing a required withdrawal?***

If you are planning to appeal the decision you received from your faculty, here are the steps we recommend you take:

1.  Submit your cancellation request as outlined above\. In the comments, let us know that you’ve been required by your program to withdraw and that you are submitting an appeal\.
2.  After submitting your appeal, [email us](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/) a copy of the appeal confirmation and the anticipated decision timeline\.
3.  Notify us as soon as you receive the decision about your appeal\.

*Successful appeals*

If your appeal is successful and you register full\-time for September, we will cancel your cancellation request, and you may remain in residence\.

*Unsuccessful appeals*

If your appeal is unsuccessful, you must move out by the end of Term 2 of the Summer Session\. Please contact us to verify your end date—or find it in your [residence contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/) under “Termination of the Residence Contract On or After Move\-In Date”\.

## Additional information

For more detailed information about cancellations and refunds, please refer to your [Residence Contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/)\.

## Living in Ritsumeikan\-UBC House

Ritsumeikan\-UBC House was established as a symbol of UBC's academic partnership with Ritsumeikan University in Japan\. Relaxing green space around the property is ideal for studying, hanging out with friends or enjoying quiet time\. The nearby Commonsblock is shared with Orchard Commons, one of our first year residences\.

## Quick Facts

-   Winter session \(September to April\)
-   Mainly first\-year undergraduate students
-   [Optional meal plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/ubccard-value-plan/ "Suite-style Residences") available
-   205 beds: 50 four and five\-person units, 5 one\-bedroom units
-   Single gender roommate assignments
-   Furnished kitchens, living areas, and private and shared bedrooms
-   [Internet access \(ethernet port\) in each room](https://it.ubc.ca/services/email-voice-internet/resnet)
-   [Eligibility requirements](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/ "Eligibility")
-   [Fees](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/fees-payments/ritsumeiken-ubc/)
-   [Residence sustainability features](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/)

**Ritsumeikan\-UBC House/Orchard Commons Front Desk**  

6363 Agronomy Road  
Vancouver, B\.C\. V6T 1Z4  
Tel: 604 827 2778

[information@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:information@housing.ubc.ca)

-   [Map\_Ritsumeikan\_3](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/Map_Ritsumeikan_3.png)

# Rooms at Ritsumeikan\-UBC House

-   [icon\-four\-bedroom\-suite](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon-four-bedroom-suite.png)  
    
    # Four Bedroom
    
    Four single private bedrooms with two communal bathrooms, kitchen, living area and eating area\. All areas fully furnished\.
    
    [Four Bedroom Suite](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/rooms/four-bedroom-suite/ "Four Bedroom Suite")[btn\-arrow\-teal](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/btn-arrow-teal.png)
    

# Ritsumeikan\-UBC House Photo Gallery

-   [https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2014/03/Res\_detail\_Rits\_exterior3\_720x480\.jpg](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/Res_detail_Rits_exterior3_720x480.jpg)[Exterior view of Ritsumeikan\-UBC House, UBC\.](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/Res_detail_Rits_exterior3_720x480-180x120_c.jpg)
    
    Exterior view of Ritsumeikan\-UBC House\.

    Rits\-UBC entryway\.
    
-   [https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2014/03/Res\_detail\_Rits\_pingpong\_720x480\.jpg](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/Res_detail_Rits_pingpong_720x480.jpg)[Residents play ping\-pong in the Rits\-UBC common space\.](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/plugins/soliloquy/assets/css/images/holder.gif)
    
    Common area for games\.
    
-   [https://vancouver\.housing\.ubc\.ca/wp\-content/uploads/2014/03/Res\_detail\_RU\_exterior4\_NA\_720x480\.jpg](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/Res_detail_RU_exterior4_NA_720x480.jpg)[Exterior view of Rits\-UBC\.](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/plugins/soliloquy/assets/css/images/holder.gif)
    
    Exterior view\.
    

# Facilities at Ritsumeikan\-UBC House

-   [icon\_facilities\_frontdesk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_commonsblock.png)  
    
    ## Commonsblock
    
    Ritsumeikan\-UBC residents share a Commonsblock with Orchard Commons\. Includes: Wi\-Fi, dining room, fitness room, music rooms, group and private study spaces, ballroom, games lounge, and after\-hours convenience store\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_frontdesk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_frontdesk.png)  
    
    ## Support Staff
    
    From our Front Desk staff and Overnight Mobile Team to Residence Life professional and student staff, you are never alone\! [Meet the people](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/meet-the-team/) you can contact with questions, concerns or a request for support\.
    
-   [sorting station](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/icons_sorting_orange.png)  
    
    ## Sort It Out\!
    
    Sustainability is a shared value in residence\. Rits\-UBC has a large sorting area with collection bins for household recyclables, e\-waste, charitable donations, and trash\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_laundry](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_laundry.png)  
    
    ## Laundry Facilities
    
    Machines operate on a convenient card system—no need to worry about coins\. Facilities are located within each residence block\.
    

-   [icon\_facilities\_parking](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_parking.png)  
    
    ## Parking & Bicycle Storage
    
    Limited monthly [parking](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/parking/) is available for a fee\. Outdoor bicycle storage is available\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_outdoor](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_outdoor.png)  
    
    ## Outdoor Facilities
    
    Basketball, tennis courts, playing fields and beaches are easily accessible\. Nearby Pacific Spirit Regional Park has over 35 kilometres of multipurpose trails to explore\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_health](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_health.png)  
    
    ## Health and Safety
    
    Residents have access to a campus medical clinic and safety programs such as SafeWalk\. There are regular nightly patrols of residence properties\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_family](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_mealplan.png)  
    
    ## Meal Plan
    
    Ritsumeikan\-UBC suites come with kitchens\. Students can purchase an [optional meal plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/ubccard-value-plan/ "Food Services Meal Plans") for convenience—no need to cook or carry cash\.
    

## Sustainability Features

UBC has been recognized internationally for its commitment to sustainable living\. Many residences and rooms have modern [sustainability features](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/ "Sustainability Features") designed to reduce waste, energy consumption, and water use\.

# Ritsumeikan\-UBC House Residence Life

“You live here only a few years but will carry the memories forever\.” – UBC resident

-   [Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/res_detail_rezlife_ru1_720x480.jpg)
-   [Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/res_detail_rezlife_ru2_720x480.jpg)
-   [Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/res_detail_rezlife_ru3_720x480.jpg)
-   [Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/res_detail_rezlife_ru4_720x480.jpg)

Ritsumeikan\-UBC House’s [Residence Life](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/ "Get Involved") team consists of one professional staff member and three student staff who work hard to promote a safe, inclusive and enjoyable community for residents\.

Brock Commons is one of our newest residence areas\. Home to over 1,000 students, residents enjoy its central location, spectacular views and unique building features\. The AMS Nest, bus loop, and many campus classrooms and recreational facilities are nearby\. It is also where you'll find Tallwood House, one of the tallest mass timber hybrid buildings in the world\.

# Facilities at Brock Commons

-   [icon\_facilities\_frontdesk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_commonsblock.png)  
    
    ## Commonsblock
    
    The hub for residence activities\. Includes: Wi\-Fi, fitness room, activity and meeting rooms, group and private study spaces, lounge areas and a convenience store\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_frontdesk](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_frontdesk.png)  
    
    ## Support Staff
    
    From our Front Desk staff and Overnight Mobile Team to Residence Life professional and student staff, you are never alone\! [Meet the people](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/meet-the-team/) you can contact with questions, concerns or a request for support\.
    
-   [sorting station](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/icons_sorting_orange.png)  
    
    ## Sort It Out\!
    
    We strive to be a “Zero Waste” campus\. Brock Commons has a large sorting area with collection bins for compost, household trash, recyclables, e\-waste, and charitable donations\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_laundry](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_laundry.png)  
    
    ## Laundry Facilities
    
    Machines operate on a convenient card system—no need to worry about coins\. Facilities are located on the main floor\.
    

-   [icon\_facilities\_parking](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_parking.png)  
    
    ## Parking & Bicycle Storage
    
    Limited monthly [parking](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/parking/) is available for a fee\. Bicycle storage hooks are available in each suite\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_outdoor](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_outdoor.png)  
    
    ## Outdoor Facilities
    
    Basketball, tennis courts, playing fields and beaches are easily accessible\. Nearby Pacific Spirit Regional Park has over 35 kilometres of multipurpose trails to explore\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_health](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_health.png)  
    
    ## Health & Safety
    
    Residents have access to a campus medical clinic and safety programs such as SafeWalk\. There are regular nightly patrols of residence properties\.
    
-   [icon\_facilities\_family](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/icon_facilities_mealplan.png)  
    
    ## Meal Plan
    
    Brock Commons suites come with kitchens\. Students can purchase an [optional meal plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/ubccard-value-plan/ "Food Services Meal Plans") for convenience—no need to cook or carry cash\.
    

## Sustainability Features

UBC has been recognized internationally for its commitment to sustainable living\. Many residences and rooms have modern [sustainability features](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/sustainability-features/ "Sustainability Features") designed to reduce waste, energy consumption, and water use\.

# Brock Commons Residence Life

“Living in Brock Commons has been a great experience\. Everything about the building is amazing\. The community has made it feel like home\.” – Louisa Pumilia, Tallwood House resident

-   [Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/Res_life_PV_bouncing_720x480.jpg)
-   [Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/Res_life_PV_Holi1_720x480.jpg)
-   [Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/Res_life_PV_Tec_720x480.jpg)
-   [Image](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/Res_life_PV_ultimate2_720x480.jpg)

The Brock Commons [Residence Life](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/) team consists of one Residence Life Manager and six Residence Advisors, plus numerous Front Desk staff who work hard to promote a safe, inclusive and enjoyable community for residents\.

title: FAQs
content_markdown:
## On this page

-   [Prospective residents](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/faq/#prospective)
-   [Current residents](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/faq/#current)
-   [Returning and graduate residents](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/faq/#returning)

### Prospective undergraduate residents

When can I apply to live in residence?

New students usually apply to live in residence at the end of the UBC Admissions process in February\. Student Housing also accepts applications directly through the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/) or print an [application form](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-to-apply/application-forms/ "Application Forms")\. See [Important Dates](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/important-dates/ "Dates & Deadlines") to confirm the deadline to apply\.  

Who is eligible to live in residence?

See [eligibility](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/ "Eligibility")\.  

How are residence offers sent?

All residence offers are sent by email\.  

What if I don’t respond to the offer by the deadline?

Please contact Student Housing immediately\.  

What if I’m unable to pay a deposit?

Please contact Student Housing immediately\.  

What if I don’t want to live in the area I’m offered?

If you want to live in residence, we recommend you accept the offer\. If the offer is declined, you will not receive another one\. If you are unhappy with your room, you may [apply for a room transfer](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/switch/ "Switches & Transfers") in mid\-September\. Transfers are considered on a case\-by\-case basis and not guaranteed\.  

How much does it cost to live in residence?

[Fees vary](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences-rooms/residences/ "At a Glance") by residence and room type\.  

How can I pay fees?

There are a few ways\. See [Fees & Payments](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/fees-payments/ "Fees & Payments") to find an option that works best for you\.  

How can I check my account balance?

Use the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/)\. When a payment is received, a credit will appear on your account\.  

Can someone else call the main office on my behalf to ask about my application or fees?

We will only release this information if you provided consent to release it on your application form\. See [how we value privacy](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/privacy/ "Privacy")\.  

Do I have to buy a meal plan?

Students who live at Place Vanier, Totem Park and Orchard Commons must purchase the [Residence Meal Plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/residence-meal-plan-all-access-dining/ "Totem & Vanier")\. Students assigned to other residences can purchase an optional [UBCcard Value Plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/ubccard-value-plan/)\.  

Can I bring my car?

UBC is a very walkable campus—flat and pedestrian\-friendly, with everything inside a 15\-minute walk or so, and much of campus a car\-free zone\. So you don’t need to bring a bike or vehicle to get around\.

Learn more about [alternative transportation options](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/what-should-i-pack/#bikes-vehicles) for on and off\-campus\.

If you do end up bringing a vehicle, find out [how to apply for parking and what it costs](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/services-amenities/parking/)\.

Can first year students request a roommate?

Yes\. [Roommate group requests](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/living-with-roomates/ "Living With Roommates") are part of the application process\.  

Can I contact my roommate\(s\) before moving in?

Yes, if they have provided their consent\. Use the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/) to consent to release your information to each other\. Roommates usually contact each other in mid\-August\.  

When can I move into residence?

Learn more about [moving in](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/) and [Move In Day](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/move-in-day/)\.  

Can I move in early?

Early arrivals are typically not permitted\. Check [eligibility](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/ "Housing Eligibility")\.  

### Current residents

What if someone calls the main office to get in touch with me?

To [comply with privacy law](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/privacy/ "Privacy"), we don’t release information about any residents unless consent is provided\.  

Who do I contact about lost or stolen keys?

Visit your Residence Front Desk immediately to file a report\.  

What if residence property needs maintenance?

Use the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/) to send a maintenance request\. Do not attempt to fix residence property on your own\.  

Does UBC cover damages to my personal property?

No\. UBC’s insurance coverage is for the physical structure of buildings \(walls, roof, flooring\) and components \(fridges, stoves\) only\. The university is not responsible for lost, stolen or damaged personal property, regardless of the cause\. We strongly recommend that you get [renter’s insurance](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/renters-insurance/)\.  

Can I switch rooms with someone?

There are procedures to [switch rooms with someone or apply for a transfer](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/moving-in/switch/ "Switches & Transfers")\.  

What if there is a conflict within residence?

All residents must adhere to [Residence Standards](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/residence-standards/ "Residence Standards")\. Conflicts or breaches of Residence Standards are investigated by Residence Life staff\.  

What happens during the winter break?

Place Vanier, Totem Park and Orchard Commons residents are not permitted to stay in their rooms during the [winter break residence closure](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/winter-break-residence-closure/ "Key Dates & Deadlines")\. Students in other residences are permitted to stay; however, campus services are limited throughout the break\.  

When is the deadline to move out of residence?

Check our [Important Dates](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/important-dates/) page for this year’s move out date\. But if you’re moving directly into another residence operated by UBC Student Housing, watch for an email with information about when to move—or [contact us](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.  

Where can I dispose of garbage and unwanted items when I move out?

Check out our [Moving Out](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/moving-out/) page to learn more about how to move out of residence and what to do with the stuff you’re not taking with you\.  

Are there fees when I move out?

Students may receive assessments if there is any damage to residence property or required cleaning was not completed to our satisfaction\.  

What is the policy for cancelling a Residence Contract?

-   **Before moving in:** See [Cancellations](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/cancellations-refunds/ "Cancellations & Refunds") and [Refunds](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/refunds/)\.
-   **After moving in:** Visit your [Residence Contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/ "Residence Contracts")\.

Cancellation must be initiated using the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/)\.

### Returning and graduate residents

What type of housing should I apply for?

Year Round residence is the place for upper year and graduate students\. Learn more at [Returning Students](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/returning/) and [Graduate Students](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/graduate-students/)\.  

Can I apply for Winter Session residence too?

You are welcome to apply for upper year Winter Session housing; however, there is a very limited number of spaces available\.  

How do I increase my chances of getting into residence?

Apply to live in Year Round residence as early as possible\.  

What about roommate requests?

After receiving a residence offer, go online to update your application preferences and submit a roommate grouping request\.  

What if I change my mind about living in residence?

-   **Before moving in:** See [Cancellations](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/cancellations-refunds/ "Cancellations & Refunds") and [Refunds](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/refunds/)\.
-   **After moving in:** Visit your [Residence Contract](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/ "Residence Contracts")\.

Cancellation must be initiated using the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/)\.

Are sublets allowed?

[Subletting](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/subletting/) is permitted in eligible residences during the Summer Session\.

title: Prospective Students
content_markdown:
Welcome prospective undergrads—domestic and international\!

For many new students, living in residence is where the university journey begins\. And at UBC, it’s an extraordinary experience unlike any other\.

Living in residence makes it easy for students to meet new people, live in a study\-oriented atmosphere, get help for academic and personal challenges, and be part of all that UBC and its surrounding neighbourhoods have to offer\. Campus residents have easy access to beaches and recreational activities, theatre, restaurants, guest speakers and special interest clubs\.

Year after year, students tell us that living in residence helped them become better learners and make long\-lasting friendships\. UBC houses nearly 14,000 students in [15 residences](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences-rooms/residences/ "At a Glance")\.

Applying to live in a first year residence area, Marine Drive or Ponderosa Commons?

Be aware that the Lower Mall Precinct project, a new 1,500\-bed student residence, is being built near Marine Drive, Place Vanier and Ponderosa Commons\. There will be construction activity and noise in the area\. [Learn more](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences-rooms/projects/lower-mall-precinct/construction/)\. 

## Guaranteed rooms

Many prospective students will qualify for our [First Year Guarantee](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/first-year-guarantee/ "Who Gets Priority") in Winter Session Residence\. Most students in this group are assigned to live in [Orchard Commons](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/orchard-commons/), [Place Vanier](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/place-vanier/ "Place Vanier") or [Totem Park](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/totem-park/ "Totem Park")\. These residences all have furnished shared and single rooms, vibrant common areas for socializing, and plenty of space for quiet study time\. Based on availability, some students will be assigned to live in [Ritsumeikan\-UBC House](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/ritsumaiken-ubc-house/ "Ritsumeiken-UBC House"), [Walter Gage](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/walter-gage/ "Walter Gage"), or [Fairview Crescent](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residences/fairview-crescent/ "Fairview Crescent") where upper\-year students and some graduate students also live\.

## Eating made easy

Never worry about planning, shopping, prepping or cleaning up after meals\. Residents in Orchard Commons, Place Vanier and Totem Park purchase a required [residence meal plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/residence-meal-plan-all-access-dining/ "Totem & Vanier"), with residence dollars for use at all three residence dining halls and flex dollars for use at select campus partners\.

Students who are offered accommodation in other residences will have a kitchen, but can also enjoy added convenience and savings with a [UBCcard Value Plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/ubccard-value-plan/)\.  

> “The dining hall gives you a huge array of options and they switch it up every day, so there’s always something new to try\.” — Amy Miles, Totem Park resident

## Support and fun

No matter which residence you live in, you will be part of a safe, supportive, inclusive environment that’s designed to help you pursue your academic goals and enjoy your time as a student\. Our Residence Life teams are among the best\-connected people at the university\. Residence Advisors—current UBC students—are plugged into the resources and support services available to you in residence and around campus, including [health services](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/health-wellness/ "Health & Wellness") and [safety programs](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/health-safety/safety-security/ "Safety & Security")\. RAs spend countless hours organizing fun [opportunities to get students involved in residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/residence-life/get-involved/ "Get Involved")\. Be an actor in a residence play, join a committee, or go on a field trip to one of our local ski hills\. When you live at UBC, there’s always something to do\.  

> “You’ll meet people from all over the world with all different backgrounds\. The one thing we have in common is UBC pride\.” — Brandon MacKay

## Jump Start

All direct\-entry, first\-year undergraduate students are invited to participate in [Jump Start](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/get-ready/), which takes place in August, prior to the start of classes\. Jump Start is specifically designed to help first year students adjust to their new academic environment, make friends, and explore their new home, school and city\.  

> “Before arriving at UBC, I was anxious about moving to a new place, meeting new friends and being in a different academic setting\. I made friends and got to know UBC through Jump Start and now I feel more confident going into my classes\.” — UBC Jump Start participant

## Costs

[Fees and payments](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/fees-payments/ "Fees and Payments") vary depending on what residence and room type you live in—and whether you are a first year student with a required [Residence Meal Plan](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/residence-meal-plan-all-access-dining/)\.

Note that undergraduate students entering their first year could be eligible for a [Student Housing Supplemental Grant](http://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/awards/ubc-bursary/student-housing-supplement-grant)\. Explore information about [financial resources for UBC students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances)\.

Guide for gender diverse students

Check out our [guide for gender diverse students](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/prospective/gender-diverse/) to learn more about the process of applying, indicating gender identity and receiving room assignments for trans, non\-binary and other gender diverse students\.

## How to apply

You can start your residence application when you [apply to UBC](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/), and then visit the Student Housing and Community Services \(SHCS\) [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/) to finish your residence application\.

If you didn’t apply for housing when you applied to UBC, you can apply directly in the [Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/) before May 1\.

### Tips

-   Don’t wait to apply for residence until you’ve received an offer of admission to UBC\. Apply by the Winter Session Residence deadline \(May 1\)\.
-   Review [essential application facts](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/essential-facts/ "Essential Application Facts") and [important dates](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/important-dates/ "Important Dates") to ensure your application is submitted properly and on time\.
-   If you are considering both the Okanagan and Vancouver campuses for your studies, apply to both residences by the deadline\.

Applying to live in Thunderbird Residence?

Be aware that building repairs at Thunderbird are taking place in summer 2026, and there will be construction activity and noise in the area\. [Learn more](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/thunderbird-repairs/)\.
